- Each model names the simulator invariant of each property in its own section's property table,
  so this map holds only the configuration results. The sessions model's invariants are registered
  by [MetaStore invariants](#metastore-invariants) (phase 4), which plants its leader-side
  negatives, and [Session fencing on storage nodes](#session-fencing-on-storage-nodes) its
  storage-side ones. The sessions model's client-side negatives are planted by
  [Client sessions](#client-sessions); the purge model's invariants are registered, and its
  negatives planted, by the phase 6 items its rows in `scripts/model-rules.tsv` name; the recall
  model's by phase 7 (Tier 2), except the grace period's and the attribute timeout's, which
  [Owner failover and grace period](#owner-failover-and-grace-period) and
  [Client fencing](#client-fencing) plant.
- The sessions model's leader measures its rate over a client's exactly once two renewals reached
  it (`Measured`), so pairing an answer with the heartbeat that names it, lost and repeated
  requests, and a leader's own stop are checked only by the Go tests of
  [Control-plane sessions](#control-plane-sessions); `ci-rates` passing does not cover them.
- The sessions model has no session start, fetch or answer: each storage node is one table version
  that `ApplyTable` sets, so "a live session's write is never refused" is in no model. Fencing
  safety does not rest on the fetch, since any table applied fences. The property is checked only
  by the Go tests of [Storage node session wiring](#storage-node-session-wiring) and
  [Control-plane sessions](#control-plane-sessions). A model with starts and fetches would have
  found a new leader whose applied table lagged a start answering a fetch under its lease alone,
  which the node took as refusing that live session.
- The epoch change model's counterexamples each also appear as a planted bug that trips the mapped
  invariant: those for property 2 in [MetaStore invariants](#metastore-invariants), the rest in
  [Placement faults and invariants](#placement-faults-and-invariants). The exceptions, with no
  planted bug yet, are named by the unticked build checklist item [Plants for the epoch model's new
  rules](build-checklist.md#phase-4-embedded-metastore).
- Snapshot cuts and pool moves are modelled in phase 11, and cross-shard commit in phase 13, each
  before its code (design.md Roadmap), so this map has no rows for them yet.

## Model gate

`scripts/model-gate.sh`, run by `scripts/lint.sh`, over the commits since `MODEL_GATE_BASE` (the
merge base with `origin/main` by default; the commits of a push or pull request in CI).
`scripts/model-gate-test.sh` plants each row below in a throwaway clone, and CI's lint job runs it.

| Case | Result |
| --- | --- |
| A commit changes a protocol file, no spec or configuration under `models/`, and has no `Model: none, <reason>` line in its body | Fails, naming the commit and the file |
| The same with a reason, or with a change to a spec or configuration | Passes |
| The same line with no reason, or in the subject, or a stray file under `models/` | Fails |
| A merge whose resolution changes a protocol file, the same way | Fails |
| A clean merge | Passes |
| A commit changes only tests, docs or an excluded file | Passes |
| A negative configuration has no row in `scripts/model-rules.tsv`, or a row has none | Fails |
| A row has the wrong shape, as one with no plant or no test | Fails |
| A row's plant is in no file of its package, its test does not exist, or its test's file does not name the plant | Fails |
| A row is open on a checklist item that is ticked, or on a phase the checklist now lists | Fails |
| No base commit can be found | Warns, and fails in CI |

- Every `.go` file of a protocol package is a protocol file unless the script excludes it, so a new
  file starts covered. Test files are excluded, and files that hold no model's rule.
- A push to `main` checks the commits it adds, and a push to any other branch every commit since the
  merge base, so a commit on top of a failed one does not hide it. A force push to `main` has no old
  commit to start from and checks nothing, which branch protection covers.
- That a test fails under its plant is that test's own assertion, as in [Placement faults and
  invariants](#placement-faults-and-invariants). The gate checks only that the link stands, so a
  test that shares a file with a plant it does not use passes it.
- `scripts/model-gate.sh for FILE` lists each rule whose plant FILE holds, with the property it
  breaks, the lines that hold it and the rule in words. It says so when there is none, since that
  does not mean no rule applies, and fails on a file that does not exist.

## Spec conformance

Whether the code follows a spec, the question [From spec to code](design.md#testing-strategy) sets.
Finding a new bug is no part of what passes or fails here: a run with none is the result wanted.
Not to be confused with the POSIX conformance suites of [Testing strategy](design.md#testing-strategy).

| Part | Holds when | Fails when |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Traces pass | Every seeded trace checked is a behavior of the spec | A record has no spec action, or a step the spec does not allow |
| Traces can fail | Each rule the [rule map](#model-gate) gives a plant is caught with the spec left as it was: the seed's unplanted baseline passes, and the line TLC rejects with the plant set is the planted behaviour, even if an invariant also broke. A catch with every invariant intact is clean, and clean catches are reported beside the total | A planted rule removal passes every trace |
| Traces cover the spec | Every action of the spec appears in some trace, and each one that cannot, as on a fault no run lands, is listed with why | An action no trace reaches is not listed |

- A spec action with no mapping to a record kind fails, and so does a record kind with no spec
  action. No line is filtered out to make a trace pass.
- A compressed spec action, one that stands for several code steps, names those steps in its
  mapping.
- The trace spec holds no protocol logic of its own: the spec it wraps stays the only statement of
  the protocol. The tools in `tools/` decide no protocol step, and each holds the mapping's judgement
  in named places. In `tools/tracedata`, `classify` names the spec's changes for a table, and
  `landOpen` and `crash` name the versions a node may have made durable with no record. In
  `tools/votersdata`, `state` names the change of a replica's Raft state each line stands for,
  `replicate` places an append at its send, and `support` writes the lapses a fortification's
  lines need.
- The verdict is the same on every run of a trace, spec and mapping, on TLC's one worker.
- Each discrepancy is recorded as code, spec, compression or logging, and settled as
  [From spec to code](design.md#testing-strategy) says.
- The spec stays passing: a spec patched for a discrepancy passes `scripts/models.sh ci` on its model
  before it merges.
- The check states the seeds it ran and the time per trace, and which spec actions and rules each
  run covered, so a claim of conformance says what it rests on.

### The epoch model's check

`scripts/conform.sh` runs `TestConform*`, or the test `RUN` names, with `CONFORM_DIR` set, so each
run keeps its trace, and `tools/tracedata` writes each trace into a data module: the run's constants,
its membership plan and one line per protocol step. `models/epoch/trace_epoch.tla`, with `epoch.tla`
unchanged by it, has TLC 1.7.4 on one worker take each line by the action it names, compare what the
record saw with the state that action leaves, and pass by reaching the end with the safety invariants
intact; `KEEP=dir` keeps the traces and data. Each trace is its own TLC process with its own directory, heap
and temporary directory, and `JOBS=n` runs that many at once, with no effect on a verdict: the lines print in
order once all are done. On the M4 Pro use at most 6, so 12 GB of heap, or 4 beside anything busy, and nothing
heavy beside it. A failure names the line no state could take, or the
invariant a line broke; a run out of time or heap prints `no verdict`, which is neither. Each trace
starts at the first `Table` record, which is the spec's `Init`, so interval 1's bootstrap peering is
out of scope. A trace with no line but tables gives no data, so it cannot pass.

`NoLateCompletion`, `DropsAreSuffix`, `VersionsGrow` and `UnchangedIntervalAccepts` hold on every
state. `NothingCommittedDropped`, `OneWritePerVersion`, `MergesOnKept` and `TablesForward` read sets
that only grow, so a break stays, and each is checked once, at the last line, since on every state a
long trace runs at 14 states a second: a trace a line stopped evaluates none of them, and only the
first branch to reach the end is evaluated. `OneReader`, `ReadsAcked` and `ReadsMapped` are left out,
since no line moves a lease, and so is `NoResurrectedWrite`, since no traced write is a reissue.

| Records | Spec action | Compression |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Table`, `PGEntry`, `Member` | `Membership` or `Reactive` | `tracedata` splits a table's fold from its membership change. The harness's own last ask is an `Edit` that changes nothing. A reorder of a PG, with at most one mark, in one table is one `Edit`, one interval, as the code's `Next` makes it; `ci-edits` checks that action. Any other table of several of a PG's changes is one `Refill`. A `table` line then compares each changed entry with the spec's: interval, last activated, members, marks, leaving member, `min_live` and past intervals, so a member changed at an unchanged interval fails. `PastInterval` records carry the past intervals |
| `Adopt` | `Adopt` | A repeat of the table the spec's node holds, as after a restart, which empties the code's table and leaves `ep`, is a stutter. An epoch no `Table` named stops `tracedata` |
| `Send` | `Send` | A send the spec has disabled is a stutter, so ordering it later fails |
| `Order` | `Order` | Logs on the primary and sends to members in one step; the primary's record is durable at its `Logged` |
| `Accepted`, `Logged` | `Deliver` | A store's in-flight version may land before an `Adopt` or crash (`maydeliver`), and `Logged` is then a stutter. One its member logs after the `Adopt`, with no crash between, was taken before it, so `tracedata` writes its first `maydeliver` line as `logged`, which delivers it there; only a crash leaves open versions to land in any subset |
| `Logged` of the primary's own copy | `OwnLogged` | Its record durable, in any version order, as a write covering part of a block waits for its base |
| `Committed` | `Answer` | Once the own record and every member's are durable and the chunk's earlier pending versions are answered, as the store maps committed versions in version order. A stutter for a version the decision that settled its interval already acknowledged |
| `PeerReply`, `PeerChunk`, `Decide`, `Kept`, `Listed` | `Peer`, taken as `PeerOn` | `askPeers`, `peerAsked`, `answerPeers`, `mayPeer`, `peerReplied` and `decide`, with each reply compared to the spec's `Reply` at the decision. `tracedata` places the line before the format of a disk that answered first. The line gives the set `J` the code decided on, the disks that persist are those of the trace's `Persisted` lines for the interval, and the members listed beyond `Entry`, `T`, are those the code's `Listed` records name, so the trace adds no branching. `T` must meet `TornSets`' guard, the lists must equal `ListOf`'s under it for every up member, and every reply with `logged` above `whole` on a member `Entry` leaves off must be in it. A `logged` above `whole` must name a version ordered; otherwise the two are equal, the one number the spec's reply has |
| `Persisted` | `PeerOn` | `persistLists`, `persist`, `persisted`, `persistAck`, `persistAcked`: a stutter for a disk that persisted at the decision, refused once the interval activated unless it repeats that disk's list |
| `Activate` | `Activate` | `tryActivate`, once every up member's `Persisted` was seen, so `Activate` itself persists no list |
| `Crash` | `Restart` | Own records not reported durable may be lost (`mayfail`, by `OwnFail`), newest first: a line loses its version only if the line before lost its own. A crash loses a suffix of the disk's log in LSN order, and a primary's store submits its own records in the order it orders them, so what a crash keeps of them is a prefix of that order (`TestACrashKeepsAPrefixOfTheOrderedVersions`), and a crash with n such lines has n + 1 branches, not the product of each chunk's. A reply's `logged` above `whole` for a version of its node's last crash names the record that crash kept in part, the oldest it lost, so the `mayfail` line after it kept its version (discrepancy 32). With two or more rounds in flight a later round can land before an earlier one, and replay ends at the gap: a quarter of the seeds run at `CommitDepth` 2 for it, the test at 3. No traced run injects a disk fault nor fills a disk, so an own record is never refused without a crash, which would leave its line open below a kept one |
| `Format` | `Format` | |
| `Recovered` | `Recover`, taken as `RecoverFrom` | The line binds the source the record names, which a member has from the recovery write, and 0 for no source must meet a listed version of 0. The version is the listed one or one the interval ordered. `tracedata` places a record from after the primary, the target or the source left the interval before the first of those steps, if the primary ordered the write before it, and leaves any other where the line fails. A primary's record of its own copy of a recovery write is a stutter while a member lists the chunk or once one recovered that version, and so is the record of a gated write settled by a later activation of the PG by the same primary, whose entry stays. Either stutter needs the line's node to have decided the record's interval, its version to be that decision's kept one or one of the interval, and its source an up member of the interval, none only at kept version 0. A primary's record of its own copy that lands after it took its own disk's reply for an interval later than the record's and than every one it decided that some primary activated, and before that interval activated, is `recoveredlate`, a stutter once the primary left the interval: the decision of that interval, made or to come, reads the reply and lists the chunk again (discrepancies 23 and 36). A line for a chunk no disk lists fails |
| `RecoverOrder` | A stutter | The primary ordering a recovery write, target or not: it must lead the interval, activated, with some disk listing the chunk, and every `recovered` or `mayrecover` line needs its order earlier. A primary ordering after it left stays at its record and fails. An order naming a source formatted since goes before that `format` when the source's `RecoverRead` record, the member reading the image for the primary, came before it, as `Recover` takes the read with the write; otherwise it stays, and the `recovered` line after it fails on a source with no node |
| `Recovering` | `Recover` or a stutter | A store taking a recovery write, with the version it is logged under. A crash before its `Recovered` lets it land under that version (`mayrecover`), as replay maps it |
| `Reported`, `Ask` | `ReportRecovered`, `AskNext`, `CounterOut` or `RestartAsk` | The action's interval is compared to the line's. `tracedata` names an ask `restartask` if its node restarted and has not activated the PG since, which only `RestartAsk` takes |
| `Lost` | `Lost` | The operator's declaration, recorded by the harness |
| `MemberFail`, `Fail` | `MemberFail` | No traced run injects a disk fault, so the one refusal of a version of the member's interval with a step is `unready`, the record's field for a store not serving: replaying its log after a restart, rebuilding its index or stopped by a disk fault (discrepancy 40). A later refusal the failed version causes carries the field it failed with, even once the store serves. The run's plan gives `MemberFail` a fault budget for it. A refusal by a serving store (`mfail`) has no step, nor has a refusal of a recovery write that is not `gone` (`mfailrecover`, `unreadyrecover`). `tracedata` holds the line until the primary's `Fail` of the chunk, the step that ends the version there, or until the member moves on or the primary crashes |
| `MemberFail` with `gone` | `GoneRefuses` | A node whose disk was formatted again, refusing what the primary sends the old disk. A repeat is a stutter |
| `MemberFail` with `gone` and `recover` | `GoneRefusesRecovery` | The same node refusing a recovery write for the old disk, which ends the interval at the primary |

The record kinds of the event loop, such as `NetRecv` and `DiskDone`, have no spec action: they are
the machine's steps below the protocol's, and the records above say what those steps did. `tracedata`
lists them in `belowProtocol`, and stops on a record neither mapped nor listed.

`TestALeftMemberDownAtItsMovesEndKeepsAcknowledgedWrites`, seeds 0 to 9 (`leftdown`): all 10 pass, 586 to 856
lines in 4 to 241 s, with no discrepancy. The code drops a left PG's gated versions in the drain after it adopts

a reply still carrying a dropped version would fail its `peer` line. In seeds 3, 4, 5 and 8 the spec's `ldrp`

Not yet run, and owed by the [checklist](build-checklist.md): `TestReplicatedWritesSurviveFaults`, the lease half and the give-up.

The `conform` workflow runs this check nightly on a window of 500 seeds that moves each day, from seed
40 up, of the primary-change run and of the voter model's replacement run, with 20 minutes per trace
where a local run gives 400 s, and the plants over seeds 0 to 39. A failure names its seed,
and `RUN='^TestPeeringKeepsAcknowledgedWritesAcrossPrimaries$|^TestConformReplacementSeeds$' FIRST=<seed>
COUNT=1 scripts/conform.sh` replays it. The real-group runs' traces (`real-primaries-<seed>`) are not in it. For a change to
the epoch or voter model, its trace spec, `internal/chunkstore`, `internal/lease`, `internal/raftshard`, `internal/trace`,
`tools/tracedata`, `tools/votersdata` or the script (`scripts/conform-paths`), the `gate` workflow runs 40 seeds of
each model with the scripted traces, and the plants over seeds 0 to 9, each caught plant rejected on one of them, and a failure there is a discrepancy to settle before the change
merges. Both run on the SYS-2 runner, so a pull request's gate skips them. `scripts/gate-branch.sh` runs the local default, the epoch model's scripted and sweep traces and 50 seeds of the voter model's, on a branch that touches those paths. A plant run fails as each model's [traces can fail](#traces-can-fail-in-the-epoch-models-check) section says.

`refillSoleHolder` is not in `conformPlants`: the primary-change run is too short for a member merely down to go missing, so a refill of one appears only in `scripted-refill`, and a `Stay` only in `scripted-stay`, and `TestPlantedPeeringBugsBreakTheOracle` breaks the rule through the simulator's invariant.

Each run ends with what its passing traces covered, and each trace's rows stay in its directory's
`cover` file. TLC prints the behavior a trace passed by, and `cover` in `scripts/conform.sh` reads it: a
line took its action when a variable of `epoch.tla` moved from the state before it, and stuttered when
none did. A pass shows one behavior TLC found, so a line counted as a stutter may also have had a real
step open to it, and on `maydeliver`, `mayfail` and `mayrecover` a line counted as taken may also have had
a stutter open to it: it shows only what that behavior did. TLC's own `-coverage` does not fit: it counts how often each expression was evaluated
over every branch of the search, abandoned ones and `ENABLED` too, so on seed 55 `Remove`'s first guard
shows 8 against the 2 removals the trace took.

Over the 56 traces of that run, which pass. `RestartAsk` takes 59 `restartask` lines and finds the ask already made on 106, and `maydeliver` lines are left only at a crash or at a second table, and none landed in the behaviors TLC found:

`table`, `persisted` and `recoverorder` lines check a state and take no action, as their
mapping says. Each `gonerecover` refusal lands after the interval already ended, so `GoneRefusesRecovery`
changes nothing on its lines (discrepancy 33). The actions of `Next` no trace took:

| Action | Why |
| --- | --- |
| `Persist` | Compressed: a `peer` line takes it in `PeerOn`, and a `persisted` line only checks it |
| `CounterOut` | An `ask` line can take it, but it needs a chunk at 1,000,000 versions, which no run writes |
| `MemberFail` | Only an `unready` line takes it, a refusal by a member whose store is not serving, which no trace here has: seed 20 of the real-group run, a member whose store still replays after a restart, does (discrepancy 40) |
| `GoneRefusesRecovery` | Its lines change nothing, as the interval had already ended, so they count as stutters (discrepancy 33) |
| `AskNext` | Each of its 13 `ask` lines finds the PG's ask already made |
| `Refuse` | A fenced client write. No record maps it |
| `SetMinLive`, `Die`, `Isolate` | No run of the test changes `min_live`, ends a daemon or cuts a node from the control plane |
| `Split` | No traced run doubles a pool's `pg_count`, so the `reported` line matches a report by PG number and interval and leaves out the model's split count; a traced split would map the report's `pg_count` to it |
| `OpenGrant`, `OpenLapse`, `Ask`, `Grant`, `GrantRefused`, `SendHb`, `RecvGrant`, `RecvHb`, `RoundTrip`, `Beat`, `EndWait` | The lease half, not traced: the spec's time moves by `Tick` only when no protocol step is enabled, where a run works while time passes, so a lease record has no mapping yet |
| `GiveUp` | No traced run gives up a chunk or a PG, and the leader's give-up has no record |
| `Fortify`, `Elect`, `Transfer`, `StepDown` | Raft, not traced: `MaxTerm` is 0 |
| `Tick`, `Suspend`, `Wake`, `Freeze`, `Thaw`, `RateStep`, `Reboot`, `BootUp`, `NetFault` | Clock and network faults, not traced: `Clocks` is off |

The code refuses any write while its store is not serving, and the trace's plan gave `MemberFail` no budget, since no traced run injects a disk fault | spec | Settled, seed 20 of `TestPeeringKeepsAcknowledgedWritesAcrossPrimariesOnTheRealGroup` at line 272: the restart is the fault. The record's `unready` field says the store was not serving (replaying, rebuilding its index or stopped by a disk fault) when the refused version, or the failed one it follows, failed. `tracedata` writes such a refusal as an `unready` line, and `trace_epoch.tla` takes it by `MemberFail` with `"mfail"` in the plan, leaving an `mfail` line, a serving store's refusal, with no step. `TestARecoveringMemberRefusesWrites` holds the field for refusals while the store replays and after it serves. Open: an `unreadyrecover` line, an unready store refusing a recovery write, has no step, as an `mfailrecover` line has none, since the spec has no member failure of a recovery write but `GoneRefusesRecovery`; a recovery target restarted after its interval activated could make one, and no trace has. The restart already makes the member ask for a new interval, so the refusal costs the PG no extra one. Of the real-group run's seeds 0 to 39, checked at 60 s each, only seed 20 has such a refusal; 5 pass, 35 give no verdict, and none stops at a line |

### Traces can fail in the epoch model's check

`scripts/conform.sh plants` runs `TestPlantsKeepTraces` over `conformPlants`, the plants of the
`chunkstore.*` rows of the [rule map](#model-gate) and of `TestPlantedPeeringBugsBreakTheOracle`, each in
the primary-change run with every invariant checked. On a seed whose unplanted trace passes it
compares the planted trace's lines with the baseline's. Fired means only that those lines differ, not
that the rule was reached: a plant can move timing alone. The same lines are no evidence. Otherwise TLC
checks the trace. `FIRST` and `COUNT` choose the seeds, `PLANTS` the plants and `JOBS` the checks at once, the
seeds' baselines first and then the planted traces of those that pass. A run stops at its first
broken invariant, keeping the trace up to there and saying which broke in a `.stop` file.
`CONFORM_RUNON=1` runs on past the break, needed when the invariant sees a step before its record:
`sameMembers` and `keepID` pass every trace cut at the break. Over all 40 seeds run-on passes Go's
10-minute test limit, so it runs a seed at a time. A rejection counts once the failing line has been
read to be the planted behaviour. The run fails when a seed's baseline fails, or when one of the 17
plants of the rules the check catches below fires on some seed and TLC rejects it on none. Each fires
on some of seeds 0 to 39, so over those seeds, a pull request's, one that fires on none fails too, as a
plant that no longer does anything; on another window, where most fire on a few seeds in 40 or none, that
is no evidence.

`mergeOnDropped`, `editKeepsInterval`, `relistNever`, `peerInOldInterval`, `oldReport`, `recoverFromListed`,
`listerVetoes`, `listerOrders` and `noDegradedHold`, the last once, the oracle breaking first on its other seeds, and for 2 more, `sameMembers` and `keepID`, running on over 30.
At a8c61104, over seeds 0 to 39, the 17 plants `conform.sh` expects caught are rejected on these counts of the seeds they fire on:
`activateEarly`, `editKeepsInterval`, `reportDecided` and `goneWhileUp` 40 of 40, `sendEpoch` 34 of 34, `oldReport` 17 of 40,
`peerInOldInterval` 14 of 18, `noDegradedHold` and `removeOnActivation` 14 of 14, `mergeWhileLacking` and `listerOrders` 11 of 11,
`recoverFromListed` 9 of 9, `mergeOnDropped`, `relistNever`, `listerVetoes` and `ownInterval` 4 of 4, `ackOnLoneCopy` 3 of 3.
`readOldDisk`, the 40th rule, is shown cleanly by its scripted trace rather than a seed.
`settleByNumber` and `mapOnReplay` are rejected at lines not yet read to their rules. Open: `coverAtRead`,
which needs a record of the blocks a recovery write leaves out; `neverAsk`, `memberNoAsk` and `writeOnUnfound`, omissions no line can name;
`freshGrantNoCheck`, with the lease half; `resendNewestFirst`, `stopPreviousOnly`, `lastActivatedOnly`, `forgetImage`
`mapOnDemote` and `clearNoSource`, which need a seed that reaches them; and the seven that never fire. Of the oracle plants with no rule,
`settleSubset` needs a record of what `Settle` answered.

Every relaxed path has a plant: `img` in `Order`, which the hold on a primary that lists the chunk leaves only to `ListerOrders`, by `mergeWhileLacking` with `listerOrders`, `img` as a
recovery source by `recoverFromListed` and `mergeOnDropped`, `Recover` at kept version 0 by `clearNoSource`, and `GoneRefuses` by
`goneWhileUp`. Each breaks a seeded invariant in `TestPlantedPeeringBugsBreakTheOracle` and fails its negative
configuration. Of the 46 plant traces that passed to their end, checked again with each path removed, 3 stop
where their baseline does not, and all three are schedules legitimately on the path, by a plant that does not
touch it: at `neverAsk` 6 and 22 and `freshGrantNoCheck` 37 the primary dropped a version it ordered itself, so its
image is the kept version, and it merges at once or, as `startRecovery` prefers, serves recovery from itself.
`mayfail` and `maydeliver` let none of the plants tried through, which says nothing of a plant not tried: every
planted step the check missed lies in a variable or record no line reads. A version a primary drops right after
`OutOrder`, by `r.fail` in `ordered`, stays in `ownOpen` and becomes a `mayfail` at a later crash; that path needs
a lead that is asking or has left the interval, which `Order`'s guards refuse first, so it loosens no passing trace.

### The voter model's check

`scripts/conform.sh` checks the `voters-*` traces of `internal/raftshard` against
`models/voters/voters.tla`: `TestConformScriptedReplacement`, a replacement with no fault but the
cut-off voter, and `TestConformReplacementSeeds`, the replacement run of
`TestVoterReplacementRunsReplayFromTheirSeed` under the Raft runs' faults with its first leader
crashed, over `COUNT` seeds, 50 unless set. While conforming, the harness records each round's
entries (`RaftEntry`) and snapshot (`RaftSnap`) as the replica takes them, its Raft state after each
pass that logged entries or moved its term, lead, commit, applied index or flags (`RaftState`), the
leader of its term it supports and, as leader, the peers whose fortification of its term runs, after
a pass that moved either, with why the support it had ended (`RaftSupport`), a test's forced hand-off (`RaftForced`) and the plan it
hands the replicas (`RaftPlan`).
`tools/votersdata` writes the run's constants (the replicas, base voters and plan, and the terms,
crashes, halts and deaths taken, as bounds) and one line per Raft step. `models/voters/trace_voters.tla`,
with `voters.tla` unchanged by it, takes each line as the epoch model's check does, with `TypeOK`,
`AtMostOneLeader`, `CommittedNeverLost`, `CommittedAgree`, `ReportsHold`, `VotersCaughtUp`,
`DeletesOnlyRemoved` and `LearnsOnlyRemoved` on every state; the lease invariants are left out,
since no line reads a lease and a leader's count of a peer that ends and comes back on the node-pair
lease is no line, so the spec's count runs ahead of the code's. `voters.tla` has no command entries
and no failed-election terms but a halted leader's failed hand-off, so `votersdata` takes a code
index as the entries up to it that are not commands, past the boot snapshot at index 1, and a code
term as its rank among the terms a replica led in or a halted leader's hand-off failed in. A line that
moves no spec index, such as a command's commit, is a stutter at every state, and holds back no
placement below.

| Records | Line | Spec action | Compression |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `RaftState` taking the lead | `elect`, `transfer` | `Elect`, `Transfer` | A campaign on a `MsgTimeoutNow` is a `transfer`, unless a `RaftForced` record asked for it: the outgoing fault's hand-off to the replica the plan drops, which `Transfer` never makes, is the outgoing half's `Elect` (discrepancy 9). Only a `MsgTimeoutNow` taken in the campaign's own pass counts, so one the shard holds while a round is in flight and steps a pass later would make its campaign an `elect`. No seed has one: seed 12's three later term moves follow `MsgTimeoutNow`s from its halted leader of an older term, which etcd-raft drops, and seed 48's is a forced hand-off's. Such an `elect` fails, not passes, since the support of the leader handing off is not lapsed in a term a replica led. The line checks the term |
| `RaftState` raising the term alone | `term` | A stutter | A heartbeat of a later term, or a failed election, which raises no spec term |
| `RaftEntry` of a change the replica proposed | `addlearner`, `swap`, `leave` | `AddLearner`, `Swap`, `Leave` | The line compares the whole configuration. A pass's proposals follow its apply, as etcd-raft proposes the leave on applying the joint configuration (discrepancy 8). The leave a leader past its removal proposes again outside a joint configuration changes nothing and is no entry (discrepancy 10) |
| A follower's `RaftState` after a pass that logged entries or moved its commit | `replicate` | `Replicate`, or a stutter while the spec's follower holds as much | `Replicate` hands the follower the leader's whole log and current commit in one step, where etcd-raft batches a long log: the follower's log terms are a prefix of the spec's and its commit at most the spec's (discrepancy 6). An append that lands after its leader stopped leading the term or applied a configuration without the follower is placed at the line where that happened, unless a later line of the follower's comes first (discrepancies 5 and 15) |
| A leader's `RaftState` moving its commit | `commit` | `Commit`, the append's answer, or a stutter while the spec's is as high | |
| `RaftState` moving the applied index | `apply` | `Apply`, or a stutter while the spec's is as high | |
| `RaftState` flagging the removal | `removed`, `notice` | `Apply`, `Notice` | Learned by applying when the configuration the replica applied held it and the one it knows committed does not (discrepancy 1), a stutter once the spec learned it on an earlier apply (discrepancy 12); otherwise a notice from the peer whose message the pass took |
| A halted leader's `RaftState` stepping down to a term no replica led | `handofffails` | `HandOffFails` | Its target's failed election raised the term; the line checks it (discrepancy 18) |
| A leader's `RaftSupport` counting a voter of its applied configuration after a pass that took that voter's answer | `fortify`, then a `lapse` of each replica the code's leader has no support from | `Fortify`, or a stutter where the spec's leader cannot fortify, then `Lapse` or a stutter | `Fortify` has every voter of the term support the leader at once; the lapses leave the spec's supporters those of the code. A count of a learner, or one back on the node-pair lease with no answer, is no line (discrepancy 17); a test's halt that takes an earlier apply's place goes before it (discrepancy 19). The leader's count itself is not checked: a count that shrinks is no line, one that grows is checked as within the spec's only where `Fortify` is taken, and the lapses then strip the spec's count to the code's supporters, so a leader that counts a supporter it never had passes. The simulator's invariants that no two replicas serve lease reads at overlapping times and that a lease read sees every applied entry check it, and the epoch model checks the lease rules |
| A follower's `RaftSupport` ending its support | `askleader` after a pass that took the leader's node's answer; `lapse` for an end in the support's term, a forced hand-off's vote, or a vote the support lets through in a term no replica led; no line for any other end | `AskLeader`, `Lapse`, or a stutter where the spec's follower supports no such leader | The record says why the support ended: in its term, as the grant lapsed or the leader or its node showed it no longer leads; or on a term move, by a vote the support lets through (a transfer target's request, the leader's own, a `MsgTimeoutNow`), in a forced hand-off's term, or by anything else. The code's leader stops counting before its follower stops supporting, where `Lapse` ends both at once. A support a term move ended stays the spec's until that term's `Run` or `Replicate` ends it, so `Run`'s rule that a supporter votes only for its leader or the target it hands off to is checked: a follower that votes while it supports a leader is refused at the election (the `disloyal` plant). A forced hand-off is an `Elect` with no leader handing off (discrepancy 9), and an election no replica won has no spec step (discrepancy 20), so their votes end the support with a `lapse` |
| `RaftState` flagging a halt | `halt` | `Halt` | A test's `Shard.Halt`, with nothing left to apply, takes the place of the replica's last `apply` line, unless a later line of the replica's comes first (discrepancies 11 and 15) |
| `RaftState` flagging a deletion | `delete` | `Delete` | |
| `Crash`; a `Pause` for good; a `Restart` and the next `RaftState` | `crash`, `die`, `restart` | `Crash`, `Die`, `Restart` | The restart's commit index is at most the spec's, its applied index equal |
| `RaftSnap`, `RaftPlan` | | | A snapshot sets the replica's base; the plan is the constant `Plan` (discrepancy 13) |

Checking commit and applied indexes only as at most the spec's lets no trace pass where the code
commits or applies an entry the spec never commits. Every `replicate` line carries the follower's
log terms, a prefix of the spec's log there, so an index the code commits or applies is within the
spec's log and at most its commit, the terms pin each entry up to it, an entry is named by index and
term under `AtMostOneLeader`, and each proposal's configuration is compared at its line. Before the
terms were on the line, a follower holding other entries at the same indexes passed. What the check
does allow is the spec running ahead of the code, so a guard the code's own state did not meet can
hold in the spec's: `NoticeIndex`, `OneAtATime`, `CampaignApplied`, `Delete`'s reports. The plants of
those guards are still rejected below, so equality where the two agree is not needed. Running ahead
can also refuse a step the code takes, as discrepancy 16 did; each such case is a discrepancy.
Support does not run ahead: a `fortify` line's lapses and a support's end bring the spec's
supporters to the code's, except where a term move ended the support, which only that term's `Run`
or `Replicate` ends, so a vote is checked against the supports the code's voter held, and a node's
answer to an ask whenever the spec's follower still supports that leader. A `replicate` line's
commit at most its log's length checks the data module, not the code: `votersdata` counts both
from the same entries, capped at the replica's last, so its own output always meets it, and only a
hand-edited module fails it. One gap is left: a `fortify` line lapses every replica the code's leader
has no support from, so one that falls between a supporter's vote for another replica and the
election that vote helps win would hide the vote; no seed or plant places one there, and skipping
the replicas whose support a term move ended would refuse a legal trace in which the same leader
leads again.

Results, `COUNT` 50, in one run with `JOBS=4`, 49 s for both models' traces:

| Trace | Lines | Result | Seconds |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `voters-scripted-replacement` | 1,003 | passes | 1 |
| `voters-replace-0` to `voters-replace-49` | 73 to 9,008 | pass, across crashes, halts, deaths, the outgoing fault's hand-off and the wedge | 0 to 2 |

A voter trace takes 0 to 2 s, so the 51 fit a `JOBS=1` gate in about a minute; that is the default
count. The merge gate of the check itself passed them, conform 149 s at the default. Over those traces:

| Action | Line | Took it | Stuttered | Traces |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `Replicate` | `replicate` | 866 | 13,135 | 51 |
| `Apply` | `apply` | 787 | 23,198 | 51 |
| `Commit` | `commit` | 283 | 10,225 | 51 |
| `Fortify` | `fortify` | 183 | 16 | 51 |

### Traces can fail in the voter model's check

`scripts/conform.sh plants`, after the epoch model's plants, runs `TestVoterPlantsKeepTraces` over
`conformPlants` in `internal/raftshard`, one row per voter rule with a Go plant and one for
`disloyal`, whose rule, `Run`'s that a supporter votes only for its leader or the target it hands off
to, no flag turns off: the plant's run on the
first seed from its test's own whose run breaks the plant's invariant, to the step it broke, and the
same seed's run with no plant to its end. Every baseline passes, and 11 of the 18 plants are
caught: TLC rejects a line no state can take with every spec invariant intact. Four are clean,
rejected before the run broke its own invariant: `voter-first`, `joint-one-half`,
`one-at-a-time` and `disloyal`. The other seven are rejected at the run's last line, where the code's invariant
broke too. Not every rejection is at the planted step or by the plant's own rule: each row names the
guard that refuses the line, found by checking the trace again with flags set off. `restart-commit-at-base` and
`hard-state-old` are rejected at the later election, not at the planted restart, and
`hard-state-old` and `delete-on-plan` by a guard other than their own rule's. A row names the line
where the plant's trace first differs from its baseline's, and the run fails when a baseline fails,
a trace gives no data or no verdict, or one of those 11 passes; the other 7 may pass.

| Plant | Rule | Seed | Rejected at | Guard, or why not caught |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `campaign-unapplied` | `neg-campaign-unapplied` | 0 | The last line, the second leader's `elect` | `CampaignApplied` |
| `restart-commit-at-base` | `neg-restart-commit-at-base` | 0 | The last line, the second leader's `elect`. The planted `restart` (line 872, commit 1) passes, since a restart's commit is checked only as at most the spec's | `CampaignApplied`, on the spec's restart at its durable commit: with it or `DurableCommit` off the `elect` is taken and `AtMostOneLeader` breaks |
| `hard-state-old` | `neg-hard-state-old` | 0 | The last line, the second leader's `elect`. The `restart` (line 872, commit 1) passes, as for `restart-commit-at-base` | `CampaignApplied`, not the plant's own rules: with `NewestHardState` and `DurableConfCommit` off the line is still refused, with `CampaignApplied` off too it is taken and `AtMostOneLeader` breaks |
| `voter-first` | `neg-voter-first` | 0 | Line 747 of 1,576, the `addlearner` that adds 4 as a voter | `LearnerFirst` |
| `eager` | `neg-eager` | 0 | The last line, the `swap` of a learner that holds nothing | `CatchUpFirst` |
| `joint-one-half` | `neg-joint-one-half` | 0 | Line 843 of 2,349, the `commit` on one half's quorum | `JointQuorum` |
| `one-at-a-time` | `neg-one-at-a-time` | 0 | Line 748 of 2,366, the `swap` before the learner's addition applied | `OneAtATime` |
| `delete-on-plan` | `neg-delete-on-plan` | 0 | The last line, the removal the plant's deletion flags, which `votersdata` writes as a `notice` from the peer whose message the pass took | `Notice`'s test that the peer's applied configuration lacks the replica, not `DeleteOnCommitted`: with it off the line is still refused, as a `notice` line is never `DeleteOnPlan` |
| `notice-any-index` | `neg-notice-any-index` | 0 | Line 1, a base voter's notice from the replacement that applied nothing | `NoticeIndex`: with it off the line is taken and `LearnsOnlyRemoved` breaks |
| `notice-non-member` | `neg-notice-non-member` | 0 | Line 1, the replacement's notice before its addition | `NoticeMember` |
| `disloyal` | None | 0 | Line 892 of 898, the `elect` of a replica that campaigned while it supported the leader, won with the vote of another that supported it too | `Run`'s support rule: with it left out the line is taken |
| `no-support-ask` | `neg-no-support-ask` | 2 | Passes | The ask the plant leaves out is no line, and `NewLeader` is liveness, which a trace's lines do not check |

## Models in CI

The runs of [TLA+ and TLC](#tla-and-tlc) on GitHub's hosted runners ([Continuous
integration](design.md#testing-strategy)), each job a matrix item on its own runner. The runner
checks a `ci` configuration 2.7 to 3.2 times slower than the M4 Pro the budgets are measured on,
and a `deep` one 2.0 to 2.4 times slower, so the workflows set their own limits.

- The `gate` workflow (`.github/workflows/gate.yml`), on every change, hashes each `ci` and
  negative configuration with its model's spec and the TLC version and checksum lines of
  `scripts/models.sh`. A configuration whose hash has a pass cached by a push to main or a
  `gate/` branch is skipped and named in the run's summary; each other one gets a job that runs
  `scripts/models.sh ci` on it with `CI_LIMIT` 2,000 and, if it passes, caches its result line
  under the hash. A pull request's passes go to its own cache scope, so they skip nothing else. The
  configurations run side by side: run one after another, they take hours.
- A rule removed from a spec, with no negative configuration changed, fails some configuration's
  job: a `ci` configuration or a negative variant fails and its trace is printed.
- A configuration past 2,000 s on the runner fails its job; one past 600 s on the M4 Pro is split,
  as `ci-restarts` holds three plans and `ci-restarts-moved` the fourth, or its largest constant
  moves to `deep`.
- Nightly, and when started by hand, the `models` workflow (`.github/workflows/models.yml`) runs
  one job per model of `scripts/models.sh sim` with `SIM_SECONDS` 3,600, split evenly among the
  model's `ci` configurations but those under `FairSpec`, and prints every seed; a failing seed's
  printed replay reproduces its trace.
- Nightly, and when started by hand, the same workflow hashes each `deep` configuration the same
  way. If the job cache holds a pass under that hash, the job prints the pass's result line and
  stops; otherwise it runs `scripts/models.sh deep` on the configuration with `DEEP_LIMIT` 19,800,
  5.5 of the job's 6 hours, and, if it passes, stores its result line in the cache under the hash
  and in the run's summary, from which it goes into the [Model-to-simulator
  map](#model-to-simulator-map)'s results table. A failed run stores nothing and runs again the
  next night.
- A TLC bump therefore reruns every configuration, and a spec change every one of its model's.
- No job runs a `heavy` configuration.
- GitHub evicts a cache entry unused for 7 days, and its configuration then runs again.

## Wire messages

The frame, the PG fields and the version packing are in [Wire messages](design.md#wire-messages).
k.n is version (interval k, counter n).

| Message | Fields |
| --- | --- |
| Connection hello | The client's session ID and incarnation (the daemon's start time on `CLOCK_BOOTTIME`) |
| Chunk write, client to primary | PG fields, session ID, incarnation (8 bytes), chunk ID (16 bytes), byte range within the chunk, optional `expect_ver` and whether it flushes under a space grant, in one flags byte, snapshot epoch; as data, the blocks the range touches |
| Chunk write, primary to member | The above, plus the version; as data, the merged whole blocks |
| Recovery write, primary to member | PG fields, chunk ID, the version it brings the member to, and the disk its image was read from, 0 when it needed none; as data, the recovery buffer, or none when it only ends the chunk's listing |
| Write acknowledgment, member to primary | Version and the member's disk fill; or `NoSpace`; or a refusal (the member's table epoch and the PG's interval) |
| Write reply to the client | Version; or `NoSpace`; or a refusal (the member's table epoch and the PG's interval); or an `expect_ver` mismatch |
| Punch | PG fields, session ID, incarnation, chunk ID, byte range, optional `expect_ver`, snapshot epoch; the version when sent to a member; the shard and its Raft term when the purger sends it ([Freeing space](design.md#freeing-space)). Answered as a write is |
| Read | PG fields, chunk ID, byte range, optional `at_ver` |
| Read reply | Version, and as data the blocks read; or a refusal (wrong interval, chunk on the missing list, unfound) |
| Lease request, holder to grantor | The holder's table epoch; the grantor grants only if it is at least its own |
| Grant | Support epoch; the grantor's run ID and `CLOCK_MONOTONIC_RAW` reading `g`; no table epoch, since the request reported the holder's ([Epoch change model](#epoch-change-model)); or a refusal with the grantor's table epoch |
| Heartbeat between a node pair | The sender's table epoch; as a grantor, its run ID and `CLOCK_MONOTONIC_RAW`, on every heartbeat |
| Heartbeat to the authority | Activation reports (PG fields); recovered reports (PG fields), once every member of the interval but a leaving one is up and lists nothing, on each heartbeat until a table records the interval recovered or starts another; each member's acknowledgment latency; per disk its log ID, fill, oldest unfinished I/O age and whether its log has failed |
| `member_timeout` report, primary to authority | PG fields, member disk |
| Direct probe, authority to a disk's owner loop | Disk ID |
| Probe reply | Log ID, oldest unfinished I/O age, whether the log has failed |
| Peering request | PG fields naming the interval to adopt; the disk asked |
| Peering reply | The disk that answers; the interval of the newest decision the member persisted for the PG, 0 for none; per chunk it logged or lists, the newest version held whole, the newest version logged, and the kept version it lists, if any |
| Missing list | PG fields; the disk it is for; per chunk, the kept version the member must receive; answered by a persist acknowledgment naming the member's disk and the interval whose decision it persisted, or 0 with the member's table epoch and interval for a refusal |

**Cases**

- Every kind round-trips, with each optional field present and absent and each list empty and not.
- The frame of every kind matches `internal/chunkstore/testdata/wire_golden.txt`.
- 1.1 packs to `0x0000000100000001`.
- In a primary-to-member write of 1 block and of 1,024 blocks, the data is the message's own pool
  buffer and each block starts at a block-aligned offset of it. Decoding reads the frame and only
  the buffer's length, so the receiver keeps the buffer it received and copies no data byte.
- A frame over 256 bytes (257 bytes) travels in a pool buffer, zero-padded to whole blocks, with no
  inline bytes; one of exactly 256 bytes stays inline. The 256-byte inline limit itself is under
  [Event and Action types](#event-and-action-types).
- Each request that carries data has a reply that carries a refusal (`Refused`, `NoSpace`): a
  client write's reply and a member write's acknowledgment. That reply is what lets the driver
  release the send buffer (driver contract).
- A long frame given a data buffer is a broken invariant of the sender's own state, and panics.
- Encoding and decoding a member write, a read and a read reply allocate nothing.

**Rejects.** Each is an error returned to the caller, never a panic.

| Input | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Unknown version byte | Rejected as another version |
| Unknown message kind, or a kind its decoder does not take | Malformed |
| Truncated at every length from 0 to full − 1 | Malformed |
| A trailing extra byte | Malformed |
| A frame in a pool buffer with a non-zero pad byte, an extra block of padding, or 256 bytes or fewer | Malformed |
| Byte range with offset + length > 4 MiB, or a length of 0 | Malformed |
| Write data length ≠ the range's block count × 4,096, client or member; data on a kind that carries none | Malformed |
| A read reply's data not a whole number of blocks, past 4 MiB, or none on success | Malformed |
| A version with interval 0 and counter ≠ 0, or counter 0 and interval ≠ 0 | Malformed (0 alone is the absent chunk) |
| A member write or punch at version 0, a client's with a version, an acknowledgment of success at version 0 | Malformed |
| A write, client or member, with a shard or Raft term | Malformed |
| An absent optional version that is not 0, or a flag byte other than 0 or 1 | Malformed |
| Interval number 0 in the PG fields or a refusal | Malformed (intervals start at 1) |
| A status its reply kind does not take (an acknowledgment takes success, `NoSpace` and `Refused`; a client's reply also a mismatch; a read reply success, `Refused`, missing and unfound), a grant status other than granted or refused; a peering request with lists | Malformed |

- [fuzz] The seed corpus holds one valid frame of every kind. Random mutations never panic the
  decoder, and anything that decodes re-encodes to the same bytes.

## Pools

Unit and data-driven tests for pool settings, creation rules and capacity figures, from [Pools and redundancy](design.md#pools-and-redundancy) and [Volume size and capacity](design.md#volume-size-and-capacity). Phase 3 covers pools of 1 to 3 copies. Erasure-coded settings are refused until phase 10. C3 still checks `ec4-2`'s capacity arithmetic, which is a pure function.

**Settings and defaults**

| Input | Expected |
| --- | --- |
| A pool created with no settings | `replicas` 3, `min_live` 2, `failure_domain` node, `max_per_domain` 1, `locality` spread, `overcommit` on, `write_limit` unset (each disk's default, below), `disk_class` any, `pg_count` a power of two sized from the disk count |
| `replicas` 1 | `min_live` 1, `locality` node |
| `replicas` 2 | `min_live` 2, `locality` spread |
| `replicas` 0 or 4 | Rejected with an error naming the setting, never a panic |
| `sealed: ec`, `data`, `parity` or `encode_on_write` set (phase 3) | Rejected as not supported yet, with an error naming the setting |
| `failure_domain` other than `node` or `disk` | Rejected |
| `pg_count` 0, 3 or 1,000 | Rejected: it must be a non-zero power of two (as in IDs and hashing) |
| `pg_count` sized for 60 disks, `rep3` alone | 2048, the smallest power of two giving each disk at least 100 members (2048 × 3 ÷ 60 ≈ 102; 1024 would give 51) |
| `min_live` above `replicas`, or 0 | Rejected: it must be 1 to `replicas`, as Ceph's `min_size` must be 1 to `size` |
| `write_limit` of 10% or less | Rejected: `NearFull` starts 10 points below it |
| `write_limit` unset, member disks of 1 TiB, 256 GiB, 128 GiB, 64 GiB, 32 GiB, 16 GiB, 8 GiB and 1 GiB (segments of 64, 64, 32, 16, 8, 4, 2 MiB and 256 KiB) | Each disk's limit is ⌊size in blocks × its default⌋: 90%, 90%, 90%, 85%, 85%, 75%, 55%, 50%. `NearFull` is 10 points below each |
| `write_limit` 90% set, the same disks | Every disk's limit is 90% of its size |
| Installing a cluster | Creates one pool, `rep3`, as the default |
| `replicas` or `min_live` changed later | Accepted. The next table starts a new interval of every PG of the pool (asserted in Placement computation) |
| `failure_domain`, `write_limit`, `disk_class` or `overcommit` changed later | Accepted ("every other setting can change later") |
| `pg_count` doubled | Accepted. PG p splits into 2p and 2p + 1 |
| `pg_count` halved, or set to a value that is not a double of the current one | Rejected: it only doubles |

**Creation rules**

| Layout | Pool | Expected |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 3 nodes | `rep3`, `failure_domain` node | Accepted. The CLI states that copies survive 2 node failures, and that losing any one node leaves its PGs degraded until it returns; `rock-solid pool status` repeats it |
| 4 nodes | `rep3`, `failure_domain` node | Accepted, with no such loss stated: three nodes are left after any one fails |
| 2 nodes | `rep3`, `failure_domain` node | Rejected: width 3 > 2 domains |
| 2 nodes | `rep3`, `max_per_domain` 2 | Rejected: copies always sit in distinct failure domains |
| 2 nodes | `rep2` | Accepted. Survives 1 node failure |
| 1 node with 3 disks | `rep3`, `failure_domain` disk | Accepted, surviving 0 node failures: under `failure_domain: disk` nothing keeps a PG's copies on distinct nodes |
| 3 nodes, 2 of them with NVMe disks | `rep3`, `disk_class` NVMe | Rejected: only domains with disks of the class count |
| 1 node | `none` | Accepted |
| Any | Presets `none`, `rep2`, `rep3` | Survive nothing, 1 and 2 failures; need 1, 2 and 3 failure domains; usable/raw 1, 1/2 and 1/3 |

**Capacity figures: the capacity model spike's cases as data-driven files.** Each case file carries:

- the layout;
- the spike's converged integer table with capped targets, as member slots per disk, exported at seed 1 from the [capacity conditions study](../studies/capacity-conditions/README.md)'s port of `spikes/capacity-model/model.py`, which reproduces the spike's available figures to the digit (`internal/chunkstore/testdata/capacity`);
- the fills, and the pool's own data on each disk.

The terms:

- *Capacity* cᵢ of a failure domain is the size × `write_limit` of the pool's disks in it, less other pools' data on them: its room plus this pool's own data there. In an empty pool, capacity and room are equal.
- *Room* is a disk's capacity less this pool's data on it, never below 0.
- *Held* is the pool's data, each chunk's raw bytes divided by its form's overhead.
- *b* is the overhead: `replicas`, or 1.5 for `ec4-2`.
- *a* is the most of each byte one failure domain may hold: 1 for copies, whatever `max_per_domain` is, or `max_per_domain ÷ data` for shards.
- *Balanced* B is min over j of S₍>ⱼ₎ ÷ (b − j·a), over capacities, rounded down to whole blocks.
- *f*, the stranded fraction, is Σᵢ max(0, cᵢ − a·B) ÷ Σᵢ cᵢ; each term is a domain's *stranded room*.
- *Reprotectable* is the least balanced over the survivors of each loss the design lists (Volume size and capacity), among losses whose survivors can hold a PG's width.
- *Available* is the smallest room ÷ share over the pool's disks, computed from the case's table. The expected value is the spike's figure, to within rounding.

| Case | Layout | Capacity (per domain) | Capacity ÷ b | Balanced | Available (spike) | f | Stranded room | Reprotectable (loss) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| C1 | `rep2`, nodes of 0.7 and 2 GB | 0.63, 1.8 GB | 1.215 GB | 0.63 GB | 0.63 GB | 48.1% | B 1.17 GB (65%) | None: no spare domain, and no node has a second disk |
| C2 | `rep3`, nodes of 4, 4, 2, 1 TB | 3.6, 3.6, 1.8, 0.9 TB | 3.300 TB | 2.700 TB | 2.679 TB | 18.2% | A, B 0.9 TB each (25%) | 0.900 TB (node A) |
| C3 | `ec4-2` at 2 per node, nodes of 4, 4, 1 TB (2 disks each) | 3.6, 3.6, 0.9 TB | 5.400 TB | 1.800 TB | 1.800 TB | 66.7% | A, B 2.7 TB each (75%) | None: losing a node, or a disk of any node, leaves fewer than 6 members |
| C4 | `none`, spread, three 2 TB disks, A holding 1.2 TB of another pool | 0.6, 1.8, 1.8 TB | 4.200 TB | 4.200 TB | 4.189 TB (capped targets); 1.786 TB (size-weighted) | 0 | None | Computed (2.400 TB, B or C, not the 3.6 TB of losing A) but never raises `CannotReprotect`: one copy |
| C5 | `rep3`, ten nodes of 4, 4, 4, 2, 2, 2, 1, 1, 1, 0.5 TB | 3.6 ×3, 1.8 ×3, 0.9 ×3, 0.45 TB | 6.450 TB | 6.450 TB | 6.422 TB | 0 | None | 5.250 TB (node A) |
| C6 | `rep2`, nodes of 4, 1, 1 TB | 3.6, 0.9, 0.9 TB | 2.700 TB | 1.800 TB | 1.800 TB | 33.3% | A 1.8 TB (50%; in whole blocks 439,453,126 of 878,906,250) | 0.900 TB (node A) |

Every case also checks available + held ≤ balanced ≤ capacity ÷ b. C4 with a size-weighted table is a case of its own: its available is 1.786 TB, 57% under balanced, which is the input for `Unbalanced`.

- C2 holding 0.8 TB and 1.0 TB at balanced proportions: reprotectable is 0.900 TB in both. Over room it would be 0.633 and 0.567 TB.
- C2 holding 2.0 TB: f is still 18.2% and balanced still 2.700 TB. Over room, balanced would be 0.70 TB.
- Without a spare domain, `rep3` on three nodes: of 2 × 2 TB each, reprotectable is 1.8 TB (losing any one disk); of 2 × 2, 2 × 2 and 4 + 1 TB, 0.9 TB (losing C's 4 TB disk); of one 4 TB disk each, none (no disk to lose within a node).
- A disk past its `write_limit` because of another pool has a capacity and a room of 0, and the pool's available becomes 0, never a negative figure.

The first refused write landing within 0.3% of available is a fill-based check. It belongs to Placement faults and invariants, since Pools does not fill.

**Conditions.** These are raised on the `Pool` resource, as events and as metrics. Fill rows are for the fullest member disk with `write_limit` 90% and no grants, unless stated; a disk's limit is ⌊size in blocks × 0.9⌋.

| Input | Expected |
| --- | --- |
| 79% | No condition |
| Live blocks exactly ⌊0.8 × size in blocks⌋ | `NearFull` |
| One block under the limit | `NearFull`. Available is one block ÷ share, and a one-block write that adds data passes |
| Exactly the limit | `Full`. Available is 0, and the next write that adds data is refused |
| Back to 89.5% after a discard, with block writes held | Still `Full`, which clears at 89%: a held block volume emits one `Full` event, not one per discard |
| `NearFull`, then back to 79.5% | Still `NearFull`; it clears at 79% |
| C2 with four 256 MiB grants, a disk 1 GiB × its share under its limit | `Full`. Available is 0, and admission refuses a write that adds data |
| Two pools on one disk, limits 90% and 95%, disk at 92% | The 90% pool `Full`, the 95% pool `NearFull` (each checks its own limit against the disk's total fill) |
| C1, C2, C3 and C6 created with `rock-solid pool create`, so confirmed at their f | No `Stranded` |
| C1, C2 or C3 as a `Pool` applied without the CLI, never confirmed (confirmed fraction 0) | `Stranded`, naming B 1.17 GB (C1), A and B 0.9 TB each (C2), A and B 2.7 TB each (C3) |
| C2 confirmed at 18.2%; node D's 1 TB disk marked out after a failure | f = 1 − 3 × 1.8 ÷ 9.0 = 40% > 18.2 + 5: `Stranded`, naming A and B |
| Then `rock-solid pool confirm` | `Stranded` clears; the confirmed fraction is 40% |
| C4, C5 | No `Stranded` (f = 0) |
| A pool whose disks have no capacity left (Σcᵢ = 0) | f = 0, no `Stranded` |
| C1 to C6 with their capped tables, placement proposing no move | No `Unbalanced`: available + held is 0.0 to 0.8% under balanced |
| C4 with a size-weighted table and every PG pinned, placement proposing no move | `Unbalanced` (57% under balanced), naming disk A with its share and target |
| C4 with a size-weighted table while placement still proposes moves, or a PG has no recovered report for its current interval | `Unbalanced` keeps its last value |
| C2 with a 4 TB disk added to D by `rock-solid` and confirmed, the pool 90% held | No `Unbalanced`: available + held is within 1.5% of balanced at any fill |
| C2 holding 0.8 TB | No `CannotReprotect` |
| C2 holding 1.0 TB | `CannotReprotect`, naming node A |
| C5 holding 5.3 TB; C6 holding 1.0 TB | `CannotReprotect`, naming node A in each |
| C1 or C3 holding any data | No `CannotReprotect`. `rock-solid pool status` says losing either node (C1), or any node (C3), leaves its PGs degraded until it returns |
| C4 (`none`) at any fill | No `CannotReprotect`: one copy |
| `rep3` on three nodes of 2 × 2 TB, holding 1.7 TB, then 2.0 TB | None, then `CannotReprotect` naming one disk (reprotectable 1.8 TB) |
| `rep3` on three nodes, one node rebooting | No figure or condition changes: its disks keep their shares at their last fills |
| A PG with a missing member that copies nothing for 60 s on `ctx.Now` | `Stuck`, naming the PG; it clears when the PG copies again or has nothing left to copy |
| A PG stuck or with unfound chunks | `Blocked` names the PG, how many chunks its primary's last peering left unfound, and its candidates, the members down or in `maintenance`, a leaving one too, none if no disk is left to return; a stopped PG, with no active primary to count them, is marked `Stopped`, its count unknown (`TestABlockedPGNamesItsDisks`, `TestBlockedNamesItsCandidates`) |

**Confirmation.** `rock-solid pool create` and disk changes print, per domain, cᵢ, its load at balance min(cᵢ, a·B) and its stranded room. They ask for confirmation when some domain has 2 × stranded room > cᵢ, and record f as the confirmed fraction.

| Input | Expected |
| --- | --- |
| C1 | B strands 1.17 of 1.8 GB (65%): asks; confirmed fraction 48.1% |
| C2 | A and B strand 0.9 of 3.6 TB each (25%): no prompt; confirmed fraction 18.2% |
| C3 | A and B strand 2.7 of 3.6 TB each (75%): asks |
| C6 | A strands 439,453,126 of 878,906,250 blocks, two blocks over half: asks |
| A disk added or removed | The same output and rule; the confirmed fraction becomes the new f |
| A `Pool` created without the CLI | Confirmed fraction 0 until `rock-solid pool confirm` |
| `rock-solid pool status` | Shows f, each domain's stranded room, the confirmed fraction, and the single losses after which the survivors cannot hold a PG's width |
| Any layout that strands space | Placement never refuses it |

**Available, grants and per-node figures**

- C2 with four nodes each holding a 256 MiB grant: available is 2.679 TB less 1 GiB.
- Disks outside the pool's `disk_class`, or holding no member of the pool, have no share and do not set available.
- A `none` pool with `locality: node`, on nodes A, B and C, sized as C4 with A's only disk holding 1.2 TB of another pool: per-node available is A 0.6 TB, B 1.8 TB and C 1.8 TB, each over the node's own PGs.
- Two pools on C2's disks, `rep3` and `none` spread: `rep3` is balanced at 2.700 TB and `none` at 9.900 TB, both computed from the same 9.9 TB of capacity. Their sum is more than that.
- The CLI lists each disk's fill, capacity, room, share and room ÷ share. In C1, it names the 0.7 GB node's disk as the one that sets available.

**Reservations with `overcommit` off** (C2: balanced 2.700 TB, available 2.679 TB). S is the space snapshots hold, 0 until phase 11.

| Steps | Expected |
| --- | --- |
| `CreateVolume` 1 TB, then 1 TB | Both succeed; reservations 2 TB |
| A third `CreateVolume` 1 TB | `RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED` (3 TB > 2.7 TB) |
| `ControllerExpandVolume` of one volume to 1.5 TB | Succeeds; reservations 2.5 TB |
| `CreateVolume` 0.19 TB, bringing reservations to 2.69 TB | Succeeds: within balanced (2.700 TB), though above available (2.679 TB) |
| Then an expand by 0.02 TB (2.71 TB) | `RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED` |
| Reservations of 2.5 TB with 2.0 TB written, then `CreateVolume` 0.1 TB | Succeeds: balanced over capacity is still 2.700 TB (over room it would be 0.70 TB) |
| The same, `CreateVolume` 0.3 TB instead | `RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED` (2.8 TB > 2.7 TB) |
| With S = 0.3 TB (phase 11), reservations of 2.5 TB and an expand by 0.1 TB | `RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED` (2.5 + 0.3 + 0.1 > 2.7) |
| The same steps with `overcommit` on | Succeed: volume sizes may add up to more than the pool holds |

Block volumes in an erasure-coded pool reserve at the copies' overhead. That case is phase 10.

**Several shards per domain (phase 10).** Two shards of a PG never share a disk, so a domain holds at most min(`max_per_domain`, its disks) members of a PG. `ec4-2` at 2 per node:

| Layout | Expected |
| --- | --- |
| Nodes of 2 × 2, 2 × 2 and 1 × 4 TB | Rejected at creation: 2 + 2 + 1 = 5 < 6 members fit |
| Nodes of 2 × 2, 2 × 2, 2 × 2 and 1 × 4 TB | Accepted; balanced 8.64 TB, not the closed form's 9.60 TB |
| C3 | Balanced 1.80 TB either way |
| Node A one 4 TB disk; B, C and D two 1.5 TB disks each | Each domain is checked in turn: losing A leaves 5.4 TB. Losing B, C or D leaves 1 + 2 + 2 < 6 members, a layout fact `pool status` states |

Every PG's first `replicas` members, which hold its copies, sit in distinct domains. [property] On random layouts of 4 to 6 nodes, reprotectable is the least over each domain in turn; the largest domain alone was not the worst in 367 of 3,000 (the study's test E2).

**Property tests.** [property] For random layouts of 3 to 10 nodes with 1 to 4 disks of 0.5 to 4 TB, some disks holding other pools' data, random valid tables of 1 to 3 copies and random amounts held, laid out as the table sends data (`TestPoolFiguresHoldTheirBounds`: 20,000 seeds per commit rather than thousands, since they take about a second; 300,000 passed once in 3 s on 2 processes):

- available + held ≤ balanced ≤ Σcᵢ ÷ b, exactly in whole blocks;
- available + held stays within a block of the empty pool's available as the pool fills;
- balanced is the largest whole number of blocks D with Σᵢ min(cᵢ, a·D) ≥ b·D;
- the domains' stranded rooms sum to Σcᵢ − b·B, to within b blocks;
- f, balanced and reprotectable do not change with the amount held;
- for copies, balanced without the largest-capacity domain equals the least over single domains, and is at most balanced after any single disk loss;
- `CannotReprotect` never fires on a one-copy pool, nor for a loss whose survivors cannot hold the width.

"Available + held within the margin of balanced once converged" and "fills reach available within 1%" belong to Placement computation and to Placement faults and invariants. Pools only computes the figures from a given table and given fills.

## Placement computation

A pure function in the sans-IO core, `Next` in `internal/chunkstore`: the previous table plus
its inputs (the pools with their disks' marks, fills and drains, the primaries' asks, activation
and recovered reports, operators' edits and how many balance moves the table may make) gives the next table, with
a deterministic order of moves: no `range` over a map, and a tie between equally placed disks goes
to the lowest disk ID, then the lowest PG number.

**Which PGs get a new interval.** Each row is one placement table, and each raises the table epoch
by 1 (`TestIntervalsRaisedByTableChanges`, on 4 nodes of 3 disks with 2,048 `rep3` PGs unless the
row says otherwise).

| Table change | PGs whose interval goes up by 1 |
| --- | --- |
| Pool B created | None in other pools; B's PGs start at interval 1 |
| Disk added, before balance moves anything | None |
| Balance moves one member of PG 7: the new member added, the old one marked leaving | PG 7 only; the other 2,047 keep theirs |
| A recovered report for PG 7's interval before the add, then for the add's, its current one | None, then PG 7, whose leaving member is removed |
| Disk D, one of a node's 3, marked down | Only the PGs with a member on D |
| Node marked down | Every PG with a member on the node: all 2,048 on 3 nodes; 615 of 2,048 on 10 nodes of 3 disks (PG epochs spike F1) |
| Node marked up again | The same PGs again |
| `maintenance <node>` set, then cleared | Every PG with a member on the node, at each change (a live mark) |
| PG 7's members reordered (same set, new primary) | PG 7 |
| Pool's `replicas` 2 → 3 | Every PG of that pool |
| Pool's `min_live` changed | Every PG of that pool |
| Pool's `write_limit` changed | None |
| Activation report folded in (last activated interval set, past members trimmed) | None |
| `pg_count` doubled | Every PG p of the pool becomes 2p and 2p + 1, each one interval above p: PG 5 at 9 gives PGs 10 and 11 at 10 |
| PG 7's primary asks because a counter ran out | PG 7 only |
| Node N restarts and asks | Exactly the PGs whose primary is on N |
| Member C removed (table e + 1), then added back (e + 2) | +2 over the two tables, though the member list equals table e's |
| Down mark and refill in one table (a lost log) | +1; in two tables, +2 |
| A member down for `refill_after`, then refilled | +1 at the down mark, +1 at the refill, 10 minutes later |

- A change to the session table or the format level is no input of the computation: it makes no
  placement table and leaves the table epoch alone.
- A delta's changed entries are exactly the PGs whose member list, order, live marks, interval, last
  activated interval or past members changed. Every other entry is byte for byte the previous
  table's.
- A move starts two intervals of its PG, one when it adds the new member and marks the old one
  leaving, one when it removes the leaving member, as the epoch change model's `Add` and `Remove`
  do. So does the refill of a member merely down; the refill of a member whose disk left the pool
  starts one, as `Replace` does, and so does a table of several such changes, as `Refill` does.
- Pinning a PG without changing its members starts no interval.

**Which members are missing.** `refill_after` 10 minutes, `degraded_refill_after` 1 minute; a `rep3` pool on 4 nodes unless stated (`TestMissingMembers` and the tests named in the rows).

| State of member M | Refilled |
| --- | --- |
| Down for 9 minutes 59 s | No; its PGs write to their two live members |
| Down for 10 minutes | Yes, in the next table |
| Down 5 minutes, up, down again 5 minutes | No: the count restarts at each down mark |
| Down, and its disk then reports a new log ID | At once |
| Down, and an operator declares its disk lost | At once |
| Down for 59 s in a `rep2` PG with `min_live` 2 | No; the PG serves no reads or writes meanwhile |
| Down for 1 minute in a `rep2` PG with `min_live` 2 | Yes, in the next table, since the PG serves no reads or writes while it waits |
| Down 5 s (a network hiccup), then up, in a `rep2` PG with `min_live` 2 | No member moves; the PG resyncs the member and serves reads and writes again (`TestHiccupMovesNoMember`) |
| Down for 1 minute in a `rep2` PG with `min_live` 1, both members down, and the only member live in an interval since the last activated one | No; peering waits for it whether or not a new member joins. The other member, down longer, is refilled (`TestAwaitedMemberStays`) |
| A refill member, still recovering, in a `rep2` PG whose other member is live | Counts toward `min_live` from the table that adds it, marked up: the PG serves reads and writes once that interval activates, each acknowledged on both members, while recovery copies the older chunks on its missing list (`TestRefillMemberCountsAtOnce`) |
| In `maintenance` for an hour | No; it counts toward `min_live` throughout |
| A leaving member, down for 10 minutes | No, nor dropped: it stays until a recovered report for the current interval removes it, since its replacement holds no copy until then; on `rep1` it may hold the only one. Once its disk leaves the pool it is dropped, not refilled (`TestMovesAddThenRemove`) |
| Down on a 3-node `rep3` cluster for an hour | No eligible disk on another node; a disk failure on a node with a second disk refills there after 10 minutes (`TestRefillWithNoEligibleDisk`) |

**Placement rules**

- Refill puts every missing member on the eligible disk furthest below its target
  (`TestRefillFillsTheDiskFurthestBelow`). Balance then runs: while any disk is outside its fill
  margin, move one member from the disk furthest above its target by its fill now, even one inside
  its own margin, to the eligible disk furthest below by its fill after one more member, if that
  leaves it no higher than the source
  (`TestBalanceTakesFromTheFurthestAbove`: loads of 44, 44 and 40 against targets of 42.7 take one
  move, from the first 44, to 43, 44 and 41). When no such move is left, a move that brings a disk
  outside its margin nearer and takes neither disk outside its margin on the other side; stop when
  neither exists. The property test's seed 207 needed the second kind, and is a regression test
  (`TestPlacementSeed207`): every PG on the disks above their targets already had a member on the
  node of the disk below its margin.
- Lowering `replicas` marks the member it would drop, the PG's last down member or else its last,
  leaving, and the recovered report removes it; only a member refill would replace anyway is
  deleted at once, and a PG with a leaving member keeps any further surplus until that removal
  (`TestLoweringReplicasKeepsLiveMembers`). All up, `rep3` to `rep2`, marks C leaving; A and C
  down, `rep3` to `rep1`, marks C and keeps A; C's disk gone deletes C. With only B holding every
  chunk and A and C refill members still recovering, `rep3` to `rep1` takes two recovered reports
  and never leaves B's chunks without a member, with every member up or with A, B or C down for
  three tables.
- A disk's fill margin is max(5% of its target, 1 member). A 0.5 TB disk beside 8 TB disks, with a
  target of 10 to 20 members, has a margin of 1 member.
- Both steps keep the failure-domain rule. With `failure_domain: node`, no PG ever has two members
  on one node, and no domain holds more than `max_per_domain` of a PG's width.
- A disk's target is its capacity for the pool: `write_limit` less other pools' data on it, so this
  pool's own data counts, water-filled over domains capped at `max_per_domain` of the width, and
  split within a domain by capacity (`TestTargetsFollowCapacity`). The capacity figures list the
  same targets, counting a disk added with no member yet and giving a draining disk none
  (`TestFiguresListPlacementTargets`).
- An operator's edit that names more disks than the width, a disk twice or two disks on one node
  under `rep3` is ignored, pin and all; one that swaps a member for a disk on a node the PG lacks
  is applied (`TestEditsKeepTheRules`).
- A move adds the new member and marks the old one leaving; the first table after a recovered
  report for the PG's current interval removes it, and removals count no move, so every
  recovered PG's removal shares one table (`TestMovesAddThenRemove`). A PG makes one move at a time,
  and starts one only once its entry records a recovered report for its current interval, its
  members unchanged since: on 4 nodes of `rep2`, after a node's disk leaves the pool, a disk added
  to it draws moves only from PGs the refill left alone, not from those whose refill members are
  still recovering. The table that removes the leaving members moves nothing from their PGs, so
  settling takes one table more, which starts no interval. So a resync comes before any rebalance
  move of its PG: a node back from `maintenance` with `rep2` PGs that took writes on one copy draws
  no move from them until their recovery has copied what it missed and the interval is reported
  recovered.
  Balance counts the leaving member as gone and the failure-domain rule ignores it: on 3 nodes of
  `rep3`, a disk added to node A takes members from A's other disk. A missing member of a moving PG
  is replaced by the leaving member, which becomes an ordinary member, when its domain allows and
  its disk is up and not draining; a down or draining one stays leaving and a new disk takes the
  missing member's place.
  A report for an interval before the current one removes nothing: on 3 nodes of 2 disks, a move
  within node A, then a refill onto another disk of node C, or C's member down and back up, or in
  `maintenance` and back up, and then a late report for the add's interval keep the leaving member,
  which a report for the current interval removes. On `rep1` the leaving member may hold the only
  copy: of the writes taken while the other member was down, which a late report from before would
  remove with it, as the property test's late reports check; and of everything, when a report for
  the current interval comes in the table that marks the new member down or in `maintenance`, which
  keeps the leaving member. Activation and recovered reports in the table that doubles `pg_count`
  change no PG.
- Balance never moves a member of a pinned PG, and refill still replaces one on a lost disk. A
  draining disk keeps its members up while balance moves them all off, and holds none, a leaving
  one included, once the moves' recovered reports are in, which is when its drain finishes
  (`TestPinAndDrain`), except
  a pinned PG's, which keeps the drain from finishing until an operator edits or unpins that PG.
- Targets by capacity: after a disk is added to a pool holding data, the second computation, run
  once the first one's moves have copied, proposes no move, and the third, once the removals have
  recovered, starts no interval (`TestMovesAfterADiskAdded`; the
  counts by room are the capacity conditions study's).

  | Layout | Moves, over computations |
  | --- | --- |
  | `none`, one 2 TB node holding 1 TB, a 2 TB node added | 61, over 3 (124 over 4 with targets by room) |
  | C6 holding 0.8 TB, a 2 TB disk added to node B | 62, over 3 (98 over 3) |
  | C2 holding 1.5 TB, a 4 TB disk added to node D | 98, over 3 (153 over 5) |

**Convergence on the capacity model layouts.** C1 to C6 are the data-driven cases of the "Pools"
item, which holds their capacity figures ([capacity model
spike](../spikes/capacity-model/README.md)). Here they check only placement
(`TestConvergenceOnCapacityLayouts`):

- With capped targets, the loop converges on all six, and the table's available figure comes
  within 1% of balanced.
- With size-proportional targets on C1, C2, C3 and C6, the loop never reaches its margin (worst disk
  93, 23, 200 and 50% off). It still terminates, because it stops when no move helps.
- In C4 (three 2 TB disks, one holding 1.2 TB of another pool), targets by capacity are what keep
  the table near the 4.2 TB bound.

**Table size and deltas**

| Table | Size |
| --- | --- |
| 2,048 `rep3` PGs, each 3 × (4-byte disk ID + mark byte) + 11 bytes of intervals, flags and counts | 52 KiB (53,278 bytes) |
| 4,096 PGs × 18 members, `ec16-2` | About 404 KiB (413,726 bytes) |

Past intervals' member lists and, a PG's leaving members come on top of
these sizes; both are usually absent (`TestTableSize`).

- A delta holds the changed PG entries and the CRC32C of the resulting table. Applied to the
  previous table, it reproduces the whole table and its CRC byte for byte.
- A delta applied to the wrong base fails, and the node fetches the whole table: another table at
