- A recovery write that fails, even before the store logged any of it, ends the interval, whose
  successor recovers the chunk (`TestARecoveryWriteThatFailsEndsItsInterval`). An index rebuild
  ends the recoveries under way: a source's reply arriving after it is dropped
  (`TestARebuildEndsTheRecoveriesUnderWay`).
- A recovery read gives the chunk's live image: the written blocks' bytes after the map, and every
  other block, punched or never written, a hole (`TestARecoveryReadIsTheChunksLiveImage`). The
  map's decoder refuses a block both written and punched, bytes past the map in its first block
  and a length other than its written blocks (`TestBlockMapErrors`, fuzzed by
  `FuzzDecodeBlockMap`).
- Recovery leaves out a block that a whole-block write ordered before it covers. Kept 1.1 is on
  disk 2 only, the primary, which disks 1 and 3 rejoin; it takes a whole-block write to block 0,
  then orders the recovery of the chunk from its own copy: the recovery write carries block 1 alone,
  and the byte-range oracle shows the new write in block 0. The blocks are chosen when the recovery
  write is ordered: with the whole-block write ordered between recovery's read and its write, the
  recovery write still leaves block 0 out. So it does with the read from another member: with 1.1 on
  disks 2 and 1 and the primary's own read failing, it recovers disk 3 from disk 1, the write ordered
  between that read and the recovery write; a clean primary reads another member only after its own
  read failed or its image proved rotten. A planted variant that chooses them at the read (the epoch change model's
  `neg-recovery-covers-at-read`) copies 1.1's block 0 over the acknowledged write
  (`TestRecoveryLeavesOutTheBlocksTheIntervalsWritesCover`).
- A recovery goes with the version it was logged under. Disk 1, down while X was written, lists it
  in interval 2 and logs W1 to block 0; W2, to block 0 too, reaches disk 1 but not disk 3, and the
  recovery after it copies block 1 under W2. Disk 1 restarts and leads interval 3, whose peering
  keeps W1 and drops W2: disk 1 takes no image of the chunk, recovers it from disk 3 and serves
  X's block 1; with the image, as `imageOverDroppedRecovery` takes it, it serves zeros
  (`TestARecoveryDroppedWithItsVersionLeavesTheCopyLacking`, the epoch change model's
  `neg-image-over-dropped-recovery`).
- A primary that lacks a chunk's kept version orders a punch of it although its own store holds
  nothing of the chunk, rather than answering it done unsent; a punch of a chunk absent everywhere
  still logs nothing (`TestAPrimaryOrdersAPunchOfAChunkItHoldsNothingOf`).
- Recovery cut short by the next interval: the missing lists survive. Interval 4's peering raises
  disk 3's entry to its decision, and interval 4's recovery brings the kept version
  (`TestRecoveryCutShortByTheNextIntervalLeavesTheListsInPlace`).
- Only recovery removes an entry. Disk 2 holds dropped 1.2, which wrote block 1, and lists 1.1;
  2.1, writing block 2, lands on disk 2 before recovery reaches it, disk 3, which lists nothing,
  leading interval 2. The next peering keeps 2.1,
  whose newest copy disk 2 holds, and raises its entry to 2.1 rather than clearing it; recovery then
  brings it block 1 of 1.1's history (`TestOnlyRecoveryRemovesAMissingListEntry`).
- A partial-block write to a chunk the primary lacks waits for its recovery
  (`TestAPartialWriteWaitsForTheKeptVersion`, `TestAPartialWriteWaitsWhileThePrimaryListsTheChunk`);
  the primary holds at most 64 client writes and refuses the next
  (`TestHeldPartialWritesAreBounded`). One to a chunk the last peering found unfound is answered
  unfound at once (`TestAPartialWriteToAnUnfoundChunkIsAnsweredUnfound`).
- Warm recovery allocates nothing: a fourth round of recovering 6 chunks makes no heap allocation
  (`TestRecoveryAllocatesNothing`).
- A member never serves a chunk while it is on its own missing list, and never returns an older
  version instead.
- Open: whether a primary whose own list holds the chunk waits for recovery, forwards the read, or
  returns an error.
- Recovery writes pass `write_limit`: with disk 3 at 91% under a 90% limit, a client write adding
  data is refused while recovery still copies disk 3 what it missed
  (`TestRecoveryWritesPassWriteLimit`).
- The replica primary's seeded fault run, 20 seeds a commit and 1,000 in `scripts/seeds.sh`, also
  crashes the primary, rebuilds its index and moves it, at most one disk lost: every disk that
  answers for a version with its chunk whole at it and listed nowhere maps the same bytes ("no two
  members hold different data under one version"), and once recovery settles every member lists
  nothing and maps the kept writes but in an unfound chunk ("once recovery settles, every member
  lists nothing and maps the kept writes, but in an unfound chunk"), both registered with
  `sim.Invariants` (`TestReplicatedWritesSurviveFaults`). The planted `neg-recovery-covers-at-read`
  variant breaks the first, checked alone, at 12 of the first 300 seeds on the real control-plane
  group, seed 24 first (`TestPlantedRecoveryBugBreaksTheFaultRun`).
- Open: two faults that overlap before recovery finishes leave a chunk unfound although a member
  listed by the earlier interval holds its kept image (open question "Recovery sources across
  overlapping faults"). The fault run tolerates the same at its end in a chunk whose every recovery
  source failed a read on rotted bits: rot on the only clean copy beside divergent members is a
  second fault, so the chunk is unfound and its held writes are answered unfound
  (`TestARottedLastSourceLeavesTheChunkUnfound`).
- Losses beyond what the pool survives, for example both members of `rep2` PG 4:
  - One after the other, with an interval activated between: the PG serves, the lost chunks read
    unfound, never wrong data or zeros, and it is reported, naming the disks until they are declared
    lost (`TestRep2ServesPastTwoFailures`, `TestAChunkOnlyLostDisksHeldStaysUnfound`).
  - Together: the PG is down, and refuses reads and writes, whether or not the disks are declared
    lost, until an operator gives up what the last activated interval held
    (`TestTwoDisksLostTogetherStayStopped`; [A disk is its log](design.md#epoch-changes-and-failure-detection)).
- Open: how an empty refilled member is filled. The design says only that a PG is one key range of
  the chunk index; a scan of `(pool, h)` over that range would fit.

## Simulated network

`internal/sim`, run in one goroutine from one seeded source. A seed replays the run exactly: two
runs of one seed give byte-identical traces, compared with `cmp`.

**Message faults**

Each loop pair has one connection, which delivers each direction in order, as TCP does.

| Fault | What a test checks |
| --- | --- |
| Drop with probability p | The message is lost and its connection breaks; the sender's deadline on `ctx.Now` fires; nothing hangs |
| Delay up to D | Delivery after the delay, in seeded order |
| Round-trip jitter, seeded per message | Round trips vary message by message within the delay's bounds, as the rate bound's shortest-round-trip choice in each third needs |
| Asymmetric queueing up to 50 ms on grants | One direction only |
| Reorder | Two messages on different connections arrive swapped; one connection never reorders |
| Duplicate | The copy arrives right behind its original; a duplicated replica write of one value with identical data changes nothing (the toy protocol's replicas) |
| Partition, symmetric or one-way | Messages across it are lost. A partitioned connection fails after a seeded delay, or never, and both are run. On failure every request outstanding on it fails with one `PeerLost` |
| Node crash and restart | Every connection of the node gives its peers a `PeerLost`, after what the node had sent unless it rebooted, and before anything it sends once restarted; unflushed disk state follows the simulated disk |

The primary recognizes a resent client write by its identity in its
[resend table](design.md#data-layer-chunkstore), which the
[Consistency check of chunk histories](#consistency-check-of-chunk-histories) depends on.

**Driver contract** (Modularity), shared with the phase 5 network suite

- A reply is delivered only after its send's buffer has been released.
- A peer's `PeerLost` comes after every buffer of that peer has been released.
- A request that timed out keeps its buffer until the reply or `PeerLost`.
- A `Reply`'s buffer is freed by the network once the reply is delivered or lost, and a machine
  that frees a send's buffer while the network still holds it is reported.

**Clocks per node**

| Clock fault | Model |
| --- | --- |
| Oscillator drift | Raw rate within ±4% of real time, fixed per node per seed |
| Raw rate step after measurement | A node's raw rate rises or falls once per boot, by up to `lease_drift / 2`, at a seeded step once its clocks have run `rate_window`, so its holders have bounded it |
| Reboot | The node is down for at least a heartbeat; its raw clock restarts near 0 at a rate changed by up to 2%. A process restart keeps the raw clock and its rate |
| Time-daemon slew | `BOOTTIME` rate differs from raw by up to ±22.6%, changing at seeded steps; chrony's 8.33% as a case of its own |
| Suspend | Raw and `MONOTONIC` stop; `BOOTTIME` gains the sleep rounded down to whole seconds; one `Resumed` when that gain reaches the threshold |
| Stop or pause in place, `tsc` guest or Firecracker | Every clock gains the pause; marker unchanged |
| Stop in place, QEMU kvm-clock guest | Every clock frozen; marker unchanged |
| Restore or live migration, any hypervisor or clocksource | Every clock frozen; marker changed |
| QEMU migration held at switchover | kvmclock counts the hold, the TSC does not; marker changed (VM pause spike T4b) |
| Messages to a paused node | Queued, then delivered on resume ahead of its clients' requests and any message sent later; or lost until it resumes, on reconnected and new connections too, each loss breaking its connection |

- The simulated driver delivers `Resumed` when `core.Resumed` reports it from the model's readings,
  the loop's own rule: a suspend whose `BOOTTIME − MONOTONIC` gain reaches the threshold, or a marker
  change, and at no other time. A suspend the kernel rounded below the threshold gives none.
- The clock model can be imported alone, by `internal/loop/looptest`, which scripts the event
  loop's clocks from it.
- No message carries simulator time: a node sees only its own clocks.
- **[property]** Under every message and clock fault at once, a machine that keeps the driver
  contract never trips the network's buffer check, every buffer is freed once the run settles,
  each `Resumed` comes in a loop's first pass after a pause that calls for it and no other, and the
  seed replays to a byte-identical trace.

## Placement faults and invariants

The faults are the placement faults of [Testing strategy](design.md#testing-strategy) and every
fault in the [Epoch change model](#epoch-change-model)'s list. Seeded runs land them at random and
check the invariants below, each registered with `sim.Invariants`; the scripted scenarios at the end
land the ones a run does not combine. A failing seed prints its replay command and becomes a
scripted test before the fix ([Seed runner in CI](#seed-runner-in-ci)). Lease constants are as at
the head of [Peering and read leases](#peering-and-read-leases).

**Seeded runs**, with their seeds in `scripts/seeds.sh`:

- The replica primary's fault run (`TestReplicatedWritesSurviveFaults`, 1,000), under [Replica
  primary](#replica-primary), on the real control-plane group, and the primary-change run
  (`TestPeeringKeepsAcknowledgedWritesAcrossPrimaries`, 500), under [Peering and read
  leases](#peering-and-read-leases). Both register the epoch checks below, as the read run does.
  The primary-change run's authority knows 4 disks from the start and allows moves: it drains a
  disk or ends a drain, makes no operator edit while a move is in flight, and hands `Next` every
  recovered report again on each table, as late or repeated reports reach a real leader. Once its
  PG activates at the end, it gives recovery up to 30 s to copy every chunk to every member,
  those a drain moved included.
- The read run (`TestNoPGServesReadsFromTwoPrimaries`, 500): 3 disks and 4 PGs on the real
  control-plane group, whose leader's detector marks them, on drifting, slewed clocks and jittered
  delivery. One fault at a time lands on a disk
  node every 0.5 to 3 s for 30 s, then 10 s pass quietly: a cut from every node but the client, and
  in half the cuts from the client too, for 0.5 to 6 s, in which the node gets no table; a suspend,
  a counted VM pause, a restore from a snapshot or a held migration, for 0.5 to 6 s, its messages
  queued or lost; a reboot; or a 0.2 to 2 s delay on one path. A node back from a cut gets the
  newest table once its disk is marked up, or after 3 s, and in half the seeds that table makes
  it lead every PG it is a member of. A client incarnation writes whole and partial blocks to 2
  chunks of each PG and dies at 4 to 12 s; its successor says hello to every disk node, reissues
  the unanswered writes and writes on. Each incarnation keeps up to 6 writes with no final answer,
  sends a refused one again after 100 ms and an unanswered one after 2 s under its request ID, and
  names in every write the lowest ID it holds no final answer to, so the read run carries the
  seeded coverage of the [resend table](design.md#data-layer-chunkstore); the fault run's writer
  sends each write once, as its check of one reply per request ID needs. No seeded run splits a
  PG, so the trim's watermark at every PG count is checked by
  `TestASplitHalfsTrimKeepsItsSiblingsWritesStale` alone. Reads of a chunk's first 4 blocks go to a random PG at a
  random node every 5 to 25 ms, tagged with one of the last 4 tables or, half the time, with the
  node's own, as a client cut off with it would; about 300 are served by primaries a seed. A VM stop with every clock frozen is left out (open
  question "Stops in place on QEMU guests that run on kvm-clock"). Invariant 1 is judged on the
  replicas' own state, after every step and as each read arrives, by the condition `read` itself
  serves on: a read's reply can come a store read after its lease check, and any member answers a
  read of a frozen version. A read's version is judged on the replies: one answered OK leaves with
  a version a primary already acknowledged to a write, or one a later activated interval kept, and
  at the run's end no interval activated after it keeps less of its chunk.
- The write-limit run (`TestWritesPassTheWriteLimitOnlyWhereAdmitted`, 200): 3 disks and 4 PGs on
  all three on the real control-plane group, every disk's `write_limit` 300 blocks above its fill at the start. A
  client writes 16 chunks of 64 blocks, 8 at a time: a punch 1 write in 10, an overwrite of an
  acknowledged block 3 in 10, a granted new block 1 in 10, else a new block, while one fault at a
  time reboots a disk node or delays a path for 0.2 to 1 s. A write the primary orders while it
  holds a member at its limit, neither granted nor an overwrite, must never become a version a disk
  past its limit maps. Correct runs pass the limits through granted writes and fills reported late,
  by at most 85 blocks over the first 100 seeds; no disk may pass its limit by more than the 300
  blocks of room it had below it, a bound on the disks' own live blocks that holds whatever fills
  the primaries held and however the stores classed overwrites. Held fills are compared with the
  limit without grants, which arrive with phase 4. A run of its own, not the read run: capacity
  needs punches, overwrites and grants the read run's writers do not send.
- The lease pair run (`TestNoLeaseOutlastsItsGrant` in `internal/lease`, 10,000): one holder and one
  grantor with heartbeats, clock rates and slews drawn per seed, and in 3 seeds of 4 cuts (some
  right after a grant), a grantor VM stop, a grantor reboot of 1 to 3 s, one raw-rate rise of 0.4%,
  a holder suspend and a holder stop in place. The holder's lease is valid only while the grantor
  keeps the grant, or reboots or waits out a restart that began while the grant ran, judged during a
  grantor VM stop at its frozen raw clock. A quarter of the seeds are quiet: no step check may trip,
  and in a quarter of those, on 1 ms round trips, the holder must hold a lease `rate_gap` plus two
  round trips after the grantor first granted its request, `rate_gap` counted on a holder raw clock
  up to 4% slow and the run's steps of up to 10 ms allowed three times over: 138 ms against a 100 ms
  `rate_gap`. The lease clock counterexamples are planted here rather than in a cluster run: the run
  reaches every clock trace, 500 seeds in 0.3 s.
- The cloned-disk run (`TestAClonedDiskIsRefused`, 30) on the real control-plane group, under
  [Control-plane placement faults](#control-plane-placement-faults).
- The placement run (`TestPlacementKeepsItsRules`, 1,000) under [Placement
  computation](#placement-computation) checks each pool's figures after every table whose member
  slots on the pool's disks sum to `pg_count` × width, by the rules of
  `TestPoolFiguresHoldTheirBounds`: the figure bounds, and against the worst single loss the
  `CannotReprotect` rules and reprotectable the least balanced over any one domain's loss and no
  more than balanced after any one disk's. A table that keeps a removed disk's members, with no
  eligible disk to refill, names fewer disks than its placement needs, and the figures are claims
  about full placements: about one table in ten is such a table, and the run logs how many it
  skipped.

Too few copies return an error, never wrong data: a chunk peering found unfound is answered
unfound, reads and partial writes alike (under [Peering and read leases](#peering-and-read-leases)
and [Recovery per PG](#recovery-per-pg)), and the fault and primary-change runs' ends tolerate no
other chunk listed, but in the fault run one whose every recovery source holds rotted bits; a member
of such a chunk is left out of the byte check too.

Uniformly hashed fills reach the reported available figure within 1% (`TestUniformFillsReachAvailable`):
C1 to C6, laid out by `Next`, take about 200,000 writes of uniformly hashed chunks, each landing a
unit ÷ k on every member, and the first refusal comes at 99.40 to 100.01% of available. It runs on
the pools and placement alone: the figure is a claim about the table, and a replica run at TB sizes
is out of reach.

property 2, which [MetaStore invariants](#metastore-invariants) plants, is a variant of the code
(for the reboot that takes no time and for peer messages handled after reads, of the simulated
reboot and loop) that fails the invariant its property maps to. A planted run checks that
invariant alone, and the test runs a failing seed of the first 500; the fault and read runs, on
the real control-plane group, take theirs from the first 300 and 200. A counterexample whose trace
needs several faults coordinated, which the seeded runs land one at a time, is a scripted trace in
`TestPlantedBugsBreakTheirTraces` instead, or for a lease rule in `internal/lease`'s own: run every
commit, it must pass unplanted and break its invariant planted.

The lease pair run's plants, seeds of 500 failing and the first. No margin for a suspend that
delivers no `Resumed` (`Config.Resume` 0) 2 (28). The 1 s of that margin covers the errors of most other plants, so
these plant it away too, and the run then draws no such suspend: the holder ending on its slower
clock 68 (6), the grantor on its faster 96 (8), a lease before the first bound 1 (21), that with the
step check at `1 + lease_drift / 2` 14 (6), widening only past `1 + 2 lease_drift` 20 (9), the
margin `max(lease_drift, 1 − 1/B)` 3 of 5,000 (1,056: it needs a rate rise after the bound and a
partition after a grant), no end of leases on `Resumed` 7 (31). With the margin: no new window at a
new run ID 9 (6), no step check 52 (1), one on grants only 53 (1), no restart wait 56 (2); for
property 10, the step check at `1 + lease_drift / 2` 25 (3) and against a grant that gave no lease 3 (265).

The read run also plants a primary that commits a version once its own log holds it, before its
members do: a read returns a version the next interval drops at 128 of the first 200 seeds, seed 0 first
(`TestPlantedReadBugsBreakTheReadRun`). It is no row of the model's table; it shows the read
version check firing.

The primary-change run also plants a primary that recovers only its own copies: its members, those
a drain refilled among them, never reach the copy count, at 462 seeds of 500, seed 0 first.

The write-limit run's planted bug, a primary ordering a plain write that adds live data past a
member's limit, fails each of the run's two invariants, checked alone, at all of the first 100
seeds, seed 0 first (`TestPlantedLimitBugBreaksTheLimitRun`): its disks pass the 300 blocks of room.

The grant-room run's planted bugs each break its invariant at seed 0 (`TestPlantedGrantRoomBugsBreakTheRefillRun`): a primary copying into the grants' room (the fix reverted) and the disks reporting a log reserve of 0 hold granted flushes, at each of seeds 0 to 19, and a primary admitting a plain write on its members' fill alone, its pool's grants left out, passes `write_limit`.

| P10b | As P10, from the start, a partition right after the first grant | No lease before the second grant, `rate_gap` later; no overlap | `TestTheFirstGrantOfAWindowGivesNoLease`, `TestNoLeaseOutlastsItsGrant` |
| P11 | A first-third grant with a 50 ms round trip | The bound, and the margin with it, widens only toward safety; one slow grant beside a fast one in the same third changes nothing | `TestRateBound` "slow first third", "one slow grant in the first third" |
| P12 | Holder suspended: `BOOTTIME` gains, raw and `MONOTONIC` gain 0 | One `Resumed`; it ends every lease the primary holds, so its next read is refused, and it reads again about `rate_gap` later once its grantors renew. A grantor holding a newer table renews the holder only once the holder reports that table | `TestASuspendGivesOneResumedOnceItsGainReachesTheThreshold`, `TestTheRestartWaitAndResumedStopReads`, `TestResumed`, `TestAPrimaryReadsOnlyWithALeaseFromEveryUpMember`; the read run's suspends |
| P12b | Holder suspended for less than a second; the kernel rounds the sleep to 0 s, below the `Resumed` threshold | No `Resumed`; no read overlaps a new primary's | `TestASuspendGivesOneResumedOnceItsGainReachesTheThreshold`; the read run's suspends of 0.5 s and more |
| P13 | Holder VM stopped 10 s, clocks frozen, messages queued, marker unchanged | The step check ends the leases before any read | `TestHeartbeatsQueuedBehindAFrozenPauseEndTheLeasesBeforeAReadBehindThem`, `TestTheStepCheck` |
| P14 | Holder VM restored from a snapshot, messages lost, marker changed | `Resumed` ends the leases | `TestEachVMPauseMovesTheClocksAndMarkerAsMeasured`, `TestResumed`; the read run's restores |
| P15 | P13 with messages lost | Open: up to a heartbeat of stale reads (open question); tolerated or excluded | None |
| P16 | A member of the last activated interval crashes while a later interval peers | Peering waits for it, or reaches another member of that interval; no acknowledged version is lost | `TestPeeringJudgesAPastIntervalByItsOwnMinLive`, `TestPeeringStopsEveryIntervalSinceTheLastActivated`; the fault run's member crashes while its PG peers |
| P17 | B restarts shortly after granting A a lease | B joins no peering until both its clocks show one lease; A's reads stop at A's own end of B's grant | `TestTheRestartWait`, `TestARestartedMemberJoinsNoPeeringDuringItsWait`, `TestTheRestartWaitAndResumedStopReads` |
| P18 | Partial-block writes from two clients, pipelined, with a primary change while a base read is in flight | The byte oracle holds; a write waiting for its base when its interval ends is refused and never ordered | `TestAWriteWaitingWhenItsIntervalEndsIsRefused`; M6 in `TestPeeringKeepsAcknowledgedWritesAcrossPrimaries`, M1 and M9 in `TestSubBlockWritesMatchTheByteOracle` |
| P19 | A merge's base block fails its checksum on the primary's disk | The base is fetched from another member; the oracle holds and no rotten byte reaches a new version | `TestARottenBaseIsFetchedFromAnotherMember`, `TestTwoRottenEdgeBlocksAreBothFetched`, `TestABaseIsAskedOfTheNextMemberWhenOneIsLost` |
| P20 | Every disk of a pool a few hundred blocks under `write_limit`; new blocks, overwrites, punches, member reboots and delays; and, on the real control plane, a space grant out while a lost disk's PGs refill onto disks near the limit ([Control-plane placement faults](#control-plane-placement-faults)) | Writes adding data are refused with `NoSpace`; overwrites, punches and recovery pass; no disk passes the limit by any other path. The refill stops where a target would keep less than its log reserve plus (1 + k) × the grants outstanding, the pool goes `Stuck`, and every flush the grant covers lands | `TestWritesPassTheWriteLimitOnlyWhereAdmitted`, `TestWriteLimitAdmission`, `TestRecoveryWritesPassWriteLimit`, `TestARefillLeavesTheRoomOfTheGrantsOut`, `TestARefillLeavesTheGrantsTheirRoomOnTheRealGroup` |
| P21 | Capacity layouts C1 to C6 filled with uniformly hashed chunks | The first refusal comes within 1% of the reported available figure | `TestUniformFillsReachAvailable` |
| P22 | `rep3`, `min_live` 2, two members cut off with writes in flight | No write is acknowledged on the one copy left; every write sent then is refused, the last once a member returns; the next is acknowledged on two copies at least | `TestWritesWaitForMinLiveAfterTwoMembersGoDown`, `TestAPrimaryBelowMinLiveServesNoReads` |
| P23 | `rep3` on 3 nodes of one disk; a disk fails and its refill finds no eligible disk | Its PGs raise `Stuck` after 60 s of copying nothing, never `CannotReprotect`; a PG clears it once it copies again or has nothing left to copy. On the real control plane, a refill stopped at a disk's log reserve raises it from the leader's record of when the PG last copied, and an added disk clears it with no edit: placement parks the full member beside a member on the new disk, which copies ([Control-plane placement faults](#control-plane-placement-faults)) | `TestRefillWithNoEligibleDisk`, `TestStuck`, `TestARefillStoppedAtALogReserveGoesStuck` |
| P24 | A node reboots, its disks down for less than `refill_after` | No capacity figure or pool condition changes: its disks keep their shares at their last reported fills | `TestRebootChangesNoFigure`, `TestHiccupMovesNoMember` |

The read run cuts a disk off and its detector marks it down after `node_down_after` (5 s), when every
grant to it has already ended, so P1 (b), a grantor's wait for its grant to end, is the scripted
test's alone.

## Consistency check of chunk histories

- **Recording.** The replica runs record every client write, punch and read in the phase 1 history
  recorder (`chunkHist` in `internal/chunkstore`): a client actor's requests as it sends them, and
  the replies a replica sends the client, the decoder getting the sender's bytes of a read's
  buffer, which it records as their FNV-1a hash. Each run checks every chunk's history at its end,
  as the invariant "every chunk's history of client writes, punches and reads is linearizable": the
  fault run (`TestReplicatedWritesSurviveFaults`), the primary-change run, the read run, the
  write-limit run and the sub-block seeds. The runs with no reads of their own read each chunk back
  once they settle, the primary-change run once with each up member primary in turn, so a member
  holding other bytes than the primary shows once it leads. A read back the primary refuses is sent
  again every 200 ms, up to 20 times. One answered unfound is left unchecked, the open question on
  [recovery sources across overlapping faults](design.md#roadmap-and-open-questions): 353 of 3,032
  over 500 primary-change seeds, 228 of 2,000 over 1,000 fault seeds. One never answered OK or
  unfound fails the run, except in the fault run on a primary whose disk the run rotted, which
  refuses a block whose checksum fails: 66 of the 2,000.
- **The model** is per chunk: a 4 MiB byte array and a version. Operations:
  - `write(off, bytes, expect_ver?) → version or error`
  - `punch(off, n, expect_ver?) → version or error`
  - `read(off, n) → bytes, version`
  - `read(off, n, at_ver) → bytes`
- Linearizable: each operation takes effect at one instant between its invoke and its complete. A
  write takes effect at its version, which must follow the chunk's: the next of its interval, or
  `k.1` of a later interval `k`, since a primary numbers a chunk's versions from its interval and
  peering keeps every version a kept one rests on; and it never passes over a version another write was
  answered OK with. A read returns the chunk's version and bytes; a read at a version, that
  version's bytes. A punch of an absent chunk is answered OK with no version and changes nothing.
  `TestTheChunkModel` gives each rule a history that holds and one that breaks it.
- **Results.** A write, punch or read answered OK is definite. Every other answer and no answer
  leave the result unknown: the store refuses `NoSpace` after ordering when its log stalls, peering
  can keep a version refused for its interval after it was sent to members, and a refusal for an
  `expect_ver` compares it with the newest version ordered, pending ones included, which a later
  peering can drop, so the refusal fits no order of what the chunk kept. A write the primary never
  ordered cannot take effect and is left out, as is a read with no answer. No run sends an
  `expect_ver` or reads `at_ver` yet; `TestTheChunkModel` alone checks their rules.
- **An unknown write** is checked as maybe applied, with no completion, unless a later interval's
  peering decided its version: kept, it takes effect like one answered OK; dropped, it is left out.
  Without that, the writes a failed primary refuses, a few dozen in a fault seed, each taking effect
  or not, ran Porcupine past its timeout on histories of 50 operations. An undecided one is
  concurrent with everything after its call, so once an operation showing a later version of its
  chunk completes, where it could only be no operation, its return is moved there.
- **Resent writes.** A write sent again keeps its request ID and is one operation, which the
  primary answers from its [resend table](design.md#data-layer-chunkstore).
  `TestAResentWriteIsAppliedOnce`: client A's write of X commits as 1.1 and its reply is lost, a
  read sees X, client B writes Y as 1.2, a read sees Y, and A sends X again, which is answered 1.1,
  and a read still sees Y. With the table planted away (`noResendTable`) X commits again as 1.3:
  the reads see X, Y, X, and with the one operation answered 1.3, no write takes the 1.1 the first
  read returned, so no order fits.
- Porcupine finds a linearizable order for every chunk of every history the runs record, over the
  seeds `scripts/seeds.sh` gives them: 1,000 fault seeds, 500 each of the primary-change, read and
  sub-block runs and 200 write-limit seeds. The scripted rows P1 to P22 of [Placement faults and
  invariants](#placement-faults-and-invariants) assert actions and record no history.
- **Planted bugs** (`TestPlantedBugsBreakChunkHistories`), each checking the history invariant alone,
  with the seeds failing and the first:

  | Planted bug | Run | Seeds failing | First |
  | --- | --- | --- | --- |
  | A read served from a pending version: the primary commits once its own log holds a version (`commitOnOwnLog`), and the next interval drops it | Read | 82 of 100 | 0 |
  | An old primary serving reads with no lease check (P1, `noLeaseCheck`): a client that missed the new primary's table reads from the old one after the new one acknowledged a write | Read | 11 of 100 | 8 |
  | Merging on the committed version (sub-block M2), one client pipelining 4 writes | Sub-block | 100 of 100 | 0 |
  | Peering dropping a subset of a chunk's pending versions, not a suffix (M7, `settleSubset`) | Primary-change | 26 of 500 | 60 |

  The M7 rate is that of the primary-change run's own check of kept bytes, which fails on the same
  seeds. The holder ending its lease on the slower of its clocks (P9's slews) is not planted here:
  the read run marks a cut node down after `node_down_after` (5 s), past every 4 s lease it held,
  and a new primary waits for its members' grants to end, so no lease of the old primary outlasts
  its grant and the plant fails no seed of 100 in either this check or the one-reader check. The
  lease pair run (`internal/lease`) plants it alone.
- **Cost.** Histories are split by chunk, so the check's cost is per chunk, and each run's check
  stops at 30 s, failing the seed. The model builds a state's bytes only when a read needs them.
  The checks add a few seconds to the seed runner's list on 2 processes: none of the five runs'
  times moved by more than a second. Open: the check's time on a long history of one chunk, for
  example 3 clients × 400 operations, which no run records.
- Close-to-open and the file-level checks of Testing strategy's layer 3 belong to
  [Simulated FUSE clients](#simulated-fuse-clients).

## etcd-raft module

- The module graph resolves `go.etcd.io/raft/v3` v3.6.0 through a `replace` to the fork in
  `third_party/raft`, and `go mod verify` passes.
- **Seeded election timeouts** (`third_party/raft/seeded_rand_test.go`).
  - Two replicas built with the same seed draw the same sequence of randomized election timeouts.
    Seeds 1 and 2 differ within their first 100 draws.
  - Every draw lies in [`ElectionTick`, 2 × `ElectionTick` − 1]: 100 to 199 ticks of 10 ms, so 1.00
    to 1.99 s, and 10,000 draws reach both ends.
  - With a panicking `crypto/rand.Reader` installed, three seeded replicas elect a leader, take a
    proposal and, once the leader is isolated, elect another on their own timeouts. The test first checks
    that `crypto/rand.Int`, as `globalRand` calls it, does reach the panicking reader.
- **Replay** (the review criterion). The [Raft shard](#raft-shard)'s simulator run,
  `TestRaftRunsReplayFromTheirSeed`, run twice from one seed gives a byte-identical scheduler trace
  (Raft message types included) and a byte-identical history of every entry applied.
- **Unseeded randomness is caught** (`TestUnseededElectionTimeoutsBreakReplay`). The same run with no
  `Config.Rand`, a bug planted in the shard, so the fork falls back to `crypto/rand`, gives two
  different traces for one seed.
- **ReadIndex retry fix** (etcd-io/raft#397, its behaviour in [Raft shard](design.md#metadata-layer-metastore)).
  The fork carries upstream commits `9b9d6ee` and `63903dd`; `read_only.go` equals v3.7.0's but
  for v3.7.0's pointer messages. The fix's own `TestReadOnlyDuplicateRequest` passes on the fork
  and fails on plain v3.6.0 ("readIndex for B is 1 (should be >= 3)").
- **Tech-debt entries.** `docs/tech-debts.md` holds two entries:
  - [the version pin](tech-debts.md#version-pin-goetcdioraftv3-v360), removed when an etcd-raft
    release keeps messages and entries without per-field allocations, at most 3 per message in
    `spikes/raft-rounds`;
  - [the fork](tech-debts.md#workaround-etcd-raft-fork-in-third_partyraft), removed when an upstream
    release takes a configurable random source, includes #397 and meets the pin's bar.
- `scripts/lint.sh`'s license check over `./...` reaches `go.etcd.io/raft/v3` through the Raft
  shard, and passes for etcd-raft (Apache-2.0) and its
  dependencies (`gogo/protobuf`, `golang/protobuf` and `google.golang.org/protobuf`,
  BSD-3-Clause); with only MIT allowed it names each of them. No CockroachDB-licensed code is in
  the fork or the shard.

## Upstream Raft tests

- `scripts/raft-tests.sh` runs every test package of the fork with the main module's toolchain, in
  CI's test job: `raft` (the unit tests and the datadriven interaction tests under `testdata/`),
  `confchange`, `quorum`, `raftpb`, `rafttest` and `tracker`. All pass on the fork.
- Each of the fork's two changes comes with a test: the seeded timeouts (etcd-raft module, above),
  and #397's own test.
- A move to a new upstream tag follows the fork's [tech-debt entry](tech-debts.md#workaround-etcd-raft-fork-in-third_partyraft):
  it merges only once this suite passes on the new tag.

## Raft shard

Trace tests (`internal/raftshard`) feed events to three shards by hand, delivering their messages,
completing their flushes and moving the clock, and assert on each shard's actions. The round's
durable write is the seam the [disk log](#raft-storage-in-the-disk-log) fills: a call's output
names the round to flush and carries its contents, the driver reports it with `Durable`, and only
then does the shard write the round to its `Storage`, which these tests keep across a restart in
place of replaying the disk log.

**Configuration.** The shard builds its `raft.Config` with:

- synchronous `Ready`/`Advance`, with `AsyncStorageWrites` off;
- `CheckQuorum` off and `PreVote` on;
- an election tick of 10 ms, `HeartbeatTick` 10 (100 ms) and `ElectionTick` 100;
- election timeouts drawn from a source seeded from the replica's own seed;
- `DisableProposalForwarding` on, so a follower drops a proposal ([Routing](design.md#metadata-layer-metastore)), and a forwarded `MsgProp` from a peer is dropped as undecodable.

`TestConfig` asserts each of these from the config. Raft storage in the disk log and Leader leases refer to this test rather than repeating it.

| Input | Expected actions |
| --- | --- |
| `ctx.Now` advances 10 ms | One `Tick` to `RawNode`: a leader sends no heartbeat for nine such steps |
| `ctx.Now` advances 100 ms on a leader of an active group | 10 ticks, and a heartbeat to each follower |
| `ctx.Now` advances 35 ms, 35 ms, then 30 ms | Three ticks each time with the 5 ms remainders carried, so the third step makes the tenth tick and the heartbeat |
| `ctx.Now` advances 5 s in one event, as after a suspend or with `Resumed` | 10 ticks, one heartbeat of them, and the rest dropped: a leader sends one heartbeat to each follower, not 50, and a follower does not campaign |
| No event but the tick timer for 2 s on a follower that supports no leader | It campaigns, pre-vote first, at its randomized timeout, between 1.00 and 1.99 s; 20 seeds give at least 10 different times |
| A peer message of 256 bytes, framing included | Carried inline |
| A peer message of 257 bytes or more (an append with entries) | Carried as an `IOBuf` handle, never inline, and decodes to the same message |
| An append over 256 bytes while the buffer pool is exhausted | The message is dropped as lost and counted (`Unsent`), never a panic or a heap fallback. Once the pool has room, Raft resends it and both followers catch up |
| A `NetRecv` that fails to decode (truncated framing, garbage body, an unknown type, a type only a node sends itself, a forwarded proposal, a buffer length past the buffer, a snapshot whose data `Config.CheckSnapshot` refuses) | Dropped and counted (`Undecodable`), its buffer freed. No panic, no step into `RawNode` |
| A message for another group, or for another replica of this one | Dropped and counted (`Misrouted`), not answered: a removed replica learns from its own log |
| `PeerLost` for a follower's node | The leader calls `ReportUnreachable`, so that follower goes from replicate to probe; the other follower stays in replicate |
| A leader with proposals in a round | The `MsgApp` to followers goes out in the same pass as the round to flush, not after the flush, and not again once it is durable. Batching into one entry per round is under Shard state machine |
| A follower receiving an append | `MsgAppResp` held until the round that holds the entry is durable, then sent; storage holds the entry only from then |
| A node granting a vote | `MsgVoteResp` held until the round holding the new term and vote is durable |
| A node answering a pre-vote while a round holding an append is in flight | `MsgPreVoteResp` waits for that round, as every message stepped mid-round does, then leaves with the next round's write, since a pre-vote changes no hard state; that round's `MsgAppResp` waits for its flush |
| A `Ready` with committed entries | Applied after persistence, then `Advance`. A message stepped while the round is in flight takes no second `Ready` before `Advance`; it comes out in the next round |
| A crash before the durable notice | On restart the follower's log lacks the entry, and the leader resends it. No acknowledgment was sent for it |
| A follower's append that only moves its commit index, then an append with an entry | The first takes no round and leaves storage's commit index where it was; the second's round writes the moved commit index, which etcd-raft hands out only once (`TestTheNextRoundWritesACommitIndexMovedWithoutOne`) |
| A leader's commit jumps more than 1 MiB of entries past its applied index | The `Ready` that hands over the first page is a round of its own: the leader sends nothing, its appends carrying the new commit index included, until that commit index is durable (`TestALeaderSendsACommitIndexPastItsPageOnlyOnceDurable`) |

**Simulator runs.** `TestRaftRunsReplayFromTheirSeed`, 20 seeds in `go test`, 2,000 per commit in
`scripts/seeds.sh` (15 s at `JOBS=2`), 10,000 once in 150 s. One group of three shards on the
simulated network and on node-pair leases, with 1-in-100 drops, 1-in-50 duplicates, up to 200 µs
of jitter, partitions cut and healed, and the faults of [Leader leases](#leader-leases)
(the leader cut off past its followers' grants, leadership transfers, pauses of up to 5 s, slewed and drifting clocks, links held); each round flushes as an fsync on its node's simulated
disk, so a crash loses the rounds in flight. Leaders propose a numbered value per tick, every third
over 256 bytes, and the first leader to apply 20 crashes and restarts from its storage. After 30 s
every partition is healed, and the run must apply a value proposed after the crash within 30 s
more. Every seed checks, after every step:

- [property] "acknowledged only once durable": no accepting `MsgAppResp` leaves before its replica's
  storage holds the entry, and no granted `MsgVoteResp` before it holds the term and vote, unless
  storage already holds a later term. One `Ready` can carry a vote together with a later term the
  replica moved to before that `Ready` was taken; once the later term is durable the replica never
  votes in the older one again.
- "applied entries agree": no two replicas apply different entries at one index.
- the simulator's driver contract.
- the three lease invariants of [Leader leases](#leader-leases).

Across the 20 seeds, traces show buffered messages, pauses, restarts and lost connections. In the
trace tests, every pool holds no buffer once the group settles. Planted
bugs show the checks bite: a shard that sends every message before its round's flush breaks
"acknowledged only once durable" within 20 seeds, and one drawing election timeouts from
`crypto/rand` breaks replay (etcd-raft module, above).

**Decoder.** `FuzzDecode` feeds arbitrary framing and bodies, inline and in a buffer: decoding never
panics, never accepts a type no peer sends, and a message it accepts encodes and decodes back to
itself.

**Benchmarks.** Encoding allocates nothing, inline or into a pool buffer. One 128-byte proposal
replicated, flushed and committed on three replicas makes 24 allocations: etcd-raft's message
and `Ready` slices and decoded entries, and three `Storage.Entries` results, one per replica
reading the committed entry; the budget belongs to [Raft cost per group](#raft-cost-per-group).

## Leader leases

Trace tests (`internal/raftshard`, `lease_test.go`) for fortification on the per-node-pair leases,
on the [Raft shard](#raft-shard)'s hand-driven network. Each replica's node has its own
`lease.Holder` and `lease.Grantor`, which the test renews by hand: a lease takes two grants
`rate_gap` apart, so the holder has a rate bound. Lease time follows the two-clock rule: the
holder ends a grant `lease_drift` (40 ms of 4 s) and `core.ResumeThreshold` (1 s) early on its
faster clock, counted from when it asked; the grantor waits the whole lease on its slower one. The expiry of one grant on the holder
(2.96 s after the ask, a widened margin, no lease before a rate bound) is the lease package's, and
its tests under [Peering and read leases](#peering-and-read-leases) cover it; here the shard only
reads it. `TestConfig` (Raft shard) asserts `CheckQuorum` off and `PreVote` on.

**Votes and campaigns while supporting a leader**

| Follower state | Message or event | Expected |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Supports leader L under its node's grant to L's node, support epoch e, grant held | `MsgPreVote` from challenger C | Dropped before `RawNode`. No response, no round, term unchanged |
| Same | `MsgVote` from C | Dropped |
| Same | `MsgVote` with the transfer context, from the target of a planned transfer | Passed to `RawNode`, which votes under Raft's rules: the granted vote leaves once its round is durable |
| Same | The leader's Raft messages lost from its election until the grant lapses, 4 s | Its election timer is stopped: no campaign, though 4 s is past any election timeout |
| Grant to L's node lapsed on the grantor's clocks | `MsgPreVote`, then `MsgVote`, from C | Passed and granted under Raft's rules (the review criterion "votes once its grant lapses") |
| Same, with no challenger | The lapse | Campaigns, pre-vote first, 150 to 300 ms (`raft_lapse_campaign`) after the first event that sees the lapse, not at its election timeout; 20 seeds give at least 10 different delays. The lapse comes no earlier than 4 s after the grant |
| Same, and the other follower's grant to L's node still holds, L unreachable | Its own pre-vote | Dropped by that follower, which sends nothing; it campaigns again at its election timeout, 1.00 to 1.99 s after the lapse |
| Supports L, and L itself asks for a (pre-)vote in a later term | The request | Support ends and the request is passed: L asks only once it no longer leads: it stepped down while its node's grant held, or its node restarted in place and the old grant was renewed, by its first ask after the wait before a slowed grantor clock let the grant lapse or by an ask of its old run reaching a paused grantor late |
| Node restarted 2 s ago on both clocks (within `primary_lease`, 4 s) | `MsgPreVote`, `MsgVote` | Dropped: no answer and no round |
| Node restarted 4.1 s ago on both clocks | `MsgPreVote`, `MsgVote` | Answered under Raft's rules |
| Node restarted 4.1 s ago on `CLOCK_BOOTTIME`, 3.9 s on `CLOCK_MONOTONIC_RAW` | `MsgPreVote`, `MsgVote` | Dropped |
| Node restarted, 3.9 s of 10 ms timer events | Its election timer | Stopped: no campaign during the restart wait |
| The leader's grant from follower F lapsed in support epoch e, and the leader's node renewed it, under e + 1 | Lease read | Refused: the renewal is fresh, under e + 1, and F's fortification under e no longer counts. Once the leader's next fortification request (a heartbeat later) reaches F, F supports it under e + 1 and the leader reads again |
| The follower's node restarted after fortifying the leader, and its new run granted the leader's node again, support epochs counting from 1 | Lease read | Refused: the fortification names the old run |
| Voted for a transfer target in term T + 1 | The term-T leader's fortification request | Ignored: no answer and no support |

**Lease end: a quorum of unexpired fortifications per half**

The leader counts itself as a fortified voter whose entry never expires: it votes for a
challenger only after stepping down, and a replica that does not lead serves no lease read. The
follower nodes' grants are asked at the times given; the test checks a lease read 1 µs before and
at the end, 2.96 s after the ask named.

| Voters | Fortified, asked at | Lease ends |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 3: L, F1, F2 | F1 (0 s) | 2.96 s, F1's expiry (the review criterion: a lease to that follower's expiry) |
| 3 | F1 (0 s), F2 (2 s) | 4.96 s, the later expiry: the 2nd latest of ∞, 4.96 and 2.96 |
| 3 | L only | No lease: reads go through ReadIndex |
| 5 | a (0 s), b (1 s), c (2 s) | 3.96 s, the 3rd latest of ∞, 4.96, 3.96 and 2.96 |
| 5 | a (0 s) | No lease |
| Joint, new {L, D, E}, old {L, B, C} | B (0 s), D (1 s) | 2.96 s: each half gives its own quorum, and the old half's ends first |
| Joint, as above | B (0 s), C (1 s) | No lease: the new half has no quorum |

**Reads**

| State | Read | Expected |
| --- | --- | --- |
| New leader, fortified, its first entry not yet acknowledged | `LeaseRead` | False. `ReadIndex` gives nothing until the entry commits, then the commit index once a quorum answers the read's heartbeat |
| Fortified, an entry of its term committed, lease unexpired | `LeaseRead` | True: served from memory, with no round trip. `BenchmarkLeaseRead` allocates nothing |
| The `Ready` carrying `MsgTimeoutNow` to the transfer target taken | `LeaseRead` | False from that point to the end of the term. The target, whose vote request the supporting follower passes, leads, fortifies and serves lease reads |
| Holder ends its leases on `Resumed` (a suspend, or a VMClock marker change) | `LeaseRead` | False at once. Once the holder holds its leases again, in the same support epochs, true with no new fortification |
| A grantor's heartbeat shows its `CLOCK_MONOTONIC_RAW` moved further since the last grant than the margin allows | `LeaseRead` | False at once, as on `Resumed`. Peer messages in a pass are handled before reads (the event loop's rule) |

**Decoder.** `FuzzDecode` (Raft shard) also feeds fortification messages: one of another length,
in a buffer or of an unknown kind is dropped as undecodable, and one it accepts encodes and decodes
back to itself.

**Simulator runs.** `TestRaftRunsReplayFromTheirSeed` (Raft shard) runs the group on node-pair
leases: every node asks every other for a lease when its holder is due, grants as its grantor
allows, heartbeats the holders it grants once a second and handles `Resumed` on both, through
frames of its own on the simulated network. Its faults cover the MetaStore faults below that a
single group without configuration changes can meet: partitions cut and healed, the first leader
crashed and restarted in place, the leader cut off from both followers for 4 to 8 s, past their
grants, so they elect another before it hears of it, leadership handed to another replica at
random, pauses of up to 5 s of every kind but a stop in place on kvm-clock (`PauseFrozen`, whose
lost heartbeats leave a holder serving on an old lease for up to a heartbeat, an [open
question](design.md#roadmap-and-open-questions)), slews of `CLOCK_BOOTTIME` up to ±22.6%, raw
clocks within ±4% and a raw rate step after measurement, and one direction of a link held up to
50 ms. After every step it checks:

- [property] "at most one leader per shard per term".
- "a replica's storage holds the commit index of each configuration change it applied, and of each
  entry it applied before its last durable round": what a restart would take as its commit index,
  the durable hard state's or the base's, is at or past both. Planted, a configuration change
  applied without a round of its own breaks it in the replacement run (`TestAConfigurationChangeAppliedBeforeItsCommitIsDurableIsForgotten`,
  `neg-conf-commit-not-durable`; the first seed).
- [property] "no two replicas of a shard serve lease reads at overlapping times": when a replica's
  pass ends able to serve a lease read, no other running, unpaused replica could, at its own
  clocks, unless its next pass would first see `Resumed`.
- [property] "a lease read sees every applied entry": a replica able to serve a lease read has
  applied every index any replica applied while it led, which covers every write a client was
  told of, since only a leader acknowledges an entry, on applying it. A follower's applies do not
  count: the leader's commit index goes out with its next round's appends, while the leader applies
  what that round's `Ready` commits only once the round is durable, so a follower can apply an
  entry first.

`TestRaftRunsRegressionSeeds` keeps seed 120, which found a leader cut off from both followers and
then suspended 0.92 s: `CLOCK_BOOTTIME` gained nothing, as the kernel counts a sleep in whole seconds,
so no `Resumed` came, and its holder kept a follower's lease 0.92 s past the grant while that
follower, elected, served lease reads. The seed passes as a holder ends each lease `core.ResumeThreshold` early.

**Planted bugs.** Each must break its invariant within the seeds named, checking it alone:

| Planted bug | Invariant | Seeds of 500 | First | Test |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Followers vote and campaign while they support a leader | Lease reads | 231 | 1 | `TestFollowersVotingWhileSupportingBreakTheLeaseInvariant`, 20 seeds |
| Lease reads before an entry of the leader's term commits; most new leaders apply in time | Lease reads see every applied entry | 4 | 159 | `TestLeaseReadsBeforeAnEntryOfTheTermCommitsBreakTheInvariant`, 630 seeds |
| The [epoch change model](#epoch-change-model)'s `neg-no-epoch-bump`: the leader counts a fortification under whatever support epoch its lease from the follower now runs, as if a lapsed grant were renewed in its old epoch. It needs the leader cut off past its followers' grants, then healed | Lease reads | 11 | 19 | `TestPlantedLeaseBugsBreakTheLeaseReaderInvariant`, 230 seeds |
| The epoch change model's `neg-transfer-keeps-lease`: the leader serves lease reads after `MsgTimeoutNow` left | Lease reads | 11 | 13 | `TestPlantedLeaseBugsBreakTheLeaseReaderInvariant`, 230 seeds |
| A follower serves lease reads while it supports its leader | Lease reads | 500 | 0 | `TestPlantedLeaseBugsBreakTheLeaseReaderInvariant`, 10 seeds |
| A replica grants every vote it is asked for, so two candidates of one term can both win | One leader per term | 8 | 59 | `TestVotingForEveryCandidateBreaksTheOneLeaderInvariant`, 320 seeds |

`neg-no-epoch-bump` is planted at the leader's check rather than in `lease.Grantor`: the grantor's
plants are reachable only from `internal/lease`'s own tests, and a leader that ignores the epoch
counts exactly the fortifications a grantor that never bumps would let through. Across the 20 `go
test` seeds some pass can serve a lease read, and leaders are cut off and transfer their
leadership (9 and 10 times), which the test asserts, so the checks are not vacuous. The simulator
gets configuration changes from [Voter replacement](#voter-replacement)'s runs, which check these
three properties through the joint configuration; those runs make no random transfers or cut-offs,
since the replacement cuts and heals its own links. The [disk-log](#raft-storage-in-the-disk-log)
crash runs make both.

**Simulator faults** (MetaStore), with the invariant "no two replicas of a shard serve lease reads at overlapping times":

1. **A quiescent leader's node partitioned from one follower.** The other follower's grant keeps the lease. The partitioned follower's grant lapses and it stops supporting, but it cannot win without a majority. Expected: one lease-reading replica at any time.
2. **A leader's node suspended past its lease (5 s).** On resume it ends every lease (`Resumed`) before serving. A new leader may have been elected after the grants lapsed on the grantors' clocks. Expected: no overlap.
3. **A leader transfer while lease reads arrive.** Expected: the old leader serves none after `MsgTimeoutNow` leaves, and the new leader none before it is fortified and has committed an entry of its term.
4. **A configuration change while a lease is held.** Expected: the lease requires quorums in both halves throughout the joint configuration.
5. **Lease clocks.** A holder's or grantor's `CLOCK_BOOTTIME` slewed by up to ±22.6% while its `CLOCK_MONOTONIC_RAW` drifts by up to ±4%, and grants delayed by asymmetric queueing of up to 50 ms. Expected: no overlap. A crash fails over within 5.2 s, the most a 22.6% slew can stretch a grantor's wait, plus `raft_lapse_campaign` and an election, and so does a leader restarted in place, whose node asks for no lease during its restart wait. In the simulator runs, crash to the first value proposed after it applied: 4.1 s at the median, 5.3 s at the 90th percentile, 7.0 s at the 99th, over 2,000 seeds. With no fault but a crash and restart in place, a follower campaigns within `primary_lease`, a heartbeat and `raft_lapse_campaign` of the crash (`TestALeaderRestartedInPlaceFailsOverOnTheLapse`).

## Voter replacement

Placement is a pure function, `meta.PlaceVoters`, over the shard map, the metadata nodes,
phase 3's `DiskRecord` and the halted replicas, tested by table (`internal/meta`, `placement_test.go`); the Control-plane
group commits its result under `ctl/` and hands each group's leader its entry. The swap is the Raft
shard's: trace tests (`internal/raftshard`, `replace_test.go`) run voters A, B and C (replica IDs
1 to 3) and D, a fresh replica with empty storage on a fourth node, on the
[Raft shard](#raft-shard)'s hand-driven network, hand the leader the plan with `SetPlan`, and stand
a snapshot taken at the leader's applied index in for the point-in-time view the
[Shard state machine](#shard-state-machine) will give. `refill_after` is 10 minutes.

**Placement**

| Disks and plan | Expected |
| --- | --- |
| Four new groups on three metadata nodes of two disks each | Each group gets replica IDs 1 to 3, one per node; every disk holds two voters |
| C's node down for 9 minutes 59 s, a fourth metadata node up | No change |
| C's node down for 10 minutes | C replaced by replica ID 4 on the fourth node's least-loaded disk; A and B unchanged |
| Only three metadata nodes, C's node down for an hour | Nothing replaced; the group runs on A and B |
| C halted at an entry it cannot decode, for 9 minutes 59 s, then 10 minutes, a fourth metadata node up | No change, then C replaced by replica ID 4 on the fourth node; never on the other disk of C's node, which runs the same release |
| Only three metadata nodes, C halted for an hour | Nothing replaced |
| C's disk reports a new log ID, three nodes | C replaced at once, on another disk of its node: the new disk, which holds no voter, or the other disk on a tie |
| D, planned in place of C, down for 10 minutes before its swap | D replaced by replica ID 5 on a fifth node, the same rule |
| A voter's disk, down, reports its log from the node of another voter of the group | The voter placed again as replica ID 4; no node holds two voters, counted by where each disk now reports from |
| Twelve groups on four nodes; disk 1, down, reports its log from the fourth node, which holds no voter of some groups | Each of its voters placed again on another disk, never disk 1, though disk 1 ties for the fewest voters there |
| A node outside the metadata nodes | Takes no voter |
| The control-plane group | No test of its own: placement and the shard treat it as one more group of the map, with nothing special-cased |

**Swap**

| Events | Expected |
| --- | --- |
| The plan names the voters the group has, C cut off | No configuration change; A and B commit |
| The plan names D in place of C, C and D cut off | A adds D as a learner, its node in the change's context. Five proposals commit on A and B with D hearing nothing, and D stays a learner |
| Then the plan names A, B and C again | A removes D, the learner the plan dropped |
| D reconnected | D's first append is refused, its log empty, so A sends a snapshot; D restores it (`Output.Snapshot`), then takes the log. One `ConfChangeV2`, remove 3 and add 4, commits on A and B, and A, B and D end in voters 1, 2, 4 out of the joint configuration |
| B cut off once D was added, D caught up | Nothing commits on A and D, and D stays a learner, never promoted to make a quorum. Once B returns the swap commits |
| The plan drops the leader A | A transfers leadership to B, which adds D and swaps it for A |
| The plan drops A, B down, A holding a node-pair lease from C only | A transfers to C, never to B |
| The plan drops A, B up, C up and leased to A but five proposals behind | A does not transfer to C |
| The plan names three new replicas and none of the voters | The leader swaps new replicas in for the other two voters first, then transfers to one; the group ends on the three |
| A, the leader, cut off while B leads, and the plan swaps D in for A | A still leads its old term; once reconnected, its messages draw the removal notice and A reports `Removed` |
| A proposal every 10 ms, D's link one step slower than B's | D, trailing the current commit index for good, is swapped in; planted, a learner held to the current commit index never is |
| A removal notice at any index to D before its addition | Ignored: a notice proves a removal only to a replica its own applied configuration holds |
| B holds the joint entry swapping D in for C, and hears its commit from an append with no entry | A round of its own: B sends nothing, its acknowledgment included, and stays in the first configuration until the round is durable, then holds that commit index in storage, applies the joint configuration and acknowledges. A transfer's `MsgTimeoutNow` that came meanwhile has B campaign once the round is durable (`TestACommittedConfigurationChangeIsDurableBeforeItApplies`) |
| The same, and B halts before the round is durable | B steps the `MsgTimeoutNow` no more and stays a follower (`TestAReplicaThatHaltsDropsTheTransferItDeferred`) |
| A, holding the joint entry, hears B's acknowledgment of it, a quorum of the first configuration | A round of its own: A sends no append, none carrying the new commit index, and stays in the first configuration until the round is durable, then applies the joint configuration and sends its appends (`TestALeaderSendsTheCommitOfAConfigurationChangeOnlyOnceDurable`) |
| B applied the joint configuration and holds the leave; it crashes before it hears the leave commit, A hands D its leadership on A and D, and B, restarted from its base and the rounds it made durable, campaigns cut off from A and D | B restarts in the joint configuration and wins no term on its vote and C's. Planted, rounds that write only their own `Ready`'s hard state bring B back in the first configuration, where it leads the term D leads (`TestARestartDoesNotTakeAReplicaBackAcrossACommittedConfigurationChange`) |
| C, cut off through the whole swap, restarts after it | Within a second, inside its restart wait and with no pre-vote or vote sent, C asks its peers whether it is a member; their answer at an applied index past its own makes C report `Removed` and write a round recording it. It never leads over the next 100 heartbeats, while A leads on (`TestARemovedReplicaThatReturnsRecordsItsRemovalAndNeverLeads`) |
| C learns its removal from a peer's notice and restarts | Its disk log replays the round recording the removal, and C reports `Removed` again (`TestARemovalLearnedFromANoticeSurvivesARestart`) |
| A removal notice at an index below the replica's applied index | Ignored: a peer that has not applied the change that added it says nothing of its removal |
| B has committed D's addition, its commit index at D's applied index, but not applied it; D asks B, or sends B a Raft message | B answers at its applied index, which D ignores; an answer at its commit index would have D delete its state |
| C started with Peers that lack the leader, as one restored from a snapshot; the leader sends to it | C learns the leader's node from the message, and its reply reaches it |
| A, B, C and D in the joint configuration that swaps C for D, every node holding a lease from every other; C, in the outgoing half alone, wins an election and commits the leave | C holds its removal unapplied, so it stays a voter of the joint configuration and leads on, proposes nothing, and hands its leadership to a caught-up voter of the plan, which applies the leave. The followers that applied the leave keep C's node until the next change applies, so the target acknowledges C's re-proposed leave (`TestALeaderThatCommittedItsOwnRemovalHandsItsLeadershipOn`) |
| The same, with C's `MsgTimeoutNow` lost, so it cannot hand its leadership on; every voter of the plan applies the leave and C's node deletes C while it leads, still renewing the followers' grants | Within an election timeout each follower asks C's node about replica ID 3, which answers that it is gone; the followers stop supporting C and campaign after `raft_lapse_campaign`, and one leads voters 1, 2 and 4 within an election timeout, a heartbeat, `raft_lapse_campaign` and three heartbeats. No two replicas could serve a lease read at once (`TestFollowersOfALeaderThatAppliedItsOwnRemovalCampaign`) |
| Then an ask about replica 3 to C, and asks about 4 and about 3 to D | C, removed, answers that 3 is gone; D, live, answers neither and counts the ask about another replica misrouted: the ask names the replica ID, never the group alone, so a new replica of the group on a node is not taken for the old one. `Gone`, the node's answer for a replica it no longer holds, answers the ask and nothing else |
| B, supporting C, gets an answer that 4 is gone, then that 3 is | B keeps its support, then drops it (`TestANodeAnswersGoneOnlyForTheReplicaItNoLongerHolds`) |
| Replica 1 of group 5, live, through the control-plane host that holds it, gets asks about replica 9 of group 5, replica 1 of group 7 and itself | The first two, naming replicas its node does not hold, reach `Gone`, which answers each from the replica asked about; the ask about itself is not answered (`TestAReplicaItIsNotIsAnsweredGone`) |
| C, leading the joint configuration from the outgoing half, holds its removal and is then cut off from the others' Raft messages, its node renewing every grant | The followers ask C's node, hear that C is gone and elect a leader, which serves lease reads; C, which learned its removal, serves none. Planted, it keeps serving them at once with the new leader (`TestARemovedLeaderThatKeepsReadingBreaksTheLeaseInvariant`, the voter model's `neg-removed-keeps-lease`) |
| A leads the joint configuration, commits the leave with B, tells C alone that it committed, and halts or dies | B or D, holding the leave with only the joint configuration applied, leads with C's vote, the outgoing half's last one up, and applies the leave: after an election timeout and a round trip when A halts and hands its leadership on, once the grants to A's node lapse when it dies. Planted, a C that stops once it learns its removal, as if its node deleted it, leaves the outgoing half one voter, and no leader of the plan's configuration follows (`TestARemovedVoterKeepsTheOutgoingHalfsVoteForAVoterThatHoldsTheLeave`, the voter model's `ci-halt-live` and `neg-removed-deletes-at-once`) |
| C leads term 2 from the outgoing half and commits the leave on B and D while A lags; B wins term 3 before applying it, appends its entry to C alone and dies | C, holding the outgoing half's newest entry, wins, commits the leave on A and D and hands its leadership to one of them. Planted, a C that applies its removal campaigns no more, and A and D, which applied only the joint configuration, never win its vote (`TestARemovedVoterThatHoldsTheOutgoingHalfsNewestEntryLeadsAndHandsOff`, the voter model's `ci-leave-die-live` and `neg-removed-applies-removal`) |
| C leads the joint configuration and commits its removal, no node holding a lease from another, as in the planned voters' restart wait | C hands its leadership to a planned voter caught up past the leave, which leads having applied it within three heartbeats: a removed leader takes no proposals, so its target needs no lease (`TestARemovedLeaderHandsOffWithoutALease`); with the lease asked of it, C led on, re-proposing the leave |
| C leads the joint configuration from the outgoing half and commits its removal; every MsgTimeoutNow C sends A, its first planned voter by ID, is lost, as when A halted or is cut off one way | Once its transfer to A times out, C hands its leadership to B or D, which leads having applied the leave within three election timeouts; C retried A for good when it always took its first target (`TestARemovedLeaderTriesTheNextPlannedVoterWhenATransferFails`) |
| A leader that applied the leave crashes | It restarts with the leave committed, in the plan's configuration (`TestALeaderThatCrashesAfterCommittingTheLeaveRestartsWithItCommitted`) |
| Planted: the learner promoted at once | D swapped in holding nothing (`TestAnEagerLeaderPromotesALearnerThatHoldsNothing`) |
| Planted: D added as a voter | With C down, nothing commits while D hears nothing (`TestAReplacementAddedAsAVoterStallsProposals`) |
| D, empty, catches up from a snapshot the leader took past the leave | D reports the snapshot's index as its configuration's, so it counts as having applied the leave (`TestARestoredSnapshotMovesTheConfigurationIndex`) |

**Deleting the dropped replica.** `Control` (`internal/meta`, `deletes_test.go`) holds the plan
swapping D, replica 4, in for C, replica 3, in its shard map and hears each node's report of its
replicas: group, ID, the index its applied configuration holds at, joint or not, removed or not,
and the voters.

| Reports | Expected |
| --- | --- |
| A, B and D report the joint configuration, then C reports it with its removal, then B an earlier configuration of A and B alone, then A and D report the leave, then B; once the plan is complete, A reports its removal, then C reports none | C is named for deletion only once B too reports a configuration of the plan's voters alone at or past the lowest such index: reports of the joint configuration, whose incoming half is the plan's, never count, nor do reports of a configuration of fewer voters. A leader without its lease names nothing, a planned voter is never named, even reporting its removal, and C, last reported not having learned its removal, is not named once the plan is complete (`TestADroppedReplicaIsDeletedOnlyOnceEveryPlannedVoterAppliedTheLeave`) |
| B, a planned voter, reports the joint configuration and is then down for good, over three `node_down_after`; the next plan swaps E in for B, and A reports its joint configuration before its leave | C is kept while B is down, and while A applied only the next plan's joint configuration; once A, D and E report the next plan's leave, C is named: an earlier plan completes through the current one (`TestADroppedReplicaIsKeptWhileAPlannedVoterIsDownForGood`) |
| Real shards A, B, C and D run the swap, each replica's report reaching `Control` every tick; the one of A and B that does not lead hears nothing for 10 heartbeats once it applied the joint configuration, while the others commit the leave | C is named only once A, B and D applied the leave and C learned its removal, within a few heartbeats of the lagging voter hearing again. Mutated to count joint reports, `Control` names C while the lagging voter holds the joint configuration (`TestShardReportsDeleteTheDroppedReplicaOnceThePlanIsComplete`) |
| Planted, joint reports count: A, B and D report the joint configuration, and C its removal | C is named (`TestCountingJointReportsDeletesWhileAVoterAppliedOnlyTheJointConfiguration`, the plant of `neg-joint-report-counts`) |
| A shard map is staged whose group's last ID falls, whose plan names an ID above its last ID, repeats one, adds one handed out before, or drops voters and adds none | Each is refused, so a plan always names a replica ID no earlier configuration had, which its completion rests on; an unchanged plan, one adding a fresh ID, and a new group are staged (`TestAShardMapThatReusesAReplicaIDIsRefused`) |
| The leading control-plane host gets A's and B's reports of the leave, C's node's report of C, removed, then D's, then C's node's again | C's node is told nothing before D reported, D's node nothing at all, and C's node, on its next report, a delete naming C (`TestAReportIsAnsweredWithTheReplicasToDelete`) |
| A node whose loop reported three replicas, one removed, gets a delete naming those three and a fourth, first from a node that is no control-plane voter, then from the one it talks to | The heartbeat carries the replicas its loop last reported; the first delete is dropped, and of the second only the removed replica reaches the loop (`internal/node`, `TestADeleteReachesOnlyAReplicaThatLearnedItsRemoval`) |
| The control-plane group of hosts A, B and C, every node holding a lease from every other, with D a fresh host; its leader's own `Control` plans D in for a follower | The leader adds D as a learner, swaps it in and leaves the joint configuration; every voter reports its replica each second, and the dropped voter is told to delete it, stopping with `ErrDeleted`, only once A, B and D applied the plan; a voter of the plan then leads and answers a `Txn` (`TestTheControlPlaneGroupSwapsInItsPlanAndDeletesTheDroppedVoter`) |
| As above, then the dropped voter restarts | Its replay finds the round flagged deleted, and it stops with `ErrDeleted` before its replica starts (`TestADeletedControlPlaneVoterStaysDeletedAcrossARestart`) |
| As above, the plan dropping the leader | The leader hands its leadership to a planned voter, whose `Control` hands its replica the same plan and carries out the swap; the old leader is deleted only once it learned its removal and the plan is complete, and a voter of the plan leads (`TestAControlPlaneLeaderThePlanDropsHandsItsLeadershipOn`) |
| The `ci-halt-live` wedge on the control-plane group: hosts A, B, C and D boot in the joint configuration, A leads with a `Control` planning its incoming half, commits the leave with B and tells C alone, and the voters report for 3 s; then A halts or dies | B or D leads having applied the plan within an election timeout and a round trip, or a lapse and an election timeout once A dies. Halted, A still reports, so C is deleted once B and D applied the leave, never before; dead, A never reports again and C is kept. Planted, A's `Control` counts joint reports and deletes C before the halt or death, and no voter of the plan leads again (`TestTheControlPlaneGroupsRemovedVoterKeepsTheOutgoingHalfsVote`); with `complete` mutated to count joint reports, the unplanted runs fail too |
| The `ci-leave-die-live` wedge on the control-plane group: hosts A, B, C and D boot in the joint configuration and A is cut off; C leads and commits the leave on B and D, which do not learn it committed and whose acknowledgements past the leave C does not hear; B, its heartbeats from C lost, wins the next term, appends its entry to C alone and dies; then A returns, every node holding a lease from every other | C, holding the outgoing half's newest entry, wins, commits the leave on A and D and hands its leadership to one of them, which leads having applied the plan within four election timeouts; C is kept, since B is down for good (`TestTheControlPlaneGroupsRemovedVoterHoldingTheNewestEntryLeadsAndHandsOff`) |
| Three control-plane voters report for 3 s, every node holding a lease from every other | The leader's `Control` holds the three as voters and no node, sends a voter no table, delta, session table or disk membership, and stages the next format level, which a voter's report of release 0 does not hold back. Mutated to take a voter's report as a node's, it fails (`TestAVoterReportCountsTowardNoNode`) |
| A delete naming a control-plane voter that has not learned its removal, as a stale or replayed one would | The voter's host runs on. Mutated to stop without the removal, it fails (`TestADeleteToAVoterThatWasNotRemovedLeavesItRunning`) |
| `Control` takes a voter's report, and the buffer its voters came in then changes | The report keeps the voters it was given. Mutated to keep the buffer, it fails (`TestAVoterReportKeepsItsOwnVoters`) |

The node report's replica list and the delete cross the wire whole (`TestNodeMessagesCrossTheWireWhole`, `TestDeletesCrossTheWireWhole`), and `FuzzDecodeNodeReport` and `FuzzDecodeDelete` feed their decoders. Every message kind the package declares has a byte of its own, which `TestEveryMessageKindIsDistinct` reads from the source, so a new kind on a used byte fails it. A Raft round's deleted flag, as its removed flag, round-trips through `FuzzDecodeRound`.

The membership question, the ask about a leader and their answers are fortification-sized frames that `FuzzDecode` also feeds.

**Simulator runs.** `TestVoterReplacementRunsReplayFromTheirSeed`, 20 seeds in `go test`, 2,000
per commit in `scripts/seeds.sh` (16 s on its default 4 processes), runs the
[Raft shard](#raft-shard)'s faults, crash and lease frames on four nodes. From 2 to 4 s in, once
one of the first three replicas leads, a follower among them, or in half the seeds the leader, is cut off
from every other node, and up to 2 s later every replica gets the plan naming the fourth node's replica in its place. Every
replica's storage takes a snapshot at its applied index after each pass and compacts all but 10
entries below it, so the new replica, and any lagging voter, catches up from snapshots. The
replaced replica is reconnected up to a second after the plan, mid-swap, in half the seeds, and a
second after the swap in the rest. Two faults are drawn independently, each in half the seeds:

- `outgoing`: the leader that proposes the swap, once the replaced replica is reconnected
  mid-swap, hands it its leadership, and every `MsgTimeoutNow` the replaced replica sends is lost,
  so it cannot hand its leadership on, as in the [Voter replacement model](#voter-replacement-model)'s
  `ci-live-moved`.
- `wedge`: a leader that is the first replica to apply the plan's configuration while the
  replaced replica is reconnected sends the messages carrying that commit, and every later one, to
  the replaced replica alone until the faults stop; once that replica learned its removal, the
  leader halts, or in half of these seeds (`die`) its node stands still for good, as in
  `ci-halt-live`.

The run stands in for the control plane: once every voter of the plan applied its configuration,
the node of the replaced replica, if that replica learned its removal, deletes it, renews its
grants still and answers an ask about it that it is gone. Every node renews its node-pair leases
while it runs, whatever its replicas do, as a node does in production. A seed passes once the
replaced replica reported itself removed and the new one applied a value proposed after the swap,
and replays to the same trace and history. After every step it checks the Raft runs' properties
and:

- [property] "no learner is promoted to voter before it has caught up with its leader's log": a
  leader's round holding a `ConfChangeV2` that promotes a learner leaves only while the learner's
  storage holds every entry the leader had committed a heartbeat earlier. Promoting at once breaks
  it within 20 seeds (`TestPromotingALearnerBeforeItCaughtUpBreaksTheInvariant`).
- "only a replica the group's configuration removed deletes its state": no replica but the
  replaced one reports `Removed`, and it only once it holds the committed change that removes it
  or some replica applied a configuration without it.
- [property] "a replica leads having applied the plan's configuration within 15 election timeouts
  of the faults stopping", the model's `NewLeader`. A run done before then runs on quietly until
  a replica leads so, or the bound passes. Fifteen is past the longest wait a run allows
