  once its faults stop: a pause drawn before then holds a leader's node up to 5 s, its followers'
  grants lapse `primary_lease` and a heartbeat after its last renewal, they campaign
  `raft_lapse_campaign` later, and two split votes cost up to 2 s each, 14.3 s in all; the longest
  over 2,000 seeds was 7.8 s.

Planted, each of the voter model's rules that no scripted test alone covers breaks one of these
properties, and the same seed finishes unplanted:

| Plant | Model | Breaks | Found by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| A replica its plan drops reports itself removed and stops at once, before any change commits | `neg-delete-on-plan` | "only a replica the group's configuration removed deletes its state" | `TestAReplicaDeletedOnItsPlanBreaksTheInvariant`, seed 0 |
| A replica takes a removal notice from a peer that applied less than it: an old voter's ask a second into the run takes the fourth replica's answer, sent before that replica applied anything | `neg-notice-any-index` | Same | `TestANoticeFromAPeerBehindBreaksTheInvariant`, seed 0 |
| A replica asks its peers and takes a removal notice while its own applied configuration lacks it: the fourth replica does so a second into the run, before its addition | `neg-notice-non-member` | Same | `TestANoticeToANonMemberBreaksTheInvariant`, seed 0 |
| A restart tells etcd-raft that every entry it knows committed is applied, so the replica campaigns with a committed configuration change unapplied (the plant lies about the applied index at restart, the code's only hand on etcd-raft's check, where the model's counterexample needs no restart): the regress fault's voter restarts in its base's configuration and, on the replaced replica's vote, wins the term the fourth replica won | `neg-campaign-unapplied` | "at most one leader per shard per term" | `TestACampaignWithAConfigurationChangeUnappliedElectsTwoLeaders`, the regress fault's runs (below); seed 0 |
| A replica applies the swap one change at a time, so it counts the incoming half alone: under the split fault (below) the old voter, which applied only the learner's addition, wins on the replaced replica's vote the term the fourth replica won on the leader's | `neg-joint-one-half` | Same | `TestAJointConfigurationCountingOneHalfElectsTwoLeaders`, seed 0 |
| A leader proposes the swap and the leave behind the learner's addition, before it applied any, past etcd-raft's one-pending-change check: all three commit on a quorum of the old configuration, and under the split fault the old voter, which applied none, wins on the replaced replica's vote the term the fourth replica won on the leader's | `neg-one-at-a-time` | Same | `TestAChangeProposedBeforeThePreviousAppliedElectsTwoLeaders`, seed 0 |
| A restart starts etcd-raft at its base's commit index, not its hard state's: the regress fault's voter knows none of the swap's entries committed, restarts in its base's configuration and, on the replaced replica's vote, wins the term the fourth replica won | `neg-restart-commit-at-base` | Same | `TestARestartAtItsBasesCommitElectsTwoLeaders`, the regress fault's runs (below); seed 0 (20 of the first 20) |
| Followers never ask the node of the leader they support about it: once the removed leader's node deletes it, they support it for good | `neg-no-support-ask` | "a replica leads having applied the plan's configuration" | `TestFollowersThatNeverAskKeepARemovedLeader`, runs that always draw `outgoing` |
| A removed replica stops at once, as if its node deleted it: the wedge leaves the outgoing half one voter | `neg-removed-deletes-at-once` | Same | `TestARemovedVoterDeletedAtOnceLeavesNoLeader`, runs that always draw `wedge` and `die`; seed 1 |
| A removed replica applies its removal and campaigns no more: holding the outgoing half's newest entry, it refuses every voter of the plan its vote | `neg-removed-applies-removal` | Same | `TestARemovedVoterThatAppliesItsRemovalLeavesNoLeader`, the same runs; seed 30 |
| A halted replica that no longer leads leaves an ask about it unanswered: a halted leader whose hand-off fails steps down on the target's later term and never campaigns, and a follower still supporting it refuses every candidate | `neg-halted-silent` | Same | `TestAHaltedLeaderThatStepsDownAndKeepsSilentLeavesNoLeader`, seeds 770 and 1388 of the run, which found the bug |
| A halted leader never hands its leadership on: when the wedge fault's leader halts instead of standing still, it keeps leading, its followers supporting it, and no replica that has not halted leads | `neg-halted-keeps-leading` | Same | `TestAHaltedLeaderThatKeepsLeadingLeavesNoLeader`, seed 1 |

A halted wedge leader's heartbeats tell the others the leave committed once the faults stop, so
only a dead one wedges the `neg-removed-*` runs.

A halted leader that still leads serves no lease read, and its replica answers no ask about it
as gone, so its followers keep their support until it steps down
(`TestAHaltedLeaderReadsNothingAndIsNotGoneWhileItLeads`).

With the regress fault (`TestAVoterRestartedMidSwapKeepsTheConfigurationItKnewCommitted`, 20 seeds
in `go test` and 2,000 per commit in `scripts/seeds.sh`, with no other fault but the pauses), the first old voter that follows, applied the joint
configuration and holds the leave past its commit index crashes; until 10 s on it reaches only the
replaced replica, which reaches only it, and once the leader applied the leave it hands the fourth
replica its leadership. Every seed finishes. Planted, rounds that write only their own `Ready`'s
hard state and none for a `Ready` that commits a configuration change (`neg-hard-state-old`)
bring the crashed voter back in the configuration before the swap, where it wins the term the
fourth replica won on the replaced replica's vote: "at most one leader per shard per term" breaks
within 5 seeds (`TestRoundsThatLeaveTheCommitOfASwapBehindElectTwoLeaders`; 39 of the first 40).

The split fault is the regress one with no crash: the old voter is cut off the same way once the
leader applied the plan's configuration while that voter applied neither it nor the joint one.
Unplanted it never fires, as the voter acknowledged the leave and so applied the joint
configuration first; a replica that applies the swap one change at a time (`neg-joint-one-half`),
or a leader that commits every change on the old configuration (`neg-one-at-a-time`), opens that
window.

`TestVoterReplacementRegressionSeeds` keeps three seeds that found bugs: 6389, which found a
lease-reading leader behind a follower that applied first (the run has since changed and no longer
reaches it); only a leader's applies count against it (above, under [Leader leases](#leader-leases)); 8218, a leader whose
configuration change of an earlier term was lost and that proposed none again; and 1005, a dropped
leader waiting for a follower to reach its own durable index, which steady writes never allow.

[property] "a replacement never stalls proposals while two voters of the old configuration are
up": `TestAReplacementNeverStallsProposals`, 20 seeds in `go test` and 2,000 per commit (9 s),
runs the same replacement with no fault but the cut-off voter, and the new replica's node
suspended for 2 s as the plan names it; between the plan and the swap the two running old voters
never go 100 ms without a commit (12 ms at most over 20 seeds, a tick and a round). Adding the
replacement as a voter instead stalls them past 100 ms within 20 seeds
(`TestAddingTheReplacementAsAVoterStallsProposals`).

## Raft storage in the disk log

- **Record contents.** A chunk write and two shards' rounds submitted while another round is in flight go out together in the next record of the hot stream, with one write and one flush: the chunk blocks, then each shard's round as blob payloads. The host reports both rounds done from that record's `Durable` event.
- **Serving entries.** `raft.Storage.Entries(lo, hi, maxSize)` serves every entry after the last compaction from the payload chunks it keeps in memory, with no disk read and no allocation per entry.
  - It returns `ErrCompacted` for lo at or below the compaction index.
  - It honours `maxSize`, returning at least one entry, and allocates for the entries it returns, not the range asked: `Entries(1, 100,001, 1)` over 100,000 entries allocates under 64 KiB, where etcd-raft asks a lagging follower's range up to the last index.
  - `Term(i)` returns `ErrCompacted` below the first index and `ErrUnavailable` past the last, as etcd-raft's `MemoryStorage` does.
  - A hi past last + 1 is a broken invariant of the caller.
  - `FirstIndex` and `LastIndex` are consistent with `Entries`.
  - Chunks start at the larger of 4 KiB and the payload and double up to 64 KiB; a compaction drops the chunks only compacted entries used, keeps those the rest still read, and frees every chunk once no payload is left (`TestCompactionFreesChunks`).
- **Round blobs.** A round larger than a log record goes out as several blobs of at most a record each, every one but the last a `BlobRaftEntries` and the last a `BlobRaftState`, and the host reports it done only once its last blob is durable. A round the pool has no buffers for waits, and goes out on the next `Durable` event once buffers are back, after a round submitted meanwhile; with nothing in flight it goes out when the driver's timer retries it. Fuzzed: a round record decodes only when it encodes back to the same bytes, and replays the same in one blob as cut into several.
- **Compaction.** Once the memtable that applied entries up to index i has been flushed, the state machine compacts the shard to i through the host. A round's blobs leave the usage table's live count once every index it holds is at or below i and a later durable round holds a newer hard state; a round without a hard state needs only the compaction. Until then they stay live, and a block two rounds' blobs share stays live until both are dead. A Raft blob reported dead twice is refused, and an open's recount adds the replayed Raft blobs to the owner's chunk counts.
- **Removed replica.** Once a replica reports itself removed, every blob of its rounds is dead, those still in flight once they are durable. Hosting its owner again while one of its rounds is in flight panics, since the new shard would take that round as its own.
- **Replay.** After a crash, each shard's storage is rebuilt by replaying its rounds in LSN order. Later records win: an entry at index 5 of term 3 replaces the earlier record's index 5 of term 2, the earlier record's entries 6 and on of term 2 are dropped, and `LastIndex` after replay is 5. On a recorded base, a later round whose entries all lie at or below the base still drops the entries after it: rounds of 5 to 12 in term 1, then 7 to 8 and 9 to 10 in term 2, replayed on a base of 10, leave `LastIndex` 10. The latest hard state in LSN order wins, and a round restoring a snapshot makes its index, term and configuration the base. The blobs of an owner no shard on the disk claims are dead.
- **Torn tail.** A torn record at the log's tail drops every item in it, chunk writes and Raft blobs alike (the disk log's torn-record tests); no acknowledgment was sent for the round, the leader resends, and no committed entry is lost (the crash run below). A round missing its last blob changes nothing, nor does one missing its first, and the blobs of a round missing its last are dead once replay ends.
  - Regression (seed 5003 of the crash run below): the torn round stays in the log, so the replay after a second crash meets its first blob again just before the rounds written since the first restart. The next round's first blob drops it, rather than the next round being read as its continuation.
- **Crash with rounds in flight.** [property] Three replicas, each on its node's disk log, run under the Raft shard's network faults, cut-off leaders and leadership transfers; a node crashes three times, one at a time, each while its log has a round in flight, landing unflushed writes at random, so a round can be durable with its shard never told, and restarts by replaying its log on the base it booted with. The simulator checks "a committed entry is never lost": the newest applied entry stays held by a majority of the replicas' storages, a crashed replica's as it was until its replay ends, and a restarted replica holds every committed entry it held before its crash; and "a replica keeps its term and vote across a crash": a restarted replica's term is at least its term before the crash, and with the same term it holds the same vote. Each run is done once a value proposed after the last crash is applied, and replays to an identical trace. Over 20 seeds at least one restart replays a round its shard was never told was durable. Planted: a restart that replays nothing breaks the first invariant, and one that forgets its vote the second. `TestCommittedEntriesSurviveCrashesOnTheDiskLog`, 20 seeds in `go test`, 2,000 per commit in the [seed runner](#seed-runner-in-ci); 10,000 seeds passed in 219 s on 2 processes, each under 200 MiB resident.
- **Snapshot at the applied index.** A learner whose log is empty gets a snapshot built when the leader needs one, at its applied index, whose configuration holds the learner, and catches up from it. A snapshot kept from the last compaction, before the learner joined, is refused, and the learner never catches up (planted). A replica cut off and behind the compaction, probed as the leader applies a learner's addition, gets no snapshot then, since the applied index and configuration do not yet hold the change, and gets one holding the learner at the leader's next append. A snapshot sent whole in one message is reported finished a heartbeat later, so a leader whose log compacted past the snapshot probes the follower again rather than wait in `StateSnapshot`, and a follower that refused it gets at most one more a heartbeat.
- **Asynchronous storage writes stay off** (asserted under Raft shard). The two guards that would allow them get their own scenarios when they are built: drop apply work that a restored snapshot covers, and never compact past the durable commit index ([async snapshot apply study](../studies/etcd-raft-async-snapshot-apply/README.md)).

## Raft cost per group

`internal/raftshard`, `cost_test.go`. Three nodes run 1,000 groups each through `Shard` and
`Storage`, every shard of a node sharing its buffer pool, node-pair leases and output, as the
shards of one loop do: 128 B proposals to random groups at 60,000 proposals/s in 1 ms passes, a
10 ms tick, a 100 ms heartbeat, synchronous `Ready`, flushes and network that take no time, and
every storage compacted to its applied index once a second, more often than checkpoints would.
The node-pair leases are never granted, so no group fortifies and no fortification message is
counted. `TestCostPerGroup` fails `go test` past any bar, in about 0.2 s. `BenchmarkCostPerGroup`
reports every row but the written idle group, `load` a pass and `idle` a tick with no proposals,
and runs nightly; a tracked figure 20% worse than measured is a bug. The benchmark is exempt from
the zero-allocation rule for "Benchmarks" by the etcd-raft version pin in `docs/tech-debts.md`,
whose exit condition is this test's bar of 3 allocations per message.

| Measure | Setup | Bar | Measured (M4 Pro) | Spike figure |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Allocations per Raft message | Under load | ≤ 3 | 2.9 | 2.7 |
| Heap per idle group, never written | One second after the elections, per replica | ≤ 4 KiB | 3.1 KiB (3.1 MiB per node) | 2.8 KiB (2.7 MiB per node) |
| Heap per idle group, written | After the load, compacted to its applied index, one second idle | ≤ 4 KiB | 3.2 KiB | Not measured |
| Allocations per proposal | Under load | Tracked | 25, over 8.7 messages | 22.6, over 8.4 |
| CPU per proposal, across its three replicas | Under load | Tracked | 4.2 µs | about 27 µs on a shared VM |
| Collection's share of CPU | Under load, the runtime's estimate | Tracked | 8% | 14% |
| Idle CPU per node, 10 ms tick, not quiesced | 1,000 groups | Tracked | 0.9% of a core | 2 to 8% |

Quiesced groups (0.07% of a core in the multi-raft spike) are phase 13.

## Maelstrom harness

`tools/maelstrom` runs one replica of a single Raft group as a [Maelstrom](https://github.com/jepsen-io/maelstrom) node, and `scripts/maelstrom.sh` runs it under Maelstrom's `lin-kv` workload (`read`, `write`, `cas`) with network partitions, checked linearizable by Maelstrom's checker: the [done-when checkpoint](design.md#learning-project). The adapter is test code off the data path, in ordinary Go: a goroutine reads stdin, and one loop hands each message, or the shard's timer firing, to the node and writes what it sends to stdout.

- **Adapter.** Every node boots the same group, with each Maelstrom node a voter whose replica ID is its place in `node_ids` plus one. A Raft message travels as a Maelstrom message carrying the shard's inline bytes and pool buffer, and the shard runs unchanged behind `OnEvent`, `Propose`, `ReadIndex` and `Durable`. The storage is the process's memory, and each round is reported durable as soon as the shard takes it, since `lin-kv` never crashes a node. The state machine is the harness's own map from key to value, applied from committed entries; `Txn` is the [Shard state machine](#shard-state-machine)'s. The group never compacts or reconfigures, so a snapshot or a removal stops the node. No node-pair lease is ever renewed, so no leader is fortified, and each node's grantor holds its restart wait: no vote is granted in a node's first 4 s.
- **Writes.** A `write` or `cas` is a log entry naming the node that proposed it and its ID there. Every node applies it, and the proposer answers its client once it applies. A follower resends a client's `write` or `cas` to the leader `Shard.Leader` names, as the daemon resends a `Txn` on [`NotLeader`](design.md#metadata-layer-metastore), and relays the answer; the node it resent to proposes it or answers 11, never resending it again. Without the resend, two writes in three fail on 3 nodes, and a 30 s run acknowledged about 40 writes, too few for the planted bug to fail reliably.
- **Error codes.**
  - A `cas` or `read` on an absent key returns error 20 (key does not exist), and a `cas` whose `from` does not match returns 22 (precondition failed).
  - Error 11 (temporarily unavailable, a definite error) is returned only for an op that was never proposed: by a node that names no leader, names itself but cannot propose (as while a leadership transfer runs), or was resent the op and no longer leads.
  - An op proposed and then orphaned by a leader change gets no reply, which Maelstrom's client records as indefinite when it times out.
- **Reads.** Every read goes through ReadIndex, on any node: etcd-raft passes a follower's ReadIndex to its leader, and the node answers once it has applied up to the index a quorum confirmed. A read that is never confirmed, on a node with no leader or a leader cut off from its quorum, gets no reply, which Maelstrom records as a failed read since a read changes nothing. The harness makes no lease reads, as it carries no node-pair lease traffic; the [Leader leases](#leader-leases) tests cover them.
- **Unit tests.** `TestLinKV` routes messages between three nodes in memory: a write before any leader returns 11; on the leader, a `cas` on an absent key returns 20, a write succeeds, a `cas` from the wrong value returns 22 and one from the right value succeeds; on a follower, a `cas` resent to the leader succeeds, a read returns its value and a `cas` from the old value returns 22; a read of an absent key returns 20. `TestOrphanedWrite` cuts the leader off, sends it a write and a read, elects a new leader that takes a write to the same key, heals the cut, and checks that the old leader serves the new value and never answers either request. `TestAReadWaitsUntilItsIndexApplies` hands a node a confirmed read whose index is past what it applied, and checks that it answers only once that index applies. `TestLeaderNamesTheElectedReplica` (`internal/raftshard`) checks that no replica names a leader before an election, and every replica names the elected one after it.
  Maelstrom does not see what these tests check: on 3 nodes, a read answered as soon as its index is confirmed, or with no value, and a write acknowledged before it commits all passed its checker.
- **Pass criterion.** `scripts/maelstrom.sh` downloads Maelstrom v0.2.4 once into `~/.cache/rock-solid/maelstrom` (`$XDG_CACHE_HOME` when set), its archive and jar checked against their pinned hashes, the jar on every run ([tech-debts.md](tech-debts.md#version-pin-maelstrom-v024)), builds the adapter into a temporary directory, and runs `lin-kv` with `--nemesis partition --nemesis-interval 5 --rate 100 --concurrency 2n --time-limit 30` (`TIME_LIMIT` overrides) and a 2 GB Java heap: on 3 nodes and then on 5, each of which must have the workload valid and no checker invalid. Without gnuplot, Maelstrom's latency graphs fail and its overall verdict is unknown, so the script reads each run's `results.edn` ([tech-debts.md](tech-debts.md#workaround-maelstrom-runs-judged-by-their-resultsedn)). Each invocation empties the cache's `store/` and leaves its own runs there. The script takes about 1 minute 45 seconds and needs Java 17 or later. The `maelstrom` workflow runs it in CI on Temurin 17, with the extracted release cached by version, on every push and pull request that changes `internal/raftshard`, `internal/lease`, `internal/core`, `third_party/raft`, `tools/maelstrom`, the script, `go.mod`, `go.sum` or the workflow.
- **Planted bug.** `-stale-reads` serves every read from the node's map at once. The script then runs it on 5 nodes, up to three times, and passes on the first run with the workload invalid. A run fails only when a partition cuts a follower off from a leader that keeps its quorum and takes writes: on 3 nodes a 30 s run caught it in 2 of 4 runs, on 5 nodes in all of 6, and three tries cube the chance of missing it.

Three runs of the script on a Mac mini (M4 Pro), each op count those Maelstrom recorded `ok`:

| Run | 3 nodes: writes, `cas`, reads | 5 nodes: writes, `cas`, reads | 5 nodes, `-stale-reads`, first try |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | 330, 125, 962 | 281, 103, 979 | Invalid |
| 2 | 243, 93, 808 | 316, 125, 921 | Invalid |
| 3 | 322, 119, 849 | 322, 131, 924 | Invalid |

Every 3- and 5-node run had the workload valid, with no checker invalid.

## Shard state machine

**`Txn`: checks first, then writes in order, all or nothing**

| Ops | Expected |
| --- | --- |
| put a=1 | Committed; get a = 1 |
| check a == 1, put a=2 | Committed; a = 2 |
| check a == 1 (a is 2), put a=3, put b=1 | Fails with `FailedCheck` 0 and `Actual` 2. Neither a nor b changes |
| check a absent, put a=1, where a exists | Fails. This is `create`'s `EEXIST` and S3's `if-not-exists` |
| delete a, where a is absent | Committed: a delete of an absent key succeeds, as in CockroachDB, etcd and TiKV; the purger depends on it |
| put a=1, delete a, in one `Txn` | Committed; a is absent. Writes apply in list order |
| check a absent, put a=1, in one `Txn`, where a is absent | Committed: checks see the state before the `Txn`, not its own writes |
| `Update(a, 0, Add, 5)`, `Update(a, 8, Bump, 3)`, put b, delete c, on an absent a | Committed; a's two fields read 5 and 3; `Updated` is [5, 3] |
| `Update(a, 0, Bump, 10)` where the field holds 20 | Field 21: `Bump` stores max(n, field + 1) |
| `Update(a, 0, Add, 1)` where the field holds 2^64 − 1 | Field 0: `Add` wraps |
| `CheckEmpty(d/, PrefixEnd(d/))` over a directory with one entry, then after that entry's delete | Fails, then passes. `rmdir` of a non-empty directory fails with `ENOTEMPTY` |
| `DeleteRange(k1, k3)` over k1, k2, k3 | k1 and k2 removed, k3 kept: the range is half-open |
| A key of 1,033 bytes, or a value of 1,001 bytes | Refused with an error before proposing, never a panic (`MaxKey` 1,032, `MaxValue` 1,000) |
| A `DeleteRange` or `CheckEmpty` bound of 1,001 bytes, or a start not below its end | Refused before proposing; a bound of 1,000 bytes commits |
| A `Txn` with a replay key and 125 `Update`s | Refused before proposing; 124 commit, and their record fits `MaxValue` |
| An op carrying a field its kind does not encode (a `CheckEmpty` marked absent, a `Put` marked final), or an oldest-outstanding value without a replay key | Refused before proposing: an entry decoded differently from what its leader checked would fail that `Txn` and every later one in the entry on every replica. [property] Every `Txn` that passes the check, its fields drawn at random, decodes from its encoding to itself (`TestCheckedTxnsDecodeToThemselves`) |
| A `Txn` encoding to more than 256 KiB (`max_txn_bytes`), as an 82 KiB xattr in pieces fits and 1 MiB does not; one of only `ctl/` keys to more than 896 KiB (`max_ctl_txn_bytes`), as 800 KiB fits unless it names one other key | Refused before proposing with a size error, never split |
| Empty ops | An error |
| Two racing `Txn`s, each check a absent, put a=x | Exactly one commits (the design's lock-race example) |
| 64 concurrent `create`s in one directory, distinct names, inodes from each daemon's reservation | All commit in one round with distinct inodes; no check fails, since the parent's times move by `Update` |
| 1,000 `create`s in one directory over 100 rounds | All commit without one failed check |
| A `create` from a node whose clock is 10 s behind the directory's `mtime` | The parent's `mtime` still moves forward by 1 ns |

**`Scan(start, end, limit)`**

| Keys | Call | Expected |
| --- | --- | --- |
| a, aa, ab, abc, b | Scan(a, PrefixEnd(a), 10) | a, aa, ab, abc; `more` false |
| Same | Scan(ab, PrefixEnd(ab), 10) | ab, abc |
| Same | Scan(aa + 0x00, PrefixEnd(a), 10) | ab, abc: "after aa" is `start` = aa + 0x00 |
| Same | Scan(a, PrefixEnd(a), 2) | a, aa, `more` true; then Scan(aa + 0x00, PrefixEnd(a), 2) gives ab, abc, `more` false |
| Same | Scan(zz, PrefixEnd(a), 10) | Empty (start past end) |
| Same | Scan(c, PrefixEnd(c), 10) | Empty |
| Same | limit 0 | An error, since an unbounded reply would allocate without bound |
| Same | Scan(k, k + 0x00, 1) | The point read of k |
| Keys and values totalling 1 MiB | Scan with limit 10,000 | Stops at 256 KiB (`max_scan_bytes`) with `more` true; resuming from the last key + 0x00 returns the rest |
| A key of `MaxKey` bytes | Resume from it + 0x00 | Accepted: a scan bound of `MaxKey` + 1 bytes is never stored |
| 1,000 directory entries under one directory | Scan of the directory's `d/` prefix | All 1,000 in name order, from one point-in-time view, while writes continue |

**Rounds and reads**

- **One log entry per leader per round.** 100 `Txn`s arriving at a leader during one round become one Raft entry. The trace shows one entry per round.
- **Reads never wait for writers.** A scan's reply is read from the state in one call and copied into the caller's buffer, so the 1,000 puts that commit after it change neither the state it read nor the reply.
- **Answers.** A leader answers each `Txn` it proposed as it applies its entry. A follower refuses a `Txn` with `ErrProposalDropped`; a leader cut off with two `Txn`s proposed answers both dropped once it applies the new leader's first entry, and neither applies anywhere, while a deposed leader's entry the next leader committed is answered with its result, as it applies under its own term. A deposed leader that catches up by a snapshot answers its waiting `Txn`s dropped at the restore, and a replica told it was removed answers its waiting and gathered ones dropped at once. Each of these fails with its plant: dropping by the replica's term instead of the entry's, no answers at a restore.
- **Restarts.** A replica restarted on a storage rebuilt from its rounds' records rebuilds the same state, from its boot base and from a snapshot it restored, whose data the replay keeps for the state machine.
- **An entry a replica cannot decode.** A follower whose newest entry format is older than an entry's halts at it: its applied index stays before the entry and its compaction point does not pass it, it reports the entry's index, refuses `Txn`s and scans with `ErrHalted`, and halts at the same entry after a restart, while the other replicas keep committing. A leader that halts answers its `Txn`s from the entry on dropped and hands its leadership to another voter, under which the next `Txn` commits. Both fail when the replica skips the entry instead, and the compaction point when it is the Raft replica's applied index. An entry whose first `Txn` decodes and whose second does not halts every replica before it, and none applies the first, which a replica decoding `Txn` by `Txn` would.
- **A halted replica acts as a down one.** A halted follower's log stops growing while the other two commit five more `Txn`s; cut from its leader for three election timeouts it stays at its term, campaigning in no election; told it was removed, it reports itself removed. Its leader, probing it behind its compaction, sends it a snapshot, which it does not restore, and it fails with the plant that lets a snapshot through. A halted leader probing a follower behind its compaction builds the snapshot without data, which the follower refuses; one built from its state would be asked at an index its state never reached. When all three replicas halt at one entry, with the clock standing still for 200 rounds of deliveries and flushes, the term rises by at most three, where handing leadership on after every call raised it by 66.
- **A replay key holding no record.** A client may write any key; a `Txn` whose replay key holds a value that is no record answers `ErrMalformed` and changes nothing, and the oracle property writes replay keys with ordinary ops.
- **[property]** Txns against an oracle (`TestTxnsMatchTheOracle`): 300 random `Txn`s per seed over six keys, every op kind and mode, half of them under replay keys of three mounts with random oldest-outstanding values, applied through their log encoding; each result and the whole state, replay records decoded, equal a map-based model's after every `Txn`.
- **[property]** Replayed requests (`TestReplayedRequestsReturnTheirFirstFinalResult`): requests of three mounts, each resent 0 to 3 times at random later points with honest oldest-outstanding values; a resend of a request whose result was final returns that result and leaves the state byte for byte as it was, and a result that was not final leaves no record. The planted bugs "a replay record ignored" and "a check failure that is not final stored as the request's result" each fail within 20 seeds.
- **Fuzzing.** The `Txn` decoder (a `Txn` that decodes is within the limits, encodes back to the same bytes and applies without a panic), the snapshot data decoder (`CheckSnapshot` accepts exactly what restores, and a refused snapshot leaves the state as it was) and the replay record decoder.
- **Snapshot data at the handed-over index.** A snapshot the Raft shard builds in the step that hands entries over to apply carries the state machine's contents with every one of them applied, since `Config.SnapshotData` is called with the last index handed over and `Config.Apply` hands them over within the call. A leader whose durable round hands over an entry and commits the next, probing a follower cut off behind its compaction, builds the snapshot in that call and the follower restores the leader's state; a state machine that applies only once the call returns has the snapshot asked at an index it has not reached.
- **Consumed lists.** A purge list consumed in key order has each consumed run removed by one `DeleteRange` op in a `Txn`, so it replicates like every other write and a seek to the queue's head steps over 1 removal, against 10,820 point removals in the LSM deletions study.
- **Benchmarks** (bars from the KV engines and MetaStore memory spikes): a get from a shard of 10 million files at about 1 µs (0.96 to 1.00 µs from the memtable in the spike), and no slower than redb's 7.2 µs; a 1,000-entry listing no slower than redb's 196 µs in the [KV engines spike](design.md#appendix-kv-engines-spike). Measured on a 14-core Apple M4 Pro, from the memtable, with no allocation per operation: a point read `Scan(k, k + 0x00, 1)` takes 509 ns among 10 million files (1.1 GiB resident) and 431 ns among 1 million; a create's decode and apply 750 ns; a 1,000-entry listing 30 µs, which passes: the memtable iterator's seek and 1,000 steps take 26 µs (about 26 ns a step), and copying the keys and values into the reply in one pass the other 4 µs. `BenchmarkScanListing` stays as the regression guard.

Recovery from manifest and log is under Shard indexes in the disk owner's checkpoint and MetaStore invariants. Bytes per file are under the LSM tree item.

## Shard indexes in the disk owner's checkpoint

- **Replay LSN per shard.** A shard's replay LSN is the older of its oldest live round's LSN and its memtable's start, and the disk owner's checkpoint names it beside the chunk index's. An idle shard whose newest hard-state round holds its replay LSN behind gets that hard state written again in a new round at the next checkpoint, after which the old round's blobs die and the replay LSN moves on. A deleted shard whose oldest live round holds an entry past its commit is written again whole with its deletion flag, so a crash after the rewrite kills the deletion round restarts it deleted, with every entry and its hard state; a rewrite without the flag brings it back (`TestAFullRewriteOfADeletedShardKeepsItDeleted`).
- **Bound.** [property] A shard takes no new entries once it retains its share of twice `max_replay_bytes`, counting its rounds its storage has not taken, so a disk's retained entries never exceed twice `max_replay_bytes` (128 MiB at the default 64 MiB). A follower shard on a chunk store whose leader is gone keeps being sent entries it cannot commit while chunk writes go over the disk three times: it retains no more than its share and a round; each checkpoint writes its entries again, so the replay floor moves past its rounds and every chunk write is answered, where before the store stopped with no free segment at the 254th of 1,536; a restart every 500 writes keeps every entry it acknowledged; and once its leader is back it applies them all and, after the checkpoint the store takes for it, is full no more (`TestAStuckFollowerShardNeverStallsChunkWrites`). Over seeds (`scripts/seeds.sh`), three shards beside chunk writes that go over the disk twice, one a follower whose leader is gone, are sent bursts of 1 to 6 rounds while the store does not report them full, their durable rounds reach them up to 12 pumps late, and the store crashes every 256 chunk writes: each retains at most its share and a round, checked right after each burst and again after the steps that follow, and every chunk write is answered. Right after a restart a shard holds at most twice that, and until it compacts again no more than it restarted with, since its restored base predates its last compaction (`TestRaftShardsRetainAtMostTheirShare`).
  - Regression (seed 0): a shard told late of its durable rounds retained past its share, since the store counted such a round neither in flight nor in the shard's storage and let the shard take more (`TestAShardToldLateOfItsRoundsKeepsWithinItsShare`).
  - Regression: a stuck follower that keeps taking one-entry rounds under its bound, while chunk writes drive due checkpoints and the store crashes every 100 writes, keeps every entry it acknowledged; its round durable in the handler that begins a checkpoint is not yet in its storage, so the full rewrite waits for the shard to take it, where before the rewrite left the round's entries out and a restart failed with a malformed round (`TestAStuckFollowerTakingRoundsKeepsThemAcrossRestarts`, and at the host `TestAFullRewriteWaitsForTheShardToTakeEveryDurableRound`).
  - A full rewrite larger than the pool has free goes out a few blobs at a time as buffers free, a compaction waiting until it has read the entries, and a shard after it still gets its own rewrite: both floors move on and a restart recovers every entry and hard state, where before the rewrite asked for every buffer at once, found none and skipped every later shard (`TestAFullRewriteLargerThanThePoolGoesOutAsBuffersFree`).
  - A round written while a full rewrite goes out waits behind it: a crash after each step of the two, with and without the cleaner reclaiming dead blobs, recovers every entry and hard state the shard was told durable and never a part of the rewrite, where a held round sent at once splits the rewrite and its close kills everything (`TestARoundHeldBehindAFullRewriteSurvivesACrashAtEveryPoint`).
  - A shard's retained bytes are its storage's payload and its rounds the storage has not taken, in flight or durable (`TestRetainedCountsTheStorageAndTheRoundsNotTaken`); an append keeps the entries the storage holds at the same index and term, replaces from the first conflict, and one matching every entry ends the storage at its last (`TestAppendKeepsMatchingEntriesAndReplacesFromAConflict`).
- **Backpressure.** Retained Raft entries count toward the hold of [Checkpoint backpressure](#checkpoint-backpressure): a seed with a stalled checkpoint holds Raft rounds as it holds chunk writes, and keeps the retained entries under the bound.
- **Replay floor.** A shard idle while chunk writes make the disk checkpoint many times keeps the log's replay floor at or before its oldest live round, and a crash then replays every round it still needs.
- **Blob owners.** The checkpoint records each shard's blob owner, and a restart hosts each shard under it. A removed shard's owner goes to no new shard while a round of it is in flight (the host panics) or its blobs can still replay. A shard removed from the round driver keeps its owner from a new shard until a segment header names a manifest begun after the removal: neither the checkpoint running at the removal nor a later manifest no header names yet frees it (`TestARemovedRemoteOwnerIsReusableOnceAManifestLeavingItOutIsNamed`).
- **Removal.** A shard `Store.RemoveRaft` removes stays removed: a crash before the checkpoint after the removal, whose manifest still names it, and one after it, once the segments of its tree's pieces are freed, both restart without it and with the other shard whole; its owner goes to no new shard until the replay floor passes its blobs, and a new shard given its owner then restarts with its own entries alone. It fails without the host's removal or without its pieces reported dead (`TestARemovedShardStaysRemovedAcrossACrash`). Its tree's pieces stay live until the checkpoint after the removal ends: on a log whose `max_replay_bytes` spans two segments, so a segment header names the last manifest before that checkpoint does, every segment holding them keeps its live blocks at each step until then, and a crash at the last step before it ends restarts the shard, added again, with all it had applied; reported dead at the removal, a segment lost them at the first step (`TestARemovedShardsPiecesStayLiveUntilAManifestLeavesItOut`). It refuses an owner not hosted or already being removed with `ErrNotHosted` (`TestRemoveRaftRefusesAnOwnerNotHosted`). A removed tree's merge frees its worker for another tree's (`TestARemovedTreesMergeFreesItsWorker`), and a step of it handed out before the removal is refused with `ErrStale` at its install, leaving the tree's runs as they were, where before it installed into the removed tree (`TestAMergeOfARemovedTreeIsStale`).
- **Restore.** After a crash, a shard restores from its manifest's runs, its base (the index, term and configuration of its last compaction) with them, and replays the log after its replay LSN. Its host's compaction index restores from that base, so a round compacted before the crash is dead after it and one holding an index past the base is live. The crash oracle compares the recovered shard with its state at the last acknowledged LSN.
- **Crash with compaction and cleaning.** [property] The [crash run with rounds in flight](#raft-storage-in-the-disk-log), with each shard compacting once its applied entries are flushed, the cleaner freeing segments whose blobs the hosts reported dead, and each restart replaying from its recorded replay LSN on its recorded base, holds the same invariants. Unlike that run, which never compacts or cleans and replays every blob, dead or live, it fails if a blob reported dead was still needed. It also registers [MetaStore invariants](#metastore-invariants)' "a shard recovered from manifest and log equals its state before the crash".
- **Shards on a chunk store.** [property] Two single-voter shards on a store's log, whose entry
  `i` puts its index under key `i mod 40`, write 2,000 rounds of 1 to 8 entries of 1 to 8 KB on a
  disk of 32 segments of 128 blocks with `max_replay_bytes` 64 blocks, crashing every 50 rounds
  with unflushed writes landing at random, over seeds (`scripts/seeds.sh`). Each restart holds
  every entry committed before the crash, and its state is the one its applied index leaves;
  restarts restore compacted bases, each seed writes the disk over twice, and the crashes land
  with no checkpoint running, with a piece in flight and with the manifest in flight, each
  counted (`TestRaftShardsOnTheStoreCheckpointCompactAndRecover`).
  - Regression (seed 8): a restart's replay adds again every Raft blob past the replay floor,
    those reported dead before the manifest included, so the host reports them dead only after
    the log recounts its usage; reported before, the report underflowed a segment's live count
    and every open of the disk panicked (`TestARestartReportsBlobsDeadAfterTheLogRecounts`).
  - A checkpoint begun for a merge step alone names each shard with the replay LSN of the last
    due checkpoint that ended, the one its carried runs restore: naming it with the host's current
    one, past a compaction the runs' mark predates, restored a shard at an applied index with none
    of its entries after the base, and the next compaction panicked. A due checkpoint that fails
    leaves that LSN as it was (`TestAFailedDueCheckpointKeepsTheShardsReplayLSN`).
  - The cleaner rewrites the runs of every tree with a live piece in a metadata victim, so a
    segment holding only a shard's pieces is freed once they move; asking the chunk index's tree
    alone skipped it for good (`TestTheCleanerFreesASegmentHoldingOnlyShardPieces`).
  - A shard added while a checkpoint runs joins the next one, and a restart after it restores the
    shard on a compacted base; the running checkpoint once asked its tree for pieces of a flush it
    never began, which stopped the store (`TestAShardAddedDuringACheckpointJoinsTheNext`).
- **Shards on the round driver.** A restart of a disk whose shard moved to the round driver mails
  it, in order, only its blobs past its replay LSN, though another shard's older round keeps its
  dead ones in the replay, then the end of the replay, and a `raftshard.Rounds` on the base taking
  them rebuilds its storage and reports nothing dead (`TestARestartMailsAShardOnTheRoundDriverItsLiveRounds`).
  A store that knows a shard on the round driver stops on a broken index rather than draining its
  log for a rebuild (`TestABrokenIndexStopsAStoreWithAShardOnTheRoundDriver`), and stops with
  `ErrNoSpace` when its log is out of room (`TestAStoreWithAShardOnTheRoundDriverStopsOutOfRoom`).
  A shard reports the LSN before the oldest blob of its live rounds, once each time it moves
  (`TestRoundsReplayRebuildsTheStorage`). Until its first report a checkpoint names it with the
  durable LSN when it was added, before every blob it writes, and after a restart with the LSN
  the loaded manifest gave it (`TestAShardOnTheRoundDriverIsNamedBeforeItsFirstReport`).
  Checkpoints made due every few rounds, while such shards on the device loop and on another loop
  write thirty rounds each, and then, the shards idle, the due checkpoints and merge steps of
  chunk writes, name both with the replay LSN each reported: the replay floor moves, yet after
  every step stays before the oldest blob either still needs, though the index's replay LSN
  passes it; idle, each compacts on the mail of a due checkpoint's durable manifest and writes its
  hard state again, so the floor passes every blob it held when it went idle; and a restart
  recovers both storages whole. Leaving them out of the due or the merge steps' checkpoints moved
  the floor past a live blob, and without the mail, the compaction on it or the rewrite the floor
  stayed at an idle shard's oldest round (`TestCheckpointsNameTheShardsOnTheRoundDriver`). Idle,
  its oldest round compacted and holding its newest hard state, a `raftshard.Rounds` writes that
  hard state again in a round of its own, which the replica is never told of, whose durability
  kills the old round and moves its replay LSN, the replica's next round waiting behind it;
  holding entries past its commit, it writes every entry again at most four blobs a `Ready`, a
  compaction waiting until the rewrite has read them, and the blobs left replay into the storage
  it holds; a rewrite whose batch fails stops there, its durable blobs dead, the waiting
  compaction done, and the old round live and replaying into the storage, until a later
  `Rewrite` (`TestRoundsRewriteWhatHoldsTheFloorBack`). It is full once it retains the share its
  owner mailed, never before one arrives, and asks for a checkpoint once per commit it applied
  while full (`TestRoundsAreFullAtTheShareTheOwnerMailed`). The store mails a shard on the round
  driver beside a hosted one half of twice `max_replay_bytes`, the hosted one's share too; asked
  for a checkpoint, it takes one though none is due, and mails its durable manifest with the base
  of the due one before; a step checkpoint mails nothing, and a third shard has both mailed the
  new share, a third (`TestAStoreMailsAShardOnTheRoundDriverItsShareAndCheckpoints`). Asked from
  the `Mail` of a shard on either loop, the device loop's or another's, an idle store, which
  nothing else wakes, takes the checkpoint, has both shards flush their trees under it and mails
  both; the shard on the device loop does so alone too, the round trips of its pieces then the
  only events. The owner not delivering the mail it sends at the nil event of a reply, or not
  handing it another while shards on its loop reply, left the checkpoint waiting for good
  (`TestAFullShardGetsACheckpointFromAnIdleStore`). Each shard, its tree flushed under due
  checkpoints and compacted to the index it applied at its mark as each manifest is mailed
  durable, restarts after the last compaction with no checkpoint since: it restores its state
  and its storage's base from the runs the manifest names and then its rounds from the log, equal
  to its state before. The manifest naming no runs for it lost its state, and the checkpoint
  ending before its pieces left it none (`TestAShardOnTheRoundDriverRestoresFromItsRunsAfterItCompacts`). Restarted, checkpointed and restarted again, it recovers its state: the owner keeps the runs the loaded manifest named for the checkpoints after, and with them dropped the second restart lost the state (`TestAShardOnTheRoundDriverKeepsItsLoadedRunsAcrossASecondRestart`). The store knowing two shards before their loop
  adds them, the shares it mails as they change wait on the loop, the newest standing for the one
  before, and reach the first once added (`TestMailForAShardNotYetOnItsLoopWaitsForIt`). The shard on the
  other loop, removed with a round in flight, and then the one on the device loop: the store hears each removal with the
  LSN of its newest blob, the round in flight's for the first, and gives neither owner to a new
  shard until checkpoints move the floor past it; a new shard given the first owner then restarts
  with its own rounds alone (`TestARemovedShardsOwnerOnTheRoundDriverWaitsForTheFloor`). A
  removed shard that reports a replay LSN or its removal again panics, since either could reach
  a new shard given its owner (`TestARemovedShardRepliesNothingMore`). The shard on the other
  loop, taken off it part way through its tree's flush and its removal heard by the store only
  after the next checkpoint, as its loop holds the reply while backpressure holds its batches:
  both checkpoints, which ask it for pieces it can no longer reply, end, the loop answering on its
  behalf; without that answer the first never ended
  (`TestARemovedShardsRunsStayLiveUntilAManifestLeavesItOut`). A shard on the round driver
  removed part way through its flush keeps its pieces, its runs' and the flush's written before
  and after the removal, until the checkpoint begun after the removal ends, which reports them
  dead, and the log holds them no more once a segment header names its manifest; reporting them
  dead at the removal or at the end of the checkpoint running then, losing the flush's pieces, or
  never reporting them failed it, and so did mailing `MailCheckpointed` only after a checkpoint
  begun with something durable, which lost the first flush's run
  (`TestARemovedRemoteShardsPiecesDieOnceAManifestLeavesItOut`). A shard on the round driver
  whose merge since the last manifest left one of its runs bounded and the other out names the
  runs its flush carries: that checkpoint's manifest names them, the merge bound and the run the
  flush wrote, and so does a checkpoint begun before its next flush; with the owner ignoring the
  reply, or keeping the old bounds, it failed (`TestAShardOnTheRoundDriverNamesTheRunsItsFlushCarries`).
  The shards on both loops merge their runs in steps on their own loops until a manifest names a
  merge part way, then stop, and chunk writes make more checkpoints due: every piece their merges
  left out is gone from the log once a segment header names a manifest begun after their reports,
  and a restart mails each the runs, and bounds, its newest named manifest names; with the owner
  dropping nothing on the report a merged-away piece stayed live, and with the bounds left off the
  mail a bounded run failed to load (`TestAShardOnTheRoundDriverMergesItsRuns`). The process
  crashing as soon as a segment header names the manifest of a flush that carried other runs than
  the manifest before, before any later manifest is durable, restores exactly the runs and bounds
  that flush named; with the owner recording the shard's runs without rewriting the running
  manifest, the restart got the runs the manifest before named, without the bounds
  (`TestACrashRightAfterAManifestNamesAShardsMergedRunsRestoresThem`). After a restart, until its
  flush names its runs again, a checkpoint names a shard on the round driver with the bounds the
  loaded manifest named; with the host dropping them on the load it failed
  (`TestALoadedManifestNamesAShardsRunsWithTheirBounds`). The cleaner rewrites the runs of a
  shard on the round driver in an idle store: after the shards on both loops flush and merge
  under due checkpoints and chunk writes move the replay floor past segments holding only their
  run pieces, a restart with the cleaner wanting more free segments than the disk has, the shards
  making no rounds and nothing writing, has each shard rewrite the runs the cleaner mails it and
  report every old piece dead, with no checkpoint due; their segments free only once chunk writes
  open a segment whose header names the manifest after, and the storages recover whole. With the store weighing no
  shard's runs, or mailing no rewrite, the cleaner marked none, and with the shard not asking for
  a checkpoint for its steps the rewrite stopped at its first
  (`TestAnIdleStoreRewritesTheRunsOfAShardOnTheRoundDriver`). Pieces a shard on the round driver
  reports dead make an idle store begin a checkpoint, and die once a header names its manifest;
  its runs' table makes a cleaner that found no victim at the durable LSN look again, and weighs
  and mails a victim holding them, but never picks one where the shard's merge holds a run.
  Without the checkpoint the manifest never moved, without the look the cleaner stayed idle, and
  with the shard's held runs ignored it picked the segment
  (`TestAShardOnTheRoundDriversDeadPiecesAndRunsReachAnIdleStore`). The table weighs every
  segment as the tree's own `RunsIn` and `RewriteSteps` do, through a rewrite in steps and in a
  tree restored from a manifest that bounds the run part way; with a running merge's pieces left
  out, or a bounded run's dead pieces kept, it did not (`TestRewriteMarkedRun`). The end-to-end restart is under [Round driver](#round-driver).
  - [property] Shards on the device loop and on another retain at most their share of twice
    `max_replay_bytes` and a round, counted as each one's storage and the rounds it proposed
    that its storage has not taken, at every step of bursts of 1 to 6 rounds of 1 to 8 entries
    of 64 to 8,000 bytes, each proposed only while `Rounds.Full` says the shard is not, beside
    chunk writes, with every round told durable reaching its storage only at a later event of its
    loop; each shard is full at times and proposes four times its share, and the store keeps
    serving, over seeds (`scripts/seeds.sh`). With `Full` counting only the storage it passed
    the bound, and with the share divided over the hosted shards alone the shards were mailed
    twice theirs (`TestShardsOnTheRoundDriverRetainAtMostTheirShare`).
  - [property] Shards on the device loop and on another make bursts of rounds of those sizes
    beside chunk writes, 1,000 of the two, on a 1 GiB disk whose 256 KiB segments are large
    enough for a run's rewrite to free room, while due checkpoints flush their trees and their
    merges' steps, they compact on the mail and the cleaner wants all but 8 segments free, and
    the process crashes every 50, a third of the time once it settles, with unflushed writes
    landing at random, over seeds (`scripts/seeds.sh`). Each shard, when its replay ends, equals
    its state before the crash with or without the round it had in flight: hard state, entries
    from the first it held, or from the older base its runs restore, and its tree's state at the
    same applied index. Over the seeds restarts restore compacted bases and replay past blobs
    reported dead; a shard is at crashes with no flush of it running, with a piece of it in
    flight, and with every piece durable and the manifest not yet mailed durable; the shards
    merge and rewrite runs the cleaner marked; and the cleaner frees segments that held their
    dead blobs and their dead run pieces. With the replay LSN a shard reports one later, a
    checkpoint naming it with the durable LSN, or a restart skipping its first blob past the
    loaded manifest's replay LSN, a restart lost entries; with the running manifest naming the runs
    its begin named rather than those the flush carries, a restart loaded a dead piece
    (`TestShardsOnTheRoundDriverCheckpointCompactAndRecover`).
- **Lagging follower.** A follower behind the compaction index gets a `MsgSnap` built from a point-in-time view of the shard's LSM tree, which never blocks the writer, and catches up from it. A view held open holds back the cleaner (asserted in the LSM tree tests).
- **Index rebuild.** One index rebuilds from its manifest and the log while the disk's other indexes serve, without restarting the log.

## Key encoding

**Rules.** Each path component `word/` is a one-byte tag. Integers are fixed-width and big-endian:

- volume IDs, 32 bits;
- inode IDs, 64 bits: a 24-bit slot and a 40-bit sequence;
- session IDs and request IDs, 64 bits; mount IDs, 32 bits;
- table epochs and snapshot epochs, 64 bits; a lock mode, 8 bits.

Only the last component (a file name, an xattr name, an S3 key, or what follows a `ctl/` tag other than a session's) has variable length, with no escaping and no terminator.

- Key space 0 is the state's own: a `Txn` with a key or range start there is refused with `ErrBadOp` (`TestLimitsAreCheckedBeforeProposing`), and a `Scan` from nil or from the mark's key after a `Mark` starts at the first client key (`TestScan`).

- The run filters' inode prefix `T(fs) volume inode` has a fixed length, so every key under an inode has the same prefix and a shorter key has none, as `lsm.Config.Prefix` requires; a prefix taken up to a delimiter would not be (`fs/2/` starts `fs/23/a`).

**Tags**, from the [key layout](design.md#metadata-layer-metastore): first byte `0x01` ctl, `0x02` volume, `0x03` fs, `0x04` s3; under `ctl/` `0x01` pool, `0x02` placement table, `0x03` membership, `0x04` session, `0x05` format level, `0x06` shard map; under `volume/{id}/` `0x01` attach, `0x02` snap; an inode's keys `0x01` a, `0x02` x, `0x03` t, `0x04` l, `0x05` d, `0x06` c, `0x07` P; a slot's keys `0x10` n, `0x11` u, `0x12` o, `0x13` p, `0x14` r, `0x15` f; a piece key is its value's tag with the high bit set (`0x82`, `0x83`), then a 1-byte piece number from 1; lock modes `0x01` s, `0x02` x.

**Golden vectors.** `internal/meta/testdata/key_golden.txt` holds one key of every tag and lock mode, frozen as disk format: the test encodes each key to its line's bytes and decodes the bytes back, and never writes the file. Among them:

| Key | Bytes |
| --- | --- |
| `fs/5/2:1/a` | `03 00000005 0000020000000001 01` |
| `fs/5/2:1/d/beach.jpg` | `03 00000005 0000020000000001 05 62656163682e6a7067` |
| `fs/5/2:0/n` (slot counters of slot 2) | `03 00000005 0000020000000000 10` |
| `fs/5/2:0/p/{2:9}` | `03 00000005 0000020000000000 13 0000020000000009` |
| Root directory's attributes in volume 1 | `03 00000001 0000000000000001 01` |
| `volume/5/snap/{epoch 3}` | `02 00000005 02 0000000000000003` |
| `ctl/session/{7}` | `01 04 0000000000000007` |
| Replay key, volume 5, slot 2, session 7, mount 1, request 42 | `03 00000005 0000020000000000 14 0000000000000007 00000001 000000000000002a`, 34 bytes |
| `fs/5/2:3/l/x/{session 7}` | `03 00000005 0000020000000003 04 02 0000000000000007` |
| Piece 2 of xattr `user.big` on 2:3 | `03 00000005 0000020000000003 82 02 757365722e626967` |
| The largest volume and inode | `03 ffffffff ffffffffffffffff 01` |

**Order.**

- [property] `TestKeyByteOrderIsLogicalOrder`, 10,000 seeds of 200 pairs: for random pairs of keys of every kind, with fields at their bounds and names of 0x00, 0x01, 0x7f, 0x80 and 0xff bytes, byte order equals logical order (components compared left to right, integers numerically, the last component bytewise), and each key decodes back to itself.
- Fixed order: volume 255 < volume 256, where a decimal string would not keep it; `fs/5/2:0/n` < `fs/5/2:1/a` < `fs/5/2:1/d/\x01` < `fs/5/2:1/d/beach.jpg` < `fs/5/2:1/d/cat.jpg` < `fs/5/2:1/d/cat.jpg\xff` < `fs/5/2:2/a` < `fs/5/3:0/n` < `fs/6/1:0/n`, so every key of slot 2 sorts before every key of slot 3 and a shard can split between slots; S3 keys `a` < `a\x00` < `a/`.
- On a shard holding an inode's keys of every kind and its neighbours' keys, a prefix scan of `fs/5/2:3/d/` returns its directory entries only, and a scan from `fs/5/2:3/a` through the end of `fs/5/2:3/x/` its attributes and xattrs only, no piece key.

**Errors.** `MakeInode` refuses a slot ≥ 2^24 or a sequence ≥ 2^40. `DecodeKey` refuses each of these as `ErrBadKey`, never a panic, and `AppendKey` refuses a `Key` that would encode to one, leaving its buffer as it was:

- an empty or truncated key, or one over `MaxKey`;
- an unknown space, tag or lock mode, and a piece tag of a value other than x and t;
- a missing fixed-width field;
- trailing bytes after a fixed-width last component;
- a slot tag at a sequence other than 0, and an inode or piece tag at sequence 0;
- piece number 0, and a piece tag with no number;
- a directory entry, folded name, xattr or S3 key with an empty name.

[fuzz] `FuzzDecodeKey`: bytes that decode encode back to the same bytes.

**Replay keys.** A `Txn` whose replay key is not a key under the replay tag, a purge entry's key or one with no tags, is refused with `ErrBadReplay` before proposing, so the range its apply removes below `Oldest` holds only that mount's records. The refusal of client writes to replay-tagged keys is a [Sharded API](#sharded-api-one-shard) scenario.

**Limits and pieces.**

- An S3 key of 1,024 bytes gives an index key of 1,029 bytes, within `MaxKey` (1,032); an S3 index key over `MaxKey` is refused. A 1,025-byte S3 key is refused at the frontend.
- A value is a head of its piece count and its first 999 bytes, then pieces of 1,000 bytes but the last: 999 bytes are 1 value, 1,000 are 2, 2,000 are 3, a 4,095-byte symlink target 5 and a 64 KiB xattr 66, in one `Txn` of about 82 KiB; each splits and joins back whole with 1 + m lookups. A value over 64 KiB is refused.
- Names over 255 bytes, xattr names over 255, symlink targets over 4,095 and xattr values over 64 KiB are refused at the frontend, before any `Txn`.
- [fuzz] `FuzzPieces`: the reader refuses a missing piece, a short head or inner piece, a long or empty last piece, a last piece that takes the value past 64 KiB (65 full pieces after a full head), a piece count past 65 and a piece past the count, as errors; a head and pieces it joins are the split of the value they join to.

**Allocation.** Encoding and decoding a key, and checking a `Txn`'s replay key, allocate nothing (`testing.AllocsPerRun`).

## MetaStore replica on the round driver

On the round driver's store rig, a `meta.RoundShard` on the device loop and one on another loop, each the single voter of a group of its own, `Txn`s each putting a value under a key of its own; or the two in one group, the replica on the other loop its voter and the one on the device loop a learner that joins with empty storage, their messages handed from loop to loop.

- **Checkpoints and restart.** Both replicas take 160 `Txn`s while checkpoints come due: each compacts past its boot base, and idle it holds no merge step that no manifest names, has replied the runs its tree holds as the cleaner weighs them, and has reported dead pieces its merges left out, which the log holds no more once chunk writes have made a segment header name a later manifest; those writes move the replay floor past every blob the replicas held when they went idle. Mailed to rewrite the runs with a piece in a segment, a replica rewrites them and asks for a checkpoint to name the rewrite. A restart restores each from the runs and blobs its store mails it, on a compacted base, with every `Txn` it answered, and it replies the restored runs as the cleaner weighs them before a checkpoint flushes it; without the merge pass after the restart it replied them only once its first flush began. Without the compaction at `MailCheckpointed`, the rewrite of what holds the floor back, the base the runs restore, the dead pieces' reply, the costs' reply, the mark of the cleaner's runs or the ask for a checkpoint on an unnamed step, it failed (`TestMetaShardsOnTheRoundDriverRecoverTheirState`).
- **Held full by a stuck checkpoint.** The store learns of a shard on the replica's loop that the loop does not add, so every due checkpoint waits for its pieces: the replica takes `Txn`s until it retains its share, then refuses them with `meta.ErrOverloaded`, applying none, drops a Raft append of a higher term sent to it, and the store goes on serving; once the shard is added the checkpoint ends and compacts the replica, which takes `Txn`s again, and a restart finds every `Txn` it answered and none it refused. Without the refusal it took them all and none was refused; without the drop the append moved its term (`TestAMetaShardHeldFullByAStuckCheckpoint`). Restarted while held full, it restores what no checkpoint compacted from the blobs mailed to it, with every `Txn` it answered; ignoring them, it never started (`TestAMetaShardHeldFullRestartsWithItsCommittedTxns`). Held full, it takes a heartbeat of a later term and follows its sender; dropping every message while full, it kept its term (`TestAFullMetaShardTakesEveryMessageButAnAppend`). A learner held full behind a stuck checkpoint refuses a `Txn` with `NotLeader` naming its leader, as any follower does; refusing at any full replica, it answered `ErrOverloaded` (`TestAFullMetaFollowerNamesItsLeader`). Made full by a share mail while its store is idle, it asks for a checkpoint, which compacts it; without the ask the idle store took none (`TestAFullMetaShardGetsACheckpointFromAnIdleStore`). `raftshard.Appends` reports a Raft append, inline or buffered, and no heartbeat, snapshot or fortification message (`TestAppendsIsAMsgAppOnly`).
- **Start.** A crash before a new replica's boot round is written restarts it with nothing mailed: it writes its boot state again, starts, leads and takes `Txn`s; without that it never started (`TestANewMetaShardCrashedBeforeItsBootRoundStartsOnRestart`). Asked for its pieces before its boot round is durable, it replies at once that it has written all it has, and starts; without the reply the checkpoint waited on it (`TestAMetaShardNotYetStartedAnswersAnAskForItsPieces`). A new replica whose loop's pool holds no buffer for its boot round, on an idle store that mails it nothing, writes the round on its next message once buffers return, starts and leads; ignoring events before it started, it never did (`TestANewMetaShardShortOfBuffersWritesItsBootRoundOnItsNextEvent`). A learner that joins with empty storage restarts after a crash before its boot round is durable, and again after a checkpoint flushed its tree, marked at base 0, before its leader's snapshot reached it; it then catches up with every `Txn` its leader applied. Applying a base at index 0 as a snapshot, it never restarted (`TestAMetaShardThatJoinsWithEmptyStorageRestarts`).
- **A restored snapshot.** The learner, cut off while its voter applies `Txn`s, gets them in its leader's snapshot; the process is crashed at every step from the reconnection to 20 steps after the learner took the snapshot's round durable. Each restart restores the learner holding every index it acknowledged, and holding every key its leader applied whenever its storage is at or past the snapshot, with restarts before the snapshot, on it, and after the acknowledgment each seen. Telling Raft the round durable at once, leaving out the ask that a segment header name the manifest or the store's naming of it, or marking the flush with the storage's base rather than the snapshot's, the learner restarted short of an index it acknowledged; restoring a round's snapshot past older runs, it restarted on the snapshot without its keys (`TestALearnerCrashedAtEveryStepOfASnapshotRestoreKeepsWhatItAcknowledged`). Flushing the snapshot again at a checkpoint begun after its empty round was written, the learner was told a round durable that it had already taken (`TestAMetaShardThatJoinsWithEmptyStorageRestarts`). On runs older than the snapshot a replay drops its round whole, its hard state with it, and reports its blobs dead; on runs at it, the round drops every entry replayed before it, which a replay dropping them only for a snapshot past its base kept (`TestRoundsReplayDropsASnapshotRoundTheRunsDoNotHold`). A follower that voted, then took a snapshot's round whose hard state freed its vote's round, reports no replay LSN past that round until a later round is durable, so a restart on older runs after the LSN reported still holds the vote; reporting it at once, the restart came back with no hard state (`TestRoundsKeepTheVoteASnapshotRoundTheRunsDoNotHoldWouldDrop`). Its record carries no snapshot data (`TestARoundWhoseSnapshotIsInTheRunsCarriesNoData`).

## MetaStore replicas on a device loop

On a device loop over a simulated disk, a `node.Device` hosting MetaStore replicas, each the single voter of its group, their `Txn`s sent over the wire by a client.

- **Txns, checkpoints and restart.** The replica takes 1,200 `Txn`s of 900 bytes, more than the server holds unanswered at once, 20 at a time: every one is answered as applied, checkpoints end through the store's mail and the replica's replies, and a second replica of the group is refused (`ErrHosted`). A restart restores it from the disk's record with every `Txn` answered, and it leads and takes another. Without the mail sent, the replies taken, the restart naming the replica, or the server's count dropped on an answer, it fails (`TestADeviceHostsAMetaStoreReplicaAcrossARestart`).
- **The disk's record.** After a crash, a replica that answered `Txn`s comes back holding every one, restored from the disk's manifest under the settings of its group, while another group's settings host nothing; a disk holding a replica the device has no settings for leaves the device failed, and an ask about the replica before the store serves is not answered Gone (`TestARestartRestoresTheReplicasItsDiskHolds`). Crashed at every step from its add to its start, a new replica is restored whenever it had started; a crash before a segment header named a manifest naming it loses it, and the device answers an ask about it Gone (`TestANewReplicaStartsOnlyOnceARestartWouldRestoreIt`). A store's restart hands its `Replicas` the replica its manifest names, and with no `Replicas` stops (`TestARestartHandsReplicasTheReplicasItsManifestNames`); an ordinary round after `Log.NameNewest` opens a segment, whose header names the newest manifest, while the checkpoint's lane still appends (`TestARoundAfterNameNewestNamesTheNewestManifest`); a manifest edit names the replica of an index its base holds (`TestAManifestEditKeepsAnIndexsReplica`); a manifest of the kind before indexes named their replica does not decode (`TestManifestRoundTrip`).
- **Removal.** A replica removed with `Txn`s in flight answers each dropped, and the device then takes a new replica of its group, which leads and applies a `Txn`; without the answers, or with the group still counted hosted, it fails (`TestRemovingAReplicaAnswersTheTxnsItHolds`). The removal's checkpoint leaves the replica out and the store's empty round under its owner names that manifest, so the device answers an ask about it Gone on a disk nothing else writes; without that round, or without the manifest named, it never does (`TestARemovedReplicaIsSoonGone`). Until the store takes the removal, which waits for a round in flight, the device refuses a new replica of the group `ErrHosted`; crashed at each of 12 steps after the new replica's add, the device starts again, where taking it at once left a manifest naming two replicas of the group and the restart failed (`TestARemovedReplicasGroupTakesANewReplicaOnlyOnceTheStoreTookTheRemoval`). A removal asked during a restart's replay is refused `ErrNotServing` and the restored replica keeps its `Txn`s (`TestADeviceRemovesNoReplicaBeforeItServes`). Removed and added again 20 times, the device keeps one timer slot and no removal at each add; without the slot freed at the store's taking of the removal, or without the removal forgotten once Gone holds, it fails (`TestRemovingAndAddingReplicasKeepsTheDevicesTablesBounded`). With the checkpoint running at the removal stalled, its other replica's pieces held back, the removed replica's owner key is refused, and a crash restores the removed replica whole with no blob of another; with both of `Host.Reusable`'s checks off, the unnamed manifest and the replay floor, a new replica took the key and the restored one held its boot state (`TestARemovedOwnerWaitsForAManifestLeavingItsReplicaOut`). Crashed at every step from a removal with a round in flight, through another group's `Txn`s, to a new replica under the removed one's owner key starting, the disk restores the removed replica, holding every `Txn` it applied, only while the device would not answer an ask about it Gone, and restores the new replica, holding none of the removed one's keys, whenever it had started; answering Gone with the removal unnamed, or before the store took it, fails (`TestARestartAfterARemovalNeverRestoresTheRemovedReplicaGone`).
- **A group not hosted.** A `Txn` for a group the device hosts no replica of is answered `NotLeader` (`TestADeviceAnswersATxnForAGroupItDoesNotHost`).
- **Two groups.** A device hosting the replicas of two groups has each lead on its own Raft timer and take its own group's `Txn`s alone; with every group message routed to the first replica, or every timer, it fails (`TestADeviceHostsTheReplicasOfTwoGroups`).
- **A format drops what was restored.** A device that restores a replica on a disk whose store then finds no log and formats hosts the group again as a new replica, which leads and applies a `Txn`; with the restored replica kept, the group is refused `ErrHosted` (`TestADeviceThatFormatsHostsTheGroupsItRestoredAgain`).
- **A grown volume.** A disk reopened as twice its size reports the size its log was formatted with and restores its replica under the blob bound its log keeps from its format: it holds every `Txn` it answered, leads, and takes 100 `Txn`s at once, gathered into a round past that bound; restored under the bound of a log of the disk's new size, it answered them dropped, and reporting the configured size, it reported twice the log's (`TestADeviceRestoresItsReplicasOnAGrownVolume`).
- **A failed round.** Once the disk fails its writes, every `Txn` the replica held is answered `ErrProposalDropped` or, arriving after, `NotLeader`, and the next is refused `NotLeader` (`TestAReplicaWhoseRoundFailsAnswersTheTxnsItHolds`). A server at its bound for the group of a replica stopped so refuses its next `Txn` `NotLeader`, not `ErrOverloaded` (`TestAServerRefusesATxnForAFailedReplicaNotLeader`).
- **Dropped at once.** A leader transferring its leadership, a voter having asked for it, drops each `Txn` proposed to it within the call that proposes it: the server answers it `ErrProposalDropped` and holds it no more, so a server bounded at one `Txn` drops the next too rather than refusing it overloaded (`TestAServerAnswersATxnItsLeaderDropsMidTransfer`).
- **The server's bound.** With a replica's round in flight, a server holding at most two `Txn`s of a group refuses the third with `meta.ErrOverloaded` over the wire; without the bound it refuses none (`TestTheServerBoundsTheTxnsAReplicaGathers`). The wire carries `ErrOverloaded` as itself, not as a dropped proposal (`TestTxnsAndAnswersCrossTheWireWhole`).

## Sharded API, one shard

- **Routing.** A `Txn` routes every key it reads or writes, its ranges and its replay key through the shard map. With the control-plane group and one data shard, every key but `ctl/`'s maps to the data shard and `ctl/` keys to the control-plane group; a `Txn` within one goes to that group's leader alone, and the group's log holds it once. A route through the shard map and the route cache, with its answer, allocates nothing.
- **Two shards.** A shard map with a second data shard, used only in unit tests of the router, refuses a `Txn` whose keys, ranges or replay key reach both with `ErrCrossShard` naming both groups, before anything is sent; a range ending at the second shard's first key stays in the first. A `Txn` touching a `ctl/` key and a data key is refused the same way, since the control-plane group is a Raft group of its own; no designed transaction does that. So is a `Scan` over the whole key space, since one point-in-time view covers one group. Cross-shard transactions arrive in phase 13.
- **At a follower.** A `Txn` sent to a follower or a candidate is never forwarded: it is answered `NotLeader{group, leader replica and node, term}` and proposes nothing. The router caches that leader and resends to it, the group's log holds the `Txn` once, and the next `Txn` goes straight to the leader. A `NotLeader` of an older term than the cache's, or one naming no leader in the cached term, leaves the cache as it is, unless it comes from the cached leader, which drops it. A halted follower answers `NotLeader` too.
- **No leader.** Before an election a replica answers `NotLeader` naming none, and the router holds the `Txn` and arms its timer for an election timeout (1 s). When it fires, the router tries the group's next voter, which either takes the `Txn` or names the leader, and the `Txn` is proposed once.
- **Restarted leader.** The cached leader restarts while the router is idle and comes back a follower of its term that heard no leader. Whether or not its lost connection reached the router, the next `Txn` reaches the new leader or is held for the election, after at most two sends; it is never resent in a loop.
- **Lost node.** A lost connection fails the `Txn`s sent on it as dropped (`ErrProposalDropped`), since each may have applied, and the router forgets that node as the leader of every group, even with nothing in flight to it, so the next `Txn` goes to another voter.
- **Shard map changes.** A new map fails the `Txn`s held for an election whose group it no longer holds with `ErrGroupGone`; none was proposed, so the caller routes them again. The router copies the map, so the caller may change its own.
- **During an election.** A client request arriving during an election fails retryably and is never applied twice: its resend carries the same replay key and returns the first final result (see Filesystem schema).
- **Internal `Txn`s across a leader change.** The purger's `Check(p/i = v)` with `Delete(p/i)` applies, its reply is lost, a new leader is elected, a truncate merges a new range into `p/i`, and the purger resends: the check fails and nothing is deleted. A blind `Delete(p/i)` in its place loses the merged range; as a planted bug in the purger's simulator run it fires the purge invariant ([MetaStore invariants](#metastore-invariants)). A control-plane table version `Check(e)`, `Put(e + 1)` repeated after an election fails its check.
- **Replay-tagged keys.** A client `Txn`, one with a replay key, with a `Put`, `Delete` or `Update` of a replay-tagged key, or a `DeleteRange` holding one, is refused with `ErrReplayTagged` before proposing, so a resend under that key never meets a value that is no record and is never answered `ErrMalformed`; reading one is not refused, nor is the leader's internal `Txn` that drops a departed session's records. Replay-tagged means an `fs/` key at sequence 0 whose byte 13, the tag, is `0x14`, whether or not the rest decodes: a raw 35-byte key starting with a mount's record prefix is refused too, since the drop below `Oldest` would remove it, and so is the bare 14-byte prefix. A seeded property test checks the range test against its definition: a range holds such a key when some slot's replay-tagged prefix sorts below its end and its prefix range reaches past its start.
- **`ctl/` keys.** They go through the same `Txn` and `Scan`, and the shard map pins `[ctl/, PrefixEnd(ctl/))` to the control-plane group, the map's first, which never splits: a map with a boundary inside its range, a second range in it, or ranges that do not rise is refused.

## Control-plane group

`meta.Control` runs at the leader of a real three-replica group on the hand-driven network
(`internal/meta`, `ctl_test.go`), each commit read back from the group's state. Applying a delta
on a node is chunkstore's (`table_test.go`).

**Pools**

| Input | Expected |
| --- | --- |
| A `Pool` create or update | Checked against the [Pools](#pools) creation rules, then committed under `ctl/pool/`. A refused one commits nothing (`TestPoolsAreCheckedThenCommittedUnderCtl`) |
| `replicas` changed | The next table starts a new interval of every PG of the pool (`TestRaisingReplicasStartsAnIntervalOfEveryPG`) |
