| `pg_count` changed on an existing pool | A doubling commits in one `Txn`, the pool record with a table whose every PG splits into halves that keep its members and past intervals and start its interval plus one, which the next leader reads back; any other change is refused (`TestAPoolChangeIsCheckedAgainstTheCommittedPool`) |
| Two changes of a pool staged before a step; a pool set to the settings it has | The step commits the last; the second commits nothing (`TestAPoolChangeIsCheckedAgainstTheCommittedPool`) |
| A pool change staged by a machine whose commit then lost a race | Checked again against the pool it reads back; refused there, it is dropped with an error and the next step commits the rest (`TestAStagedPoolIsCheckedAgainAfterAReload`) |
| A `rep3` pool of 32,768 PGs, whose creation is more than `max_ctl_txn_bytes`; two of 16,384 staged together; one of 8,192 doubled | The first is refused with `ErrTooLarge`; the two are each taken, then dropped together with `ErrTooLarge`, and the next step commits a pool of 8,192 alone; the doubling, whose halves each carry a past interval, is refused with `ErrTooLarge` (`TestAPoolTooLargeForATxnIsRefused`) |
| A `min_live` or `replicas` change of a committed `rep3` pool of 16,384 PGs | Refused at `SetPool` with `ErrTooLarge`, since every PG would gain a past interval in one table (`TestASettingsChangeTooLargeForATxnIsRefused`) |

**Placement table**

| Input | Expected |
| --- | --- |
| A node holding table epoch e receives the delta for e + 1 | It applies the delta. The CRC32C of its resulting table equals the CRC in the entry (`TestATableCommitsAsItsDelta`) |
| A delta whose resulting CRC does not match | The node fetches the whole table (`TestDeltaBases`) |
| A node at e receives e + 3 (a gap) | It fetches the whole table. It loses nothing, since each PG entry carries its interval number (`TestDeltaBases`) |
| A Raft snapshot of the group | Holds the whole table (`TestANewLeaderAndASnapshotReadBackTheWholeState`) |
| A primary reports activation of interval k on its heartbeat | A later table records k as the PG's last activated interval and drops the member lists of the intervals before it. That table starts no interval (`TestAnActivationIsRecordedWithoutANewInterval`) |
| The primary and members of a PG resend their ask for a new interval every second while a commit is pending | The control plane keeps one ask per PG and interval (`TestResentAsksKeepOneAskPerInterval`) |
| An ask for a new interval tagged with a table older than its pool's split, sent while the split's commit is pending or after it | Dropped; one sent under the split's table starts a new interval of the half (`TestAnAskFromBeforeASplitIsDropped`) |
| A new pool of 8,192 PGs staged beside the down marks of a disk in two pools of 8,192, with an ask for a PG of the second the disk is not in | Commits over several `Txn`s, each within `max_ctl_txn_bytes`: the new pool whole in the first, then the marks left from where it stopped; every PG ends with the disk down, and the asked PG one interval on, the ask kept past the first `Txn` that left it out (`TestAStepOverOneTxnCommitsOverSeveral`) |
| A disk's down marks in four pools of 8,192 PGs that take two `Txn`s, with the activations of every PG the first changed reported in between | The second `Txn` starts where the first stopped and marks the disk down in every PG left, the activations after (`TestTheNextTxnResumesWhereTheLastStopped`) |
| The writes a table makes beside its entries: its head, a pool header, a dropped pool's range | Each fits the bytes the leader keeps back for it, with two to spare for the `Txn`'s op count (`TestHeadOpsBoundTheTableWritesBesideTheEntries`) |
| A disk added, a recovered report, a down mark | Each table raises the table epoch and commits only the entries it changes. Only PGs whose members change start a new interval (`TestATableCommitsAsItsDelta`) |
| The control-plane leader fails over | The new leader reads the pools, the table and the shard map back from the group's state, and its next table follows the last committed one (`TestANewLeaderAndASnapshotReadBackTheWholeState`) |
| Two machines each think they lead | The second's commit fails its checks against what the first committed; it reads the state again and its next commit lands on top (`TestARacingCommitFailsItsChecks`) |
| A table computed from pool settings another machine has since changed, with no table of its own | The commit fails its checks (`TestATableIsCheckedAgainstEveryPoolItReads`) |
| A PG entry or a group over 999 bytes | Stored as a head and pieces; a shorter one written over it drops the pieces it no longer has (`TestALongValueIsStoredInPieces`) |
| The `ctl/` keys of a pool, its table header, a PG entry, a group and their pieces | Encode as `testdata/key_golden.txt` freezes them (`TestCtlKeysAreTheGoldenOnes`) |
| A pool's settings or a group's entry as bytes | Decodes without a panic, and one that decodes encodes back to the same bytes (`FuzzDecodePool`, `FuzzDecodeGroup`) |
| Any set of `ctl/` keys and values | Decodes without a panic; a state that decodes has the CRC32C its head names and a shard map `CheckRanges` accepts (`FuzzDecodeCtl`) |
| A pool's `ctl/placement/{pool}` value with a split epoch above the table's, under a CRC32C that covers it, or of 6 bytes, with no split epoch | Malformed (`TestAPlacementPoolValueOfAnotherFormIsMalformed`) |

**Shard map**

| Input | Expected |
| --- | --- |
| `PlaceVoters` gives a group new voters | The group's entry is committed under `ctl/` before its leader is handed the plan (`TestAPlanIsHandedOutOnlyOnceCommitted`) |
| The leader fails over with a shard map change proposed and not committed | No group was handed it, and the new leader hands out no replica ID it already handed out (`TestAPlanIsHandedOutOnlyOnceCommitted`) |
| A Raft snapshot of the group | Holds the whole shard map (`TestANewLeaderAndASnapshotReadBackTheWholeState`) |

## Control-plane membership

`meta.Control` hosts the failure detector and commits the disk record at the leader of a real
three-replica group, as in [Control-plane group](#control-plane-group) (`internal/meta`,
`members_test.go`). Each node 0 to 4 holds one disk, and time moves by heartbeats a second apart.
The detector's own rules, against a whole simulated cluster, are
[Failure and fail-slow detection](#failure-and-fail-slow-detection)'s.

| Input | Expected |
| --- | --- |
| A disk misses heartbeats for `node_down_after` (5 s) | Marked down in one table, which starts a new interval of every PG with a member on it and of no other (`TestASilentDiskIsMarkedDownThenRefilled`) |
| The disk stays down for `refill_after` (10 minutes) from its down mark, no node reporting a replica | Its PG members refilled ([Placement computation](#placement-computation)) and its shard voters replaced ([Voter replacement](#voter-replacement)), not a second before, and no other voter, since no group has a majority reporting its plan (`TestASilentDiskIsMarkedDownThenRefilled`) |
| A disk marked down for the 5th time within `flap_window` (10 minutes) | Held down until it has been normal for a whole `flap_window` (`TestAFlappingDiskIsHeldDown`) |
| A primary reports a member after `member_timeout` (1 s), and the member's probe answer shows a stall | Marked down at once (`TestAStallIsMarkedDownAtOnce`) |
| The same report, but the probe answers with no stall | Not marked down (`TestAStallIsMarkedDownAtOnce`) |
| A heartbeat shows a disk stalled, with no report | Marked down at once (`TestAStallIsMarkedDownAtOnce`) |
| A disk's acknowledgment latency above `slow_disk_factor` (10×) its pool's median for `slow_disk_window` (1 min) | Marked down as fail-slow; not while another disk of its PGs is down, which would drop a PG below `min_live` (`TestAFailSlowDiskIsMarkedDownAndRejoinsAfterAWindow`) |
| A fail-slow disk's latency back to normal for 50 s, then for a whole minute | It rejoins only after the whole `slow_disk_window` (`TestAFailSlowDiskIsMarkedDownAndRejoinsAfterAWindow`) |
| A `-role meta` node | Holds control-plane and shard voters, and no PG member (`TestAMetaOnlyNodeHoldsVotersAndNoMember`) |
| A node restarted with `-role meta` whose disk holds members, then moves allowed and every PG recovered each step | Each member there is marked leaving before it is removed, none dropped in one table, until no PG names the disk (`TestANodeTurningMetaDrainsItsDisks`) |
| A node reports its two disks in swapped slots; then a new log on one device; then a log up on node 7 reported from node 8 | The disks keep their IDs; the new log joins under a new ID and only the disk last on that device has its log gone; the cloned log is refused with `ErrLogRefused` (`TestADiskIsKnownByItsLogOnItsDevice`) |
| A report naming two disks on one device, as drives with no WWN can be; then a reformat of one, and its old log reported again | Both refused with `ErrLogRefused` and neither retired; the reformat retires the old disk, whose log is refused afterwards (`TestADeviceIdentityTwiceInAReportIsRefused`) |
| A disk down for 5 minutes, then a failover to a leader whose clock reads 3 hours | The committed age is rewritten each minute and no sooner; the new leader refills the disk `refill_after` after its down mark, within a minute, not `refill_after` after the failover (`TestADownMarkCarriesItsAgeAcrossAFailover`) |
| The same, to a leader whose clock reads 2 minutes, less than the age | The new leader counts the disk down from its clock's zero and refills it `refill_after` after that, later than its down mark, never earlier (`TestADownMarkCarriesItsAgeAcrossAFailover`) |
| A disk's log replaced by a new one on its device, then 3 minutes | The old disk commits no age, so no commit rewrites it (`TestAGoneDiskIsNotWrittenAgain`) |
| After a failover, a down disk heartbeats normally for 2 minutes before its node reports; then its node reports | Not marked up until its node reports, since the leader does not know the node's release; then up (`TestADiskIsNotMarkedUpBeforeItsNodeReports`) |
| A voter's node reports it halted at an entry it cannot decode, aged just under `refill_after`, then aged `refill_after` | Kept, then replaced on another node, by the node's count of the halt's age (`TestAHaltIsCountedFromTheAgeItsNodeReports`) |
| A planned voter whose disk is up reports a configuration that has it only as a learner, or its node reports no replica of it, or it reports the joint configuration while the others report the leave; for just under `refill_after` from the leader's first step, then `refill_after`; one that reports the leave; and two of a group's three not holding the plan | Each stuck one kept, then replaced on another node, the group's other voters and another group's kept; the one that reports the leave kept; with no majority holding the plan, none replaced (`TestAPlannedVoterThatNeverReportsItsPlanIsReplaced`) |
| A node with two disks heartbeats while the disk of a voter that reports nothing stays silent for `node_down_after` and `refill_after` | The voter moves to the node's other disk by the disk rule, not off the node as a stuck one would (`TestAVoterOnADownDiskMovesToItsNodesOtherDisk`) |
| A planned voter its node never starts, for just under `refill_after`, then a failover, then `refill_after` less a second, then a second | Kept past `refill_after` from its first count, since the new leader counts from its own first step, then replaced (`TestAFailoverStartsAStuckVotersCountOver`) |
| A failover, or a commit whose answer is an error | Every committed shard-map entry is handed to its group's leader once more, and the whole table goes once to each node whose heartbeat shows an older epoch, and not to a node up to date (`TestALostAnswerIsHandedOutAgain`) |
| A restarted node | Its first table is one it fetched after it started, since a replica starts with none; a PG it leads takes a new interval before it serves (`TestARestartedPrimaryTakesANewIntervalBeforeItServes`, `internal/chunkstore`) |
| An operator drains a disk, then ends the drain; drains a disk the record does not know | Each commits in the disk record and reads back; the unknown one is refused with `ErrUnknownDisk` (`TestADrainCommits`) |
| A disk's entry, or any set of `ctl/` keys, as bytes | Decodes without a panic; an entry that decodes encodes back to the same bytes and is never up and gone or drained once gone; a state with disks has a record version (`FuzzDecodeDisk`, `FuzzDecodeCtl`) |
| The `ctl/` keys of the disk record, a disk and the format level | Encode as `testdata/key_golden.txt` freezes them (`TestCtlKeysAreTheGoldenOnes`) |

**Format level.** A `ctl/` key, raised by the operator. It is refused unless above the committed
one, at or below the release of every node heard from within `node_down_after`, so a node silent
that long no longer holds it back (`TestANodeSilentForNodeDownAfterIsForgotten`), and once every
node with a disk up has been heard by this leader. A level staged before a node is heard on an older
release is dropped at the next step with `ErrFormatLevel` (`TestAStagedFormatLevelIsCheckedAgainAtTheStep`).
A node running a release older than the level that heartbeats after it was
raised is not marked up, and a condition names it, until it heartbeats on a new enough release;
Ceph's monitor likewise ignores the boot of an OSD below its minimum release
(`TestANodeBelowTheFormatLevelIsNotMarkedUp`).

**Seeded run** (`TestTheDiskRecordKeepsItsIdentitiesAcrossFailovers`, in `scripts/seeds.sh`): six
nodes report their drives in random slot order, drives are reformatted, moved between nodes and
cloned, disks fail and are declared lost, time passes, the format level rises and the leader fails
over. After every step the simulator's invariants hold: a disk ID keeps the log ID it was first given
and no log ID is under two disk IDs; the leader's state holds the disk record and format level last
committed; a disk's log is gone only once another log was reported on its device of its node after
it, leaving out logs a cloned drive reported, or once an operator declared it lost; a disk committed
gone stays gone; and, with one node on an older release, a format level commits
only above no release of a node with a disk committed up.

## Control-plane sessions

`meta.Control` renews and fences sessions at the leader of a real three-replica group, as in
[Control-plane membership](#control-plane-membership) (`internal/meta`, `sessions_test.go`), with
the leader's two clocks moved by the test. The [Sessions and fencing model](#sessions-and-fencing-model)'s
leader-side rules are its invariants; the storage side is
[Session fencing on storage nodes](#session-fencing-on-storage-nodes)'s.

| Input | Expected |
| --- | --- |
| Daemons start 10 sessions | One commit of a `ctl/session/{id}` key each, with IDs from a counter. IDs are never reused, even after a fence (`TestASessionStartsRenewsInMemoryAndIsFencedThenAcknowledged`) |
| 100 heartbeats renewing those sessions | No Raft entry: renewals change only the leader's memory (same test) |
| The sessions fall due | One commit fencing every session due at that moment, as one new session-table version (same test) |
| Every storage node acknowledges version v, or is marked down in a committed table | v is committed as acknowledged, and the fenced sessions leave the table; while a node with its disk up is behind, it is not (same test, `TestANodeMarkedDownCountsAsAcknowledging`) |
| A fence its node has not acknowledged when its disk fails in three pools of 8,192 PGs, whose down marks take several tables | The disk record marks the disk down only with the table that marks its last PG, and the fence is acknowledged only after it (`TestAFenceWaitsForTheTableThatMarksTheDisksLastPG`) |
| The same failure with the leader's detector restarted after the first table, while the disk's down record is held | The restarted detector starts the disk down, so the PGs naming it live only fall, and the record marks it down with the last PG's table (`TestADetectorRestartMidSequenceKeepsAHeldDiskDown`) |
| A new leader receives a heartbeat before its leader lease starts | It answers none and commits nothing; a follower runs no `meta.Control` (`TestANewLeaderGivesEverySessionAFullLease`) |
| A new leader's leader lease starts | Every live session gets a full count from that start: `dead_wait` for one it has not measured, a session that sent it a single heartbeat included, and `session_lease` times its bound once two heartbeats measured it (same test) |
| The control-plane leader crashes 1 s after its last renewal of C, and a new leader whose `CLOCK_BOOTTIME` runs 22.6% fast answers 8 s, or 5 s, after the crash | C renews with it and is never fenced; D, whose daemon died with the old leader, is fenced once `dead_wait` has passed on the new leader's raw clock as well, not sooner on its fast boot clock (`TestAFastBootClockFencesNoSessionEarly`). C's side, ending its lease about 7.1 s after the crash when its own boot clock runs that fast and holding its writes until a leader answers, is the client daemon's |
| A failover to a leader whose clocks run 10% fast over C's and the old leader's, with its lease starting right after a renewal of C, at once or after the new leader stepped for 10 s while the old one renewed C; C dies then, or after two heartbeats to it, or after two heartbeats between which the new leader stands still for 200 ms with its clocks frozen and then gets `Resumed`, or after two heartbeats to it and a third to the deposed leader | C's lease from the old leader runs 9.9 s more, and C is fenced no sooner: `dead_wait` after the new lease's start, or `session_lease` × 1.1 on the new leader's clocks after the second heartbeat, or, after the stop, `dead_wait` after the second heartbeat, since `Resumed` dropped the answer it names. The deposed leader answers no heartbeat, so C's third gets it no lease (`TestAFastNewLeaderFencesNoSessionEarly`) |
| A leader whose raw clock runs 5% fast over its clients' | It measures the rate from two heartbeats and fences 10.5 s after the last renewal; a heartbeat naming an answer older than its last, as after a lost answer, leaves the session unmeasured, fenced only after `dead_wait` (`TestAFenceStretchesByTheMeasuredRate`) |
| A leader whose raw clock runs 5% fast processes C's heartbeat twice, 500 ms apart, or an older heartbeat of C's arrives 500 ms after a newer one; C's next heartbeat names the first answer | The leader pairs it with its first answer to the highest request and fences 10.5 s after the last renewal, where the later answer would bound its rate at 0.525 and fence after 10 s (`TestARepeatedHeartbeatIsMeasuredFromItsFirstAnswer`) |
| A measured bound of 0.5, 1.05, 30, or 2⁶² | The wait is `session_lease`, 10.5 s, then `dead_wait` for both of the last: no stretch passes it (`TestAStretchLiesBetweenTheLeaseAndDeadWait`) |
| The leader's loop falls behind by more than a heartbeat interval, or it resumes from a pause | Every session's timer restarts from now (`TestAStallOrAResumeRestartsEveryCount`) |
| An owner reports a recall unanswered for `recall_timeout`, or an operator evicts a session | The leader stops renewing the session and answers its heartbeats without renewing it; the session is fenced once its lease runs out on the leader's clock, like any expiry, never at once; evicting a session not live is refused with `ErrUnknownSession` (`TestAnEvictionOnlyStopsRenewals`) |
| A session's entry, or `ctl/` keys holding a session table, as bytes | Decodes without a panic; an entry that decodes encodes back to the same bytes; a table's acknowledged version is at most its version, and its sessions lie below its next ID, fenced at most at its version (`FuzzDecodeSession`, `FuzzDecodeCtl`) |

**Seeded run** (`TestNoSessionIsFencedWhileItsClientsLeaseRuns`, 20 seeds in `go test`, 2,000 in
`scripts/seeds.sh`). Four clients each hold a `lease.Holder` on their own clocks; each node's raw
clock runs within 10% of real time, and a quarter of them have their boot clock slewed up to 22.6%
apart from it. Slewing every node would hide the leader-side bugs: a holder ends its lease on its
faster clock and a grantor waits for its slower one, so random slews cover most rate errors. For
the same reason the clients keep no `Resume`, the second a holder leaves for a suspend that
delivers no `Resumed`: the run draws none, and that second would cover every leader-side bug. Five
storage nodes each send, every second, a heartbeat naming the session-table version they hold and
a disk beat to the leader's failure detector, which marks a silent disk down.

Faults: failovers, half of them crashes and half a deposed leader still answering for up to 3 s
while its lease runs, then refusing for 25 s more, past a new leader's `dead_wait`; clients
learning the new leader up to 15 s late; leader stalls of 2.5 to 5 s; 5% of heartbeats and answers
lost and each delayed up to 30 ms; evictions; two daemons that die; fenced clients starting new
sessions; storage nodes that each take the newest session-table version on a third of their
heartbeats, so acknowledgements wait; and one storage node at a time cut off for 2 to 27 s,
sending neither heartbeat nor disk beat, long enough for some cuts to be marked down. Each client
now and then takes, changes or drops a shared or exclusive lock on one inode, through an owner that
frees a lock key whose session `Control.Holding` no longer reports.

Checked every 10 ms: no session is fenced while its client's lease from any leader runs; after
every commit, a new leader reads the table back as committed; no ID is given twice; no version is
acknowledged before every node with a disk up holds it; at most one client acts on the lock while
holding a lease, unless every one holds it shared; a lock reaches its next holder only once every
node with a disk up holds its old holder's fence; a fenced session leaves the table within 1.2 s
of the time every node with a disk up holds its fence, not counting time the leader lacks its
lease, a node it hears from lags the table (time the model's `Urgent` does not let pass), or a
cut-off node's disk is not yet due its down mark: `node_down_after` + 3 s on the leader's boot
clock from the last of the cut's start, the lease start or a stall's end, so a leader that never
marks a silent disk down fails it. A dead client's session is fenced within `dead_wait` + 250 ms
on the leader's clocks from the last of its death, its start, the leader's lease start or a
stall's end. The checks cover nodes that rejoin: the leader marks a disk that was down up again
only once its node's heartbeat reports the current version
(`TestADownDiskIsMarkedUpOnlyOnceItsNodeHoldsTheCurrentTable`). At the end, every dead client's session has left the table and the version is acknowledged.

**Planted bugs** (`TestPlantedSessionBugsFenceEarly`, `TestPlantedLockBugsBreakTheLockInvariants`).
Each of the model's leader-side negatives below breaks the invariant named, in the seeded run
within the seeds named, checking that invariant alone, or every time in the fast new leader's
scenario:

| Planted bug | Invariant | Seeds of 500 | First | Caught by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `neg-dead-wait-lease`: an unmeasured session waits only `session_lease` | No early fence | 13 | 33 | Seeded run, 190 seeds; the scenario with C dying at once |
| `neg-count-on-own-clock`: every session waits `session_lease` on the leader's own clock | No early fence | 13 | 33 | Seeded run, 190 seeds; the scenario after the new leader measured C |
| `neg-evict-at-once`: an eviction fences the session at once | No early fence | 500 | 0 | Seeded run, 10 seeds |
| `neg-no-full-lease`: a new leader's lease starts no count over, so it counts from its first step | No early fence | 19 | 49 | Seeded run, 130 seeds; the scenario with the new leader stepping 10 s before its lease starts |
| `neg-answer-without-lease`: a leader answers renewals without its leader lease, and so without the grants step only its lease starts | No early fence | 46 | 6 | Seeded run, 55 seeds; the scenario with C's third heartbeat to the deposed leader |
| `neg-two-holders`: the same plant as `neg-evict-at-once`, so the evicted client still acts on its lock under its lease while the next holder takes it | One holder | 117 | 0 | Seeded run, 22 seeds |
| `neg-release-on-commit`: a fenced session's locks are freed once its fence commits, while it is still in the table | Lock order | 292 | 2 | Seeded run, 10 seeds |
| `neg-ack-reachable-only`: a version counts as acknowledged when every node the leader heard from holds it, skipping a node with a disk up it has no heartbeat from | Lock order | 35 | 12 | Seeded run, 72 seeds |
| `neg-ack-waits-down`: acknowledgement also waits for nodes whose disks are marked down | Locks free in time | 263 | 0 | Seeded run, 10 seeds |
| `neg-up-with-old-table`: a disk marked down is marked up on its disk beat while its node holds an older table | Acknowledgement | 36 | 4 | Seeded run, 70 seeds |

In the model, `neg-no-full-lease` counts from the last renewal any leader processed. Go keeps the
counts only in the leader's memory, so the plant counts from the new leader's first step, which
breaks the invariant when that step comes before the old leader's last renewal: with clocks 10% fast,
the new leader has to step about 9 s before its lease starts for its `dead_wait` to end inside C's
lease. The seeded run's new leader steps at most 4 s before, so it rarely does.

The `neg-answer-without-lease` scenario is a history the model allows, not the model's shortest
trace. In that trace the new leader has not measured C, and the deposed leader renews C while the new
leader's `dead_wait` runs, which ends inside C's new lease. The model's `dead_wait` is 1.25 ×
`session_lease`, which makes that path the short one; Go's is 2×, which makes the measured path the
short one, so the scenario has C measured by the new leader, then renewed by the deposed one, then
dead. The seeded run reaches the bug as well, since its deposed leader refuses for longer than
`dead_wait`.

## Space grants

Grants are computed on each heartbeat, per node and pool ([Client design](design.md#client-design)), in blocks. The inputs:

- A: the pool's available figure before grants;
- F: the bytes nodes reported flushed, from their cumulative counts, until the leader holds a fill of every member disk received at least 1 s after the heartbeat that reported them;
- askᵢ: min(`writeback_buffer`, what node i holds buffered + one second of its writes);
- bufferedᵢ, heldᵢ: what node i holds buffered, and the grant its heartbeat says it holds;
- Σ: the sum over nodes of max(heldᵢ, grantᵢ) until a heartbeat echoes grantᵢ, then the larger of grantᵢ and bufferedᵢ;
- k = 2: the reuse budget, in grants, between answered heartbeats;
- g_d: for each up disk d holding a member of the pool, its size less its log reserve less the larger of its fill and `write_limit`.

The rules:

- each grant is at most `writeback_buffer` (256 MiB);
- Σ ≤ (A − F) ÷ 2; lowering A by F is the same as lowering every disk's room by F × its share, since A is the smallest room ÷ share;
- (1 + k) × Σ + F ≤ g_d for every disk d;
- a binding cap is divided by water-filling: grantᵢ = min(askᵢ, max(bufferedᵢ, L)), L the level that fills it, and a node above L buffers nothing new until its buffered bytes fall below L.

The leader's side is in `internal/meta/grants_test.go`. The daemon's side (its asks, reuse budget, early heartbeats, writing through and handoff memfd) comes with [Write-back buffer under space grants](#write-back-buffer-under-space-grants); rows marked *daemon* are its cases, and the seeded run models that daemon.

| Case | Inputs | Expected |
| --- | --- | --- |
| G1: room everywhere | 4 nodes ask 256 MiB each; a 1 TB disk at 50% fill | Each node granted 256 MiB; Σ = 1 GiB (`TestGrantsMeetEveryAskWithRoom`) |
| G2: a node asks for more than its buffer | One node holds 300 MiB buffered and wrote 1 GiB in the last second | Asks and is granted at most 256 MiB (same test) |
| G2b: an idle node | A node with nothing buffered and nothing written | Asks 0, and its grant returns to the pool once a heartbeat echoes it (same test) |
| G3: half-available cap | A = 1 GiB; 4 nodes ask 256 MiB each, nothing buffered | 128 MiB each; Σ = 512 MiB (`TestGrantsAreWaterFilledUnderHalfOfAvailable`) |
| G3b: unequal asks | Cap 512 MiB; asks 256, 256, 64 and 16 MiB | 216, 216, 64 and 16 MiB; the same when the first node holds 200 MiB buffered (same test) |
| G3c: a floor above the level | As G3b, the first node holding 250 MiB buffered | 250, 182, 64 and 16 MiB (same test) |
| G3d: floors above the cap | 4 nodes hold 256 MiB grants at A = 2 GiB; the fill rises to A = 1 GiB, cap 512 MiB; asks 256 each, buffered 200, 200, 200 and 0 MiB | Grants 112, 112, 112 and 0: no reply carries more than the room the others leave under the cap, and the leader counts the three at the 200 MiB they hold buffered (same test; seed 102 of the tight run, `TestAReplyNeverGrantsPastTheCap`, where a reply carrying the floor let the daemons land past g_d); *daemon:* a node granted less than it holds buffered buffers nothing new, and the excess drains as the nodes flush |
| G4: gap cap on a large disk | A 100 GB disk at 80% fill under a 90% `write_limit`: A = 10 GB, gap 9.87 GB after its 8-segment reserve (16 MiB segments); 10 nodes ask 256 MiB | The cap is g_d ÷ 3 = 3.29 GB, below A ÷ 2 = 5 GB, so all 2.68 GB of full grants fit (`TestTheGapCapsGrants`) |
| G5: gap cap on a small, fast disk | A 32 GB NVMe disk at 80% under a 90% `write_limit`: A = 3.2 GB, gap 3.17 GB (4 MiB segments); 10 nodes ask 256 MiB | Σ ≤ g_d ÷ 3 = 1.06 GB, below A ÷ 2, about 101 MiB each by water-filling; no disk write rate enters (same test) |
| G6: no gap | g_d ≤ F | Σ grows by nothing; a node holding 200 MiB buffered is granted 0 and counted at 200 MiB (`TestNoRoomGrantsOnlyWhatIsBuffered`) |
| G7: available 0 | A pool placed at 50% whose disk then fills to its 90% `write_limit` | A = 0 and the pool is `Full`: Σ = 0 (same test) |
| G8: flushes not yet in reported fills | A = 1 GiB; 100 MiB flushed and reported | Σ ≤ 462 MiB until a fill received at least 1 s after that report; one received sooner does not cover it. After it, F is 0 again (`TestFlushesCountUntilAFillCoversThem`) |
| G8b: a lost heartbeat request, then a fill report | A node's heartbeat with cumulative count c + 100 MiB is lost; the next carries c + 150 MiB | F counts all 150 MiB from the second heartbeat until a fill covers it; nothing is lost with the first (same test) |
| G9: leader failover | 10 live sessions | The new leader counts each session at 256 MiB per pool until it echoes a grant of the new leader's, one round trip after it first hears it, and grants new ones only out of what is left (`TestANewLeaderCountsEverySessionAtAFullBuffer`); *daemon:* meanwhile one past its budget writes through |
| G9c: a late reply of the old leader | The old leader's reply granting 80 MiB reaches the daemon after its first heartbeat to the new leader, whose reply is lost; two other nodes ask | The new leader counts the session at 256 MiB until it echoes the new leader's grant, so what the three can land fits g_d (`TestALateReplyOfAnEarlierLeaderIsCounted`); *daemon:* it takes no answer whose issuer is older than the one it holds |
| G9d: a regained lease | The leader loses its lease and regains it | It starts its grants over as a new leader: nothing granted until fills received 1 s after its first step under the regained lease, every session counted at 256 MiB until it echoes that lease's grant (`TestARegainedLeaseStartsGrantsOver`) |
| G9b: a heartbeat before the new leader's first step | A session heartbeats a new leader before its first step under its leader lease | Unanswered, and the session counted at 256 MiB (`TestAHeartbeatBeforeTheFirstStepIsUnanswered`, seed 30 of the seeded run). With 80 MiB of the old leader's grant buffered, flushed onto a disk 10 MiB below its `write_limit` after the fill that readies the pool was summed, its next heartbeat adds 3 × 80 MiB to F, so two other nodes asking are granted only what the disk can take; an answer of 0 let them land 70 MiB past its top (`TestAFlushAfterAnUnansweredHeartbeatCountsInF`) |
| G9e: a leader rebuilt in its term | A second `meta.Control` built for the same term | Its answers carry a newer issuer than the first's (`TestAControlRebuiltInItsTermIssuesANewerIssuer`) |
| G10: a node stops renewing | Its grant g was carried by a renewal at t | g counts until its fence version is acknowledged, `session_lease` plus one fence round after t, then drops out of Σ (`TestANewLeaderCountsEverySessionAtAFullBuffer`) |
| G11: heartbeat replies lost | *daemon:* one reply lost | Nothing changes: the daemon's early heartbeat at half its budget gets the next reply. With that reply lost too, it writes through once it has used k grants, until a reply comes. No flush is ever refused for space (the seeded run) |
| G11b: a shrink whose reply is lost | 3 nodes shrunk from 256 to 50 MiB, the replies lost | The leader counts each at 256 MiB until a heartbeat echoes 50 MiB; counting 50 at once would let them land 2.42 GB while it counted 0.47 GB (`TestAShrinkCountsUntilEchoed`) |
| G11c: an echoed shrink with more buffered | A node granted 80 MiB buffers 80 MiB before the reply shrinking it to 0 arrives; another node's flush report tightens the cap; the heartbeat echoing 0 reports 80 MiB buffered | The leader counts the node at 80 MiB, not at the 20 MiB the cap leaves (`TestAnEchoedShrinkCountsWhatIsBuffered`) |
| G12: grants reused | *daemon:* a node's 256 MiB flush completes | The daemon reuses its grant at once; once it has flushed 256 MiB of its 512 MiB budget it sends its heartbeat early, and the reply resets the window |
| G12b: a streaming node with no faults | *daemon:* a node writing at 25 GbE under a 256 MiB grant | It stays buffered throughout, sending about 11 extra heartbeats per second |
| G12c: buffered bytes on a full disk | L = 0; a node holding 200 MiB buffered | Its grant is 0 and the leader counts it at 200 MiB (`TestNoRoomGrantsOnlyWhatIsBuffered`); *daemon:* streaming at 1.1 GB/s, it buffers nothing new: new writes go through, and its buffered bytes only drain |
| G12d: a daemon crash in the middle of a window | The successor's cumulative count is lower than the last one heard | The leader keeps the old (1 + k) × grant in F until a fill received 1 s after that heartbeat covers it (`TestARestartedCountKeepsTheOldBudgetInF`); *daemon:* the successor continues the count from the handoff memfd, and one that cannot read it buffers nothing until its first heartbeat is answered |
| G13: a disk past `write_limit` | A pool placed at 50% whose disk a refill pushes to 92% | A = 0, so the pool is `Full` and nothing is granted; g_d, for grants already counted, is measured from its fill: 8% of the disk less its reserve (`TestNoRoomGrantsOnlyWhatIsBuffered`) |

**[property]** The invariants, checked after every 10 ms step of `TestNoGrantedFlushIsRefusedForSpace` (1,000 seeds per commit, each run twice): no flush under a grant is refused for space; what the daemons in the session table can still land under their grants fits every member disk above the larger of its fill and `write_limit`; and every nonzero reply keeps (1 + k) × (the others' count + grant) + F ≤ g_d and 2 × (the others' count + grant) + F ≤ A. Each run has 6 to 10 daemons on pool 1 over 1 to 3 disks of 8 to 256 GiB at 60 to 88% fill, buffering within their grants and reuse budgets, writing through at `write_limit` and flushing mostly to one hot disk, with a cleaner freeing space; the tight run gives every daemon 3 MiB more of writes per 10 ms, every disk 8 GiB and ten times the deaths, so the daemons' own invariant, not only the leader's view, sees an overrun. `TestPlantedGrantBugsOverrun` plants each counting bug and sees it fail: a session counted after a failover at no more than it says it holds (seed 4 of the tight run, on what the daemons can land), and a lapsed session's grant dropped before its fence is acknowledged, in a session lapsing with a full grant while two others ask on a disk whose gap is three times the cap; the run's disks leave too much slack for that one to show. It plants two capping bugs too: grants capped by half of available only, not by the smallest gap (the tight run breaks what the daemons can land within 6 seeds; 415 of 500 seeds break it), and a shrink counted at its new value before a heartbeat echoes it, scripted as G11b (`shrinkRun`), since the seeded run's daemons never land past a gap under it in 500 seeds.

**Capacity figures.** From the fills and per-pool data the disk heartbeats report (8 bytes per disk and 12 per pool with data on it), each disk's size and log reserve from its node's report, the leader computes per pool the available, balanced, stranded-fraction and reprotectable figures and the conditions, with the [Pools](#pools) cases as inputs (`Control.Capacity`, checked in G7 and G13). A disk's class is the one committed in its record entry when it joined ([Blocked and unfound reports](#blocked-and-unfound-reports)). The leader takes a pool's data on a disk from its heartbeat, its own as held and the others' out of its capacity, and a count above the disk's fill or size at the smaller (`TestCapacityTakesEachPoolsDataFromTheHeartbeat`); the disk's replica reports its index's counts with its fill (`TestTheDiskHeartbeatCarriesEachPoolsLiveBlocks`), and the decoder refuses more than 256 pools, pools out of order, repeated, reserved or empty (`TestWireRejectsBadFields`, `FuzzDecodeMessage`), but not pools summing past the fill, so the detector still hears the disk (`TestAHeartbeatWithPoolsPastItsFillKeepsItsDiskUp`).

**Simulator faults** (the seeded run):

- the pool reaching `write_limit` while daemons buffer and other nodes write through;
- a heartbeat carrying a space grant lost or delayed, its request or its reply, and disk fills lost or delayed up to 300 ms;
- a control-plane failover while daemons stream under their grants, the old leader answering for up to 3 s;
- up to two clients partitioned from the control-plane leader but not from storage, half streaming under their grants and half idle, until their fences are acknowledged.

A daemon crash in the middle of a reuse window, and a write that crosses from a granted chunk into a refused one, are daemon cases, covered by [Write-back buffer under space grants](#write-back-buffer-under-space-grants).

## Control-plane placement faults

The primary-change run and its leaving-member variant run against the real control-plane group as well as the stand-in, under the same invariants. A run's authority (`internal/chunkstore`, `control_plane_test.go`) either computes each table with `Next`, the stand-in, or has `meta.Control` at the leader of a real three-replica group commit it (`ctlgroup_test.go`, in `chunkstore_test`, since `meta` imports `chunkstore`). The real one is driven as the leader's host drives it. It learns each disk from its node's heartbeat. Asks reach the control plane's node as an asks frame, and activations and recovered reports as a report frame, over the simulated network, and that node hands them to `Control.Asked` and `OnEvent`, so a node cut off from it is heard by nobody. A message takes the network's 50 µs, a group commit the disk's write and flush (1,020 µs), and `Control` steps every `StepInterval` (100 ms) with its lease read, so a commit in flight overlaps asks, reports and heartbeats. It marks disks only by its own detector, so a run's down mark becomes a cut between the disk's node and the control plane's node, marked down once silent for `node_down_after` and up at its first heartbeat after the heal. The run stages its PG edits through `Control.Edit` and its drains through `Control.Drain`, the calls the leader's host makes for the operator's commands, and sets its own balance moves; the run's pool is staged once at set-up, when no disk is down, drained or classed.

The down lever's wait reshapes the fault mix. While the mark waits, the disk stays up and its node runs. The plain run keeps pulling levers then, moves, drains, formats and second failures, each finding the PG as it was before the mark, as an operator's edit or a second failure would while a node is silent but not yet marked: 17,300 of its 17,507 levers over these seeds. It is the only seeded run with edits, drains and formats on the real group. The leaving-member variant pulls no lever while a mark waits. The tables wait for the control plane's steps, so the clients write 192 times each, not 48, or their writes end before a move's interval starts. Over seeds 0 to 39 (plain run / leaving-member variant), counting what lands in PG 0's tables:

| | Stand-in | Real group |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Levers pulled | 284 / 339 | 17,507 / 119 |
| Interval changes | 268 / 280 | 419 / 138 |
| Tables with a new down mark | 39 / 43 | 79 / 31 |
| Primary moved and marked down in one table | 19 / 20 | 6 / 0 |
| Disks formatted again | 18 / 18 | 74 / 13 |
| Leaving members crashed as the table removing them lands | 0 / 13 | 0 / 7 |
| Seeds where a restarted disk drops the gated writes of a PG it left | 3 / 11 | 0 / 7 |

The leaving variant's gate is what lets its crash reach its subject on the real group. Each of its 7 crashes is of a drained disk (3 of them down-levered too), while some disk's down mark waits and each client still has 39 to 94 of its 192 writes left; the gate then holds until the clients end, so no lever follows a crash. Without the gate, levers stack while marks wait, every leaving member's crash lands after the clients end, and none of seeds 0 to 39 has a restarted disk drop the gated writes of a PG it left, the variant's subject. So on the real group the variant crashes a left member only while a down mark is pending; the stand-in's variant covers a crash in a quiet cluster (its 13). Each leaving variant's test fails unless one of its seeds drops a left PG's gated writes.

- On the real group: the primary-change run (`TestPeeringKeepsAcknowledgedWritesAcrossPrimariesOnTheRealGroup`) and its leaving-member variant (`TestALeftMemberDownAtItsMovesEndKeepsAcknowledgedWritesOnTheRealGroup`), 10 seeds each in `go test`, and 120 and 300 in `scripts/seeds.sh`, from seed 0. Each writes a conformance trace, `real-primaries-<seed>` or `real-leftdown-<seed>`. In `scripts/seeds.sh` (4 jobs) the plain run's 120 seeds take 30 s, 1 s a seed, as its levers keep landing while marks wait, and the variant's 300 take 25 s, 0.33 s a seed, about the stand-in's. An edit that moves a primary while it stays up lets the old primary restart holding part of a version its members hold whole, and it has no veto over that version (the keep rule's last row in [Peering and read leases](#peering-and-read-leases), `TestAMemberHoldingAVersionInPartDoesNotVetoIt`). A disk formatted again and refilled can recover a chunk under a version that every member's crash leaves unacknowledged, then lead the next interval, which drops that version: the disk takes no image of the chunk, which would serve zeros over acknowledged bytes (`TestARecoveryDroppedWithItsVersionLeavesTheCopyLacking`).
- The fault, read, write-limit, detector and give-up runs, with their planted bugs, run on the real group alone, under their own sections: a down mark becomes a cut between the disk's node and the control plane's, the run reads each mark from the committed disk record, and the control plane answers the replicas' asks itself. In `scripts/seeds.sh` (4 jobs) their seeds cost what the stand-in's did, but the give-up run's 200, 40 s against 28 s, and the chunk store's list takes 927 s, P20's grant-room run below included, against 904 s. Three stay on the stand-in:
  - The fenced-session run (`TestNoFencedSessionsWriteIsApplied`) fences its first session in a session table of its own, handed to the replicas by hand, and the stand-in detector's `Lags` hook keeps a down disk down while its node's session table lacks the fence. The real leader's lag check compares each node's reported session table with the leader's own, which this run never fences. The leader's side is `internal/meta`'s: `TestNoSessionIsFencedWhileItsClientsLeaseRuns` and its plant of a disk marked up with an older table (`upWithOldTable`).
  - P7 (`TestP7SplitsAPoolWithWritesInFlight`) places PGs by hand, PG 37 on PG 18's members one interval above it and a split table moving PGs 74 and 75 to disk 4, where `Control` places them itself. The real group's splits are `internal/meta`'s (`ctl_test.go`): `TestAPoolChangeIsCheckedAgainstTheCommittedPool`, `TestAReportFromBeforeASplitIsDropped` and `TestAnAskFromBeforeASplitIsDropped`.
  - The fault run's restarted member that never asks (`neg-member-no-ask`) breaks its invariant at 1 seed of 500 on the stand-in, seed 410, and at none of the real group's first 300: it needs a member to restart while its PG stays in its interval until the run ends. That seed's trace is scripted in `TestAMemberThatNeverAsksKeepsItsReplayedWritesGated`.
- The cloned disk (`TestAClonedDiskIsRefused`, 30 in `scripts/seeds.sh`, 5 s): clients write to every PG of four disks on the real group while, at a random time 1 to 5 s in, a node's heartbeats name another node's member disk's log on its second device: in even seeds with the original up, in odd seeds once the original's node, cut off from the control plane, has its disk marked down. The control plane refuses it each time (`ErrLogRefused`), since a disk keeps its device when it moves and the same log on another device can only be a copy ([A disk is its log](design.md#epoch-changes-and-failure-detection)); the run fails unless it does, and it checks "no disk ID names two log IDs, and no log ID is up under two disk IDs" on the committed record after every step. A record that takes the clone as a new disk breaks it at seed 0 (`TestPlantedCloneJoinsBreaksTheDiskIDs`).
- P23 end to end (`TestARefillStoppedAtALogReserveGoesStuck`, scripted, 1 s): a `rep3` PG on three of four disks loses one, declared lost, and refills onto the fourth, whose node reports its size and log reserve to the leader, whose answers to the disks' reports hand them to every replica through the node's own hand-off (`node.TakeMembership`), none handed one by hand, so the primary's recovery check stops the copy one chunk short of the reserve, with some of the PG's 40 chunks still to copy and the log not yet full. The leader raises `Stuck` on the PG from `Control.Capacity` within `stuck_after` of the last copy. A fifth disk joins with no edit: the leader hands placement the `Stuck` PG with its primary's report of the full member short, placement parks the full member beside a member on the new disk, recovery leaves the parked member out of each copy, and `Stuck` clears within `stuck_after` of the join, about 3 s, the new member lacking nothing and the full disk out of the PG after the recovered report. Without the park the PG stays `Stuck` on its three disks; with the park but copies still sent to the parked member, it stays `Stuck` with the new member lacking every chunk. A log filled truly full, with no room to persist a missing list, stalls peering of every interval its member is live in, which no park clears; the recovery check, given the disk's size and reserve, is what keeps that room: with the answers' sizes left untaken, the copy fills the fourth disk's log to its reserve with 29 chunks still lacking. A seeded run would spend most of each seed waiting out `stuck_after` for one path, so the case is scripted.
- P20 with grants out, scripted (`TestARefillLeavesTheRoomOfTheGrantsOut`, 1 s): four disks, each about 60% full of a `rep3` pool's four PGs under a 71% `write_limit`, report their sizes and log reserves to the leader, which grants a daemon's session 760 blocks, the replicas learning the grants outstanding only from the leader's answers to their nodes' reports, against the smallest gap, so that k × the grant passes the slack the check's whole chunk per copy leaves on these sparse chunks: counting the grants once instead of (1 + k) times lands 99 of 114 flushes. With no disk lost the daemon flushes (1 + k) × its grant, k reuses included. With one lost, its PGs' recovery onto the other three passes `write_limit`, as recovery may, until a target would keep less than its log reserve plus (1 + k) × the grants outstanding; the copying stops there, the leader raises `Stuck`, and every one of the (1 + k) × grant's flushes then lands. Copying past the grants and a reserve reported to the leader as 0 each lose flushes (`TestARefillPlantedPastTheGrantsTakesTheirRoom`). Scripted beside it: a plain write refused for space is refused before a degraded chunk would hold it and urge a copy (`TestAPlainWritePastTheLimitUrgesNoCopy`); a member acknowledges a recovery write with its fill summed afresh (`TestARecoveryAckCarriesAFreshFill`), which the primary counts for `fillEvery` over a client acknowledgment's older sum (`TestRecoveryCountsAMemberAtItsFreshRecoveryFill`); a PG stopped for room copies again as soon as a target's fill falls (`TestACopyStoppedForRoomStartsOnceTheTargetsFillFalls`); a copy to a target whose size the primary has not learned, as after a control-plane failover before the target's node reports, waits for the size and starts once it comes (`TestACopyToADiskOfUnknownSizeWaitsForItsSize`); and a fill the leader passes on from a member's heartbeat counts no lower than the member's acknowledgment until both clocks show `fillHeld`, 4 s, since, `CLOCK_BOOTTIME` alone not sufficing, and is taken whole after it (`TestARelayedFillDoesNotUndercutARecentAcknowledgment`).
- P20 with grants out, seeded on the real group, the disks about 68% full (`TestARefillLeavesTheGrantsTheirRoomOnTheRealGroup`, 10 seeds in `go test` and 300 in `scripts/seeds.sh`, 45 s with 4 jobs, from seed 0): the same cluster takes plain writes and granted flushes, loses a random disk, declared lost, and takes more granted flushes while its PGs refill and after the pool goes `Stuck`, (1 + k) × the grant in all, at most 8 at once, since a burst past a node's buffer pool loses messages; a flush refused for a stale table is sent again, as a daemon would. It holds the [write-limit invariant](#placement-faults-and-invariants), each disk's fill counted with its share of the grants, and "no granted flush is refused or held" (unanswered for 2 s). Each log has 200 64-block segments outside its reserve, and each disk reports as its size the live blocks those segments hold less six lanes' open segments: the leader and the replicas count live blocks, while headers, open segments and tails take 6 to 30% of such small logs, so a disk reporting its raw size leaves the check nothing to protect. Reporting the live blocks a log can hold is a [checklist item](build-checklist.md#phase-4-embedded-metastore).

## Operator's disk exits

`meta.Control.Lost` and `meta.Control.Remove` at the leader of a real three-replica group, as in
[Control-plane membership](#control-plane-membership) (`internal/meta`, `exits_test.go`). The
command line that sends them is the "Operator CLI" item's.

- A dead node's two disks, refilled after `refill_after` and kept as leaving members, are declared
  lost through the leader: the leaving members go with no report, no PG names either disk, a
  repeated declaration is accepted, and a later report of their log IDs is refused
  (`TestADeadNodesDisksDeclaredLostEndTheirLeavingMembers`).
- A declaration for an up disk, or one the record does not know, is refused and proposes nothing
  (same test).
- A declaration made after the detector marks a disk down but before the table marking it down
  commits is refused; after that commit it is taken (`TestADeclarationWaitsForTheDownMarkToCommit`).
- A declaration staged on a leader whose commit loses a race to another commit is applied again over
  the state read back, and commits with the next step (`TestADeclarationOutlivesAFailedCommit`).
- The same declaration, its disk up again before the next step, is dropped with an error from that
  step: the disk is not committed gone, nor when it next goes down
  (`TestADeclarationTheStateReadBackRefusesIsDropped`).
- A removal is refused for a disk the record does not know, one never drained that no PG names,
  one not drained that PGs name, and a drained disk while any PG names it, as a member, in a past
  interval, or only as a leaving member, its intervals activated and no recovered report yet; once
  none does, it is removed with no new table, and a later report of its log ID is refused
  (`TestADrainedDiskIsRemovedOnceNoPGNamesIt`).
- The [disk record's seeded run](#control-plane-membership) declares random disks lost, and holds
  that a disk committed gone stays gone.
- A PG whose last activated interval has no member left stays stopped after its disks are declared
  lost (`TestTwoDisksLostTogetherStayStopped`); only an operator's give-up of those intervals frees it
  ([An operator's give-up](design.md#epoch-changes-and-failure-detection),
  [A refill keeps a possible last source](#placement-computation)).

## Blocked and unfound reports

`internal/chunkstore` builds the heartbeat and holds the logic both authorities share (`Watcher`);
`internal/meta` feeds it on the leader. The simulator rows run the replicas' real heartbeats through
a `Watcher` on an authority node of their own.

- A chunk unfound with a member still serving: the primary's heartbeat carries the count, and the
  pool shows `Blocked` with the PG, the count and the candidates, the leaving member too
  (`TestABlockedPGNamesItsDisks`, `min_live` 1). With both its old disks declared lost, the chunk
  keeps the PG from recovering, so it is `Stuck` too, and `Blocked` shows the count and no candidate
  (`TestAChunkOnlyLostDisksHeldStaysUnfound`).
- A PG stopped below `min_live`: once `Stuck`, `Blocked` shows its count as unknown, not 0, and its
  candidates (`TestABlockedPGNamesItsDisks`, `min_live` 2); with no member left to return, no
  candidate (`TestTwoDisksLostTogetherStayStopped`).
- A member back from a short outage with recovery held: its primary reports the 3 writes it missed
  as copies lacking and the PG goes `Stuck`; once recovery copies them the count falls to 0 and
  `Stuck` clears (`TestCopiesLackingFallAndClearStuck`).
- On the leader, its clock well past `stuck_after`: a drained disk's PG is not `Stuck` at once; with
  no active report for its interval it goes `Stuck` and `Blocked`, stopped, after `stuck_after`; its
  primary's report of copies lacking makes it no longer stopped, and a fall in them clears `Stuck`
  (`TestALeavingMemberGoesStuckAndClearsWhenItCopies`). A report of 2 unfound gives `Blocked` with
  2, cleared by a report of none (`TestAReportOfUnfoundChunksBlocksItsPG`).
- A report from the primary of an older interval, heard after the newer one's, is dropped, and an
  active report of an interval the table has moved past counts as no active primary
  (`TestStaleIntervalReports`).
- A member down makes its PG `Stuck` after `stuck_after`; a member in `maintenance` does not, though
  its PG reports copies lacking (`TestMaintenanceIsNotStuckButDownIs`).
- A report for a PG or pool the table does not have, after a split or from a stale table, or heard
  before the first step, is dropped, not a panic; the watcher forgets the PGs a shrunk table no
  longer has (`TestAReportOfUnfoundChunksBlocksItsPG`, `TestStuck`).
- A disk's class is the one it joined the record with, committed in its entry: a restarted node
  opening it under another class moves no PG and changes no capacity figure
  (`TestADiskClassIsSetWhenItJoins`), and a new leader stepping before any disk, or only one, has
  sent a heartbeat keeps every PG of a classed pool where it was (`TestAFailoverKeepsAClassedPoolsPGs`).

## Session fencing on storage nodes

`internal/chunkstore`, against the [Control-plane sessions](#control-plane-sessions)' session table. The
[Sessions and fencing model](#sessions-and-fencing-model)'s scripted scenarios 3, 5 and 9 run as
simulator seeds against the real primaries and replicas.

| Input | Expected |
| --- | --- |
| A storage node receives session-table version v | It applies v and acknowledges it on its next heartbeat; every later heartbeat repeats the version it holds |
| A write from a session v fences arrives after the primary applied v | Rejected |
| A write from that session arrived before the primary applied v and is still queued | Checked again when the primary orders it, and rejected |
| A primary that has not applied v replicates the session's write to a replica that has | The replica rejects it, so the write is never acknowledged |
| A write from a session newer than the node's table | The node fetches the session table before it judges the write, then accepts it |
| A write from a session the table the node fetched after it arrived does not know either | Refused: that session was never handed out. A table sent unasked leaves it waiting |
| More than 64 writes wait for a newer session table | The ones past 64 are refused |
| A member's primary sends a waiting write again | The member keeps only the newest copy, and answers it once its table knows the session |
| A client write or punch that carries no session | Malformed, as one carrying a version is, so it skips neither check |
| A node marked down heartbeats again with a version older than the current one | Not marked up until a heartbeat reports the current version |

The rows are unit tests in `replica_paths_test.go` (`TestAWriteFromASessionNewerThanTheTableWaitsForIt`,
`TestAWriteFromASessionNoFetchedTableKnowsIsRefused`, `TestWritesWaitingForASessionTableAreCapped`,
`TestAMemberKeepsOneCopyOfAResentWriteWaitingForASessionTable`, `TestAFencedSessionsWriteIsRefused`, `TestAMemberRefusesAFencedSessionsReplicatedWrite`,
`TestAWriteOfAnOlderIncarnationIsRefused`, which also sends a client write carrying a version: the
decoder drops it, so no client write skips the incarnation check that a member's replicated write
skips), `wire_test.go` (`TestWireRejectsAClientWriteOrPunchWithoutASession`) and `gate_test.go`
(`TestAWriteOfAFencedSessionOrNoIncarnationIsRefusedWhenOrdered`); the rejoin row is [Control-plane sessions](#control-plane-sessions)'.

**[property]** `TestNoFencedSessionsWriteIsApplied` (500 seeds per commit) is the
[read run](#placement-faults-and-invariants) with its two writers as two sessions, and half its cuts
taking a second disk node with the first, the two still reaching each other, as when a rack is cut
off. The first session is fenced when it dies, but, cut off from the control plane and alive, writes on for up to 2 s; the table reaches
each running node not cut off after its own delay of up to a heartbeat (1 s), so some nodes order
the fenced session's writes before their table holds the fence and others after; the second
session starts once every node with a disk up holds the fence. Checked after every step: no store
orders a write of the fenced session once it holds the fence, and every write of the first session
that completes is ordered, in its chunk, before every write of the second.

**Planted bugs** (`TestPlantedReadBugsBreakTheReadRun`), each checked alone:

| Planted bug | Invariant | Seeds of 500 | First |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `neg-check-on-arrival`: a primary checks the session only as a write arrives (`fenceOnArrival`), so a write that waited in its store as the fence came is ordered | No fenced write applied | 2 | 21 |
| `neg-replica-no-check`: a member takes a replicated write without checking its session (`memberNoFence`), logging one its primary ordered before the fence reached it | No fenced write applied | 123 | 3 |

`neg-up-with-old-table` is planted in the leader, under [Control-plane sessions](#control-plane-sessions).
`neg-peering-skipped` removes the rule that a new interval activates only once its earlier ones
stopped, which the epoch model's `neg-stop-previous-only` and `neg-reach-last-activated-only` also
remove: their plants (`stopPreviousOnly`, `lastActivatedOnly`) fail their traces. In this run they
break the lock order in none of 500 seeds, paired cuts included, and cannot: the model's
counterexample needs two intervals whose live members do not overlap, an old primary completing
the fenced session's writes on the members of its own interval while the new primary, whose peering
never reached them, completes the next holder's. Every PG here has 3 disks with `min_live` 2 and
the run never replaces a member, so an interval completes writes only with 2 of its PG's 3 disks
live, even when a paired cut takes two of them down together, and any two intervals that complete
writes share a live member. That member takes the older interval's writes only until it adopts the
newer one, without being peered, and the newer one's only after, so every write of the older
interval that completes is ordered before every write of the newer one. Disjoint live sets need members
replaced, as in the traces' two-member PGs. Neither of the two planted bugs above breaks the lock order in
500 seeds either, since the second session starts only once every node with a disk up holds the
fence.

## Filesystem schema

Transaction shapes, from the design's [transaction table](design.md#metadata-layer-metastore). Each is a single-shard `Txn` with one shard, asserted on the keys and ops it touches. "The parent's times" is `Update(parent a.mtime, Bump, t)` and `Update(parent a.ctime, Bump, t)`.

The tests are in `internal/meta/fs_test.go`, each building its operations with `meta.FS` and applying them to a real `State`: `TestReservations` (the reservation, root and slot rows), `TestShardWithoutFreeKeyHandsOutNoSlot`, `TestCreateMkdirLinkSymlink`, `TestUnlink`, `TestRename`, `TestRenameAcrossDirectories`, `TestNothingLandsOnARemovedInode`, `TestRenameOntoItselfChangesNothing`, `TestSymlinksLeaveTheByteCounter`, `TestAttributes` (truncate, `alloc_end`, `close`, `mtime` and the byte counter), `TestMtimeNeverGoesBackwards`, `TestLocks`, `TestXattrsAndCaseIndex`, `TestCaseFoldingMatchesEqualFold`, `TestCaseFoldIsPinned` and `TestReplayedMkdir`; `TestResentFSOpsReturnTheirFirstFinalResult` and `TestResentFSOpsAreSent` resend random operations. `FuzzDecodeFSValues` feeds any bytes to the attribute, entry, parent and purge decoders; `TestFSBuildsAllocateNothing` and `BenchmarkBuildCreate` hold every build to zero allocations.

| Operation | Ops in one `Txn` | Expected, including errors |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Inode reservation, first create of a node in slot 2 | Its own `Txn`: `Update(fs/5/2:0/n, Add, 64)` | `Updated` gives the batch's end; the daemon hands out the 64 numbers from memory and reserves the next batch in the background when 6 are left. A repeat after an election only skips numbers |
| Slot reservation | Its own `Txn`: `Update` of the shard's `f` key, `Add`, 16, once a read of `f` before the daemon's first reservation on the shard found it | 16 slots for the daemon's `mkdir`s, the next batch reserved when 2 are left |
| Slot reservation on a shard from slot 100 whose `f` no split wrote, by one daemon after another | The read of `f` finds it absent; no `Txn` | Nothing handed out and `f` stays absent; the shard counts as used up, so `mkdir` shares its parent's slot |
| The root of volume 5 | `Check(fs/5/0:0/n absent, final)`, `Put(fs/5/1/a)`, `n` = 2 and `f` = 1 at slot 0 | Created once; a second try fails. Seq 0 and slot 0 are never handed out |
| `create` of `beach.jpg` in /photos (slot 2), inode 2:k from the reservation | `Check(fs/5/2:1/d/beach.jpg absent, final)`; `Check(fs/5/2:1/P = /)`; put the entry → 2:k, type file; put `fs/5/2:k/a`; the parent's times | A second `create` of the name fails with `EEXIST` |
| Two racing `create`s in slot 2 from two nodes, different names | Each with an inode from its own reservation | Both commit in one round, with distinct inodes; neither retries |
| `mkdir` with a free slot from the daemon's reservation | As `create`, plus `Update(parent a.nlink, Add, 1)`; `Put(fs/5/s:1/a)`, `Put(fs/5/s:1/P → 2:1)`, `Check(fs/5/s:0/n absent)`, `Put(fs/5/s:0/n = 66)` | Single shard. The directory is s:1, and the creating daemon owns s:2 … s:65 |
| `mkdir` in a slot whose `n` exists, a slot handed out twice | The `Check(n absent)` fails, not final | The daemon takes another slot; the first directory's `n` stays |
| `mkdir`, then `create` in it from the same daemon | The create takes s:2 | No reservation round between them |
| `mkdir` with no free slot left | The new directory shares its parent's slot, and still gets `P` | Single shard |
| `n` = 2^40 − 1 in slot 2 | The next two `create`s | The first takes 2:(2^40 − 1), the last ID. The second goes to a fresh slot |
| `link` of 2:3 as `b` in /photos | `Check(d/b absent, final)`, `Put(d/b → 2:3)`, `Check(2:3 a)` and `Put(2:3 a)` with `nlink` + 1 and `ctime`, the parent's times | A second `link` to the name fails with `EEXIST` |
| `symlink` with a 4,095-byte target | As `create`, plus the target under `t` in 5 values | `readlink` returns the 4,095 bytes (`pjdfstest` `symlink/03.t`) |
| `unlink` of a file's last link, no open handles | `Check(d/name = inode, final)`; delete the entry; `Check(a = what was read)`; `DeleteRange` over the inode's keys; merge `fs/5/2:0/p/{inode}` with `0 .. alloc_end`; `Update(u, Add, −size)`; the parent's times | One transaction; no attribute, xattr, lock or target key of the inode remains |
| A `link` racing a last `unlink` | The `link` commits first | The unlink's `Check(a)` fails, not final; the daemon reads again and drops one link, so no entry names a removed inode |
| `unlink` of a file with a second link | Delete only the entry; `nlink` − 1 by `Check(a)` and `Put(a)` | No purge entry |
| `unlink` of a file still open | Delete the entry; put `fs/5/2:0/o/{inode}`; `nlink` − 1 | At last close, and after any grace period, the orphan moves to `p/` |
| `rmdir` of an empty directory | `Check(d/name = inode, final)`, `CheckEmpty(child's d/, final)`, delete the entry, `DeleteRange` over its keys, `Update(parent a.nlink, Add, −1)`, the parent's times | Committed |
| `rmdir` of a directory with one entry | Same | `ENOTEMPTY`, stored as the request's final result |
| `rename` within one directory | `Check(src, final)`, `Check(dst absent)`, delete src, put dst, the parent's times | `rename` moves the entry exactly once |
| Rename over a non-empty directory | As above, with `CheckEmpty(dst's d/, final)` | `ENOTEMPTY`; nothing changes |
| Rename-over of a file someone has open | Move the entry; the replaced inode goes to `o/` | As for unlink of an open file |
| Rename-over of a file no one has open | Move the entry; `Check` the replaced inode's attributes as read and remove its keys; merge its purge entry `0 .. alloc_end` | One transaction |
| Cross-directory rename of directory /a/b into /c, with /c's ancestors /c and / | Both parents' times; `Update(nlink, Add, −1)` on /a and `+1` on /c; `Put(b's P → /c)`; `Check(P = what was read)` on /c | Committed; a create in /c meanwhile does not fail it, since `P` is its own key |
| Cross-directory rename of /a into /a/b/c | The loop check reads c's ancestors up to /a | Refused with `EINVAL`: a directory never moves under itself |
| The same, while another node moves /a/b elsewhere | The moved directory's `Check(P)` fails | The rename retries from a fresh read; no loop forms |
| A `create`, `symlink`, `mkdir` (in a fresh slot or not), `link`, file renamed in, `chmod` or xattr set on /d, each built before an `rmdir` of /d that commits first | Its `Check(/d P = /)` fails, not final | The daemon reads again and answers `ENOENT`; no key of /d, and no fresh slot's `n`, comes back |
| xattr set or removed on a file whose last `unlink` commits first | Its `Check(a)` fails, not final | `ENOENT` on the retry; no `x/` key is left |
| `rename` of `x` onto itself, or onto `y`, a second link of the same inode | `Check(src, final)` and `Check(dst = what was read)` only | Succeeds and changes nothing (POSIX) |
| `case_index` on, `rename` of `readme.txt` to `README.txt` | `Check(c/README.TXT = readme.txt, final)` in place of the absent-check | Committed; `c/README.TXT` now holds `README.txt` |
| A symlink with a 5-byte target, created, then unlinked | Neither touches `u` | The slot's byte counter stays 0: it counts regular files only |
| `chmod` of a directory while 64 creates land in it | `Update(mode, Set, v)`, `Update(a.ctime, Bump, now)` | Commits in the same round as the creates; no `Check` on the directory's attributes |
| Truncate from 10,000 bytes to 5,000 | `Check(a)`, size 5,000, `alloc_end` 1, `Update(u, Add, −5,000)`, and a purge range from byte 5,000 to the old `alloc_end` merged into `p/` | The range starts at the byte offset, not at a chunk boundary |
| Truncate, then unlink before the purger runs | A 16 MiB file (`alloc_end` 4) truncated to 5,000, then unlinked | `p/{inode}` holds the union, `0 .. 4`, not the unlink's `0 .. 1` alone: no chunk leaks |
| Two truncates before the purger runs | 16 MiB to 8 MiB, then to 5,000 | `p/{inode}` holds the union of both ranges |
| `alloc_end` raise | `Check(a)`, `alloc_end` raised, plus the size written so far | One `Txn` |
| `close` whose `Check(a)` loses a race with another node's size change | The check fails, not final | The daemon reads again and retries under the same request ID, and commits |
| `close` or `fsync`, writer's clock behind | Stored `mtime` 1,000.000000005 s; the writer's wall clock reads 999.9 s | Stored `mtime` becomes 1,000.000000006 s |
| `close` or `fsync`, writer's clock ahead | Stored `mtime` 1,000 s; the writer's last write at 1,001 s | Stored `mtime` becomes 1,001 s |
| `close` of a write-shared file, writer's clock behind | Stored `mtime` 1,000 s; the node last reported 1,000.000000040 s; its last write at 999.9 s | Stored `mtime` becomes 1,000.000000040 s |
| `utimensat(500 s)` | Same stored `mtime` | Stored `mtime` becomes 500 s |
| flock `LOCK_EX` | Scan `fs/5/2:3/l/`; `CheckEmpty` over each gap between the keys found; put `fs/5/2:3/l/x/{s}` | Granted when no live session holds a key |
| flock `LOCK_EX` while a session gone from the session table holds `l/x/{t}` | `Check(l/x/{t} = v)`, `Delete` it, the gap checks, `Put(l/x/{s})` | Granted in one `Txn`, the dead holder's key gone |
| flock `LOCK_SH` from two sessions, then `LOCK_EX` from a third | `l/s/{s1}`, `l/s/{s2}`; each shared lock checks `l/x/` only | Both shared locks granted; the exclusive one refused |
| A lock key added inside a gap after the scan | The `CheckEmpty` over that gap fails | The request reads again; at most one exclusive holder |
| Size change, slot byte counter | Size from 0 to 3 bytes | `Update(fs/5/2:0/u, Add, 3)` in the same transaction, never compare-and-set, and `statfs` used is the sum of the slot counters |
| xattr `user.DOSATTRIB` on 2:3 | Put `fs/5/2:3/x/user.DOSATTRIB` | One scan returns it with the attributes |
| xattr of 64 KiB on 2:3 | The first piece and count under `x/{name}`, 65 pieces under the piece tag, `Check(a)` | One `Txn` of about 82 KiB; `getxattr` returns the 64 KiB |
| xattr set over a longer value | The new value's pieces, and `Delete` of the old pieces past the new count | No piece of the old value is left |
| flock `LOCK_SH` by a session holding `l/x/{s}`, and `LOCK_EX` by one holding `l/s/{s}` | `Check` and `Delete` its own key, `Put` the other mode's | One `Txn` converts the lock |
| `case_index` on, `create` of `Photo.JPG` | Also `Check(fs/5/2:1/c/PHOTO.JPG absent, final)` and put it → `Photo.JPG` | One extra key per create; a `create` of `PHOTO.jpg` fails with `EEXIST`; `unlink` deletes the `c/` key |
| `case_index` on, the Kelvin sign `\u212Aelvin`, long s `\u017Fun`, final sigma `οΣ` | Then `kelvin`, `SUN`, `ος` | Each second name fails with `EEXIST`, as `strings.EqualFold` matches them; `ß` and `ss` are two names |

**Replay records**

| Input | Expected |
| --- | --- |
| `mkdir` with (session 7, mount 1, request 42) applied, then resent with the same IDs | The second returns the stored result (success), not `EEXIST`, and changes nothing |
| A `mkdir` that failed with `EEXIST`, resent | Returns `EEXIST`: a final failure is stored |
| A `rename` that failed with `ENOENT`, resent after the source appears | Returns `ENOENT`, and nothing moves |
| An `unlink` that committed, resent when a new lookup no longer finds the name | The daemon sends the `Txn` it built first, and its record returns success, not `ENOENT` |
| A resent `Txn` with an `Update` | Returns its first `Result`, including the `Update`'s value |
| Two mounts of volume 5 by session 7, each sending request 42 | Two records, `r/7/1/42` and `r/7/2/42`; neither answers the other |
| A request carrying "oldest outstanding" 50 | The shard removes that session and mount's records below 50 in that slot, with one range removal |
| Session 7 leaves the session table | Each shard's leader removes `r/7/` in every slot, in the background |
| A resend after its record was dropped | It runs again and returns whatever the state now gives. An honest oldest-outstanding value rules it out |
| [property] Every mutating op, resent 0 to 3 times at random (`TestResentFSOpsReturnTheirFirstFinalResult`) | Each resend returns its request's first final result and changes nothing, and a request whose result was not final leaves no record |

Replay records are kept as `fs/{volume}/{slot · 0}/r/{session}/{mount}/{request}`, in the slot the request changed.

**Invariants** need a running filesystem workload, so they are checked under [MetaStore invariants](#metastore-invariants).

## MetaStore invariants

Simulator invariants checked after every step, with the faults that must exercise each.

| Invariant | Faults that exercise it |
| --- | --- |
| At most one leader per shard per term | Registered by [Leader leases](#leader-leases) (`TestRaftRunsReplayFromTheirSeed`) and [Voter replacement](#voter-replacement): partitions; leader crashes; a node restarted within `primary_lease` |
| No two replicas of a shard serve lease reads at overlapping times | Registered by [Leader leases](#leader-leases) (`TestRaftRunsReplayFromTheirSeed`) and [Voter replacement](#voter-replacement): a leader's node cut off past its followers' grants; a leader's node suspended past its lease; a leader transfer while lease reads arrive; a configuration change while a lease is held; slewed clocks; VM pauses |
| A committed entry is never lost | Registered by [Raft storage in the disk log](#raft-storage-in-the-disk-log) (`TestCommittedEntriesSurviveCrashesOnTheDiskLog`): crashes before and after a round's flush; a torn tail record holding chunk writes and Raft entries |
| A replica keeps its term and vote across a crash | Registered by [Raft storage in the disk log](#raft-storage-in-the-disk-log): crashes with rounds in flight, landing unflushed writes at random |
| A shard recovered from manifest and log equals its state before the crash | Registered for the control-plane group by [Control-plane host](#control-plane-host) (`TestAHostCompactsAndRestartsFromItsManifest`, `TestAHostRestartsFromRunsOfManyPieces`, `TestAHostMergesItsTreeInStepsAcrossCrashes`, planted `TestARestoreThatReappliesEntriesBreaksTheStateCheck`): crashes mid-round, with a checkpoint's piece in flight and with its manifest in flight, with merges whole and in steps, compactions, deletes and freed segments. Registered for shards on a disk's chunk store by [Shard indexes in the disk owner's checkpoint](#shard-indexes-in-the-disk-owners-checkpoint) (`TestRaftShardsOnTheStoreCheckpointCompactAndRecover`): crashes landing unflushed writes at random, counted with no checkpoint running, with a piece in flight and with the manifest in flight, while the shards compact and the cleaner frees their segments, each restart's state checked against its applied index and its commit against the last acknowledged; and for shards on the round driver, on the device loop and on another (`TestShardsOnTheRoundDriverCheckpointCompactAndRecover`): crashes landing unflushed writes at random, counted per shard with no flush of it running, with a piece of it in flight and with every piece durable and the manifest not yet mailed durable, while the shards merge, compact and rewrite runs the cleaner marks and the cleaner frees the segments of their dead blobs and run pieces, each shard's state when its replay ends checked against its state before the crash; and for `meta.RoundShard` replicas on a device loop, single voters and the learner of a group whose voter runs on another loop (`TestMetaReplicasOnADeviceCheckpointCompactAndRecover`): crashes landing unflushed writes at random, counted per replica with no flush of it running, with a piece of it in flight and with every piece durable and the manifest not yet durable, and within 100 steps of the learner holding a snapshot it was sent, while the replicas take `Txn`s beside chunk writes, compact and merge, the learner, cut off and reconnected, restores its voter's snapshots as runs, replicas are removed and new ones added under removed ones' owner keys, and the cleaner frees the segments of their dead pieces, each count over the run's own seeds at least about a quarter of what they reach, adds under a removed replica's owner key counted on their own. Every replica that started and was not removed comes back, each restarted replica holds its group's state at its applied index, the voter and the learner a term at least the highest they sent, the learner every index it acknowledged, no replica the device answered Gone comes back, and once they lead each voter has applied every `Txn` it answered. Restoring only some of the replicas a manifest names, answering Gone once the store took a removal but before the manifest a restart loads leaves it out, leaving out the learner's ask that a segment header name the manifest of its snapshot's runs, or marking that flush with the storage's base rather than the snapshot's, it failed. The replay LSN a replica holds after a snapshot round (`TestRoundsKeepTheVoteASnapshotRoundTheRunsDoNotHoldWouldDrop`) is out of its reach: the learner asks for a due checkpoint in the pass it takes the round, so every manifest begun during the hold flushes it onto runs holding the snapshot, and only a failed flush, which stops the store, would pair older runs with the LSN |
| At most one lock holder | Registered by [Control-plane sessions](#control-plane-sessions) (`TestNoSessionIsFencedWhileItsClientsLeaseRuns`): clients racing for one inode's lock in shared and exclusive modes, holders evicted, fenced and dead, and control-plane failovers. Owner failover is not in it: the owner's shard does not fail over |
| No session is fenced while its client's own lease still runs | Registered by [Control-plane sessions](#control-plane-sessions) (`TestNoSessionIsFencedWhileItsClientsLeaseRuns`, `TestAFastNewLeaderFencesNoSessionEarly`, `TestAFastBootClockFencesNoSessionEarly`): control-plane leader failover while sessions renew; a renewal answered by a deposed leader; a leader stalled past `session_lease`; clients paused past their lease; slewed clocks; a client VM stopped with its clocks frozen |
